title: Email protection: document addresses it cannot hide, and add a check that finds them (schema, other plugins' script data)
body:
## What

Email protection (#927, #959) encodes addresses in content, blocks, widgets and menus. It cannot hide, by design:

- **Schema (JSON-LD)**: SEO plugins print the organisation's email on every page (Rank Math: Titles & Meta → Local SEO → Email, stored as `email` in the `rank-math-options-titles` option). Search engines read JSON-LD as plain data, so it must not be encoded; the field is optional and can be cleared.
- **Other plugins' script data**: for example a chatbot's notice text (AI Engine: `textCompliance` in the `mwai_chatbots` option) printed into the page for its own script. Encoding it could break that plugin; change the text at its source.
- **Theme templates and hard-coded HTML** outside the filters the feature hooks.

After the 1.3.85 rollout, one of the owner's sites still showed its address on every page, from exactly the first two. Site owners have no way to know this; the owner removed both at the source once told.

## How

1. **README.md → Email protection**: add "Addresses it cannot hide" with the three cases above and what to do for each (clear the optional schema email in the SEO plugin; change the other plugin's text; edit the template). Keep plugin names to examples. Mirror one line in the setting's `description` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-email-protection.php` → `settings()`.
2. **A check on the Security tab**, on the Email protection setting's panel (`seoprostack_setting_panel`, as `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hardening.php` → `panel()` does), run on request, never on every admin load:
   - Fetch the home page (and optionally one URL the admin enters on the same host) with `wp_safe_remote_get`, as `includes/features/class-seoprostack-https-check.php` fetches `home_url('/')` (timeout, no remote hosts).
   - Report each readable address once, with its context: `schema` (inside `<script type="application/ld+json">`), `script data` (other `<script>` or an attribute holding JSON), `attribute`, `text` (a template outside the filters). Placeholders (`data-sps-e`, `data-sps-mailto`, `data-sps-attrs`) are already protected; don't report them.
   - For known sources, add a hint: Rank Math's Local SEO email when `rank-math-options-titles['email']` is that address; Yoast's equivalent if one exists (check its option before naming it); otherwise "Search your plugins' settings for this address".
   - Never change another plugin's settings (AGENTS.md: other plugins' settings only through presets, on request).
3. **WP-CLI**: `wp seoprostack email-protection check [<url>]` printing the same rows (address, context, hint), exit 0; register as `includes/features/class-seoprostack-added-keys.php` does (`WP_CLI::add_command`).
4. Changelog (`changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, README Changelog) per STANDARDS.md; no version bump unless releasing.

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-email-protection.php`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`
- `readme.txt`

## Acceptance

1. On a test site (`scripts/test-site.sh up`) with a page containing an address in JSON-LD, in an inline script's JSON and in plain post content: the check lists the first two with contexts `schema` and `script data`, and does not list the post content address (it is protected).
2. With Rank Math active and its Local SEO email set, the hint names that field.
3. `wp seoprostack email-protection check` prints the same rows.
4. The check makes no request on ordinary admin page loads.
5. `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline` and `scripts/plugin-check.sh` report no errors.

## What

Fluent Boards starter data gets a **Website Setup** board whose tasks are the accounts and keys a site needs, in the order to do them, each with plain step-by-step instructions and links: aidevops, SSH access for aidevops, hosting (Hostinger, referral link), Cloudflare, Cloudflare R2, Purelymail, Amazon SES, Google Cloud, payment processing (Stripe, PayPal, Paddle, Polar), GPL Vault.

Starters can't add tasks today (`fluentboards_boards` has stages and labels only), so:

- New starter item type `fluentboards_tasks`: `board` (title), `title`, `description` (Markdown, as Fluent Boards 2.1+ stores it), optional `after` (the task it follows). Matched by title on the board, so a board that already has a task of that name keeps it. Added through `TaskService::createTask()` in the board's first stage, then placed with `Task::moveBetweenTasks()` after the task named in `after` (or the item before it in the starter), at the top when neither is on the board. Other plugins add tasks to the same board with the `seoprostack_starters` filter (SEO Pro Directory will).
- Remove deletes only tasks SEO Pro Stack added that are unchanged (title and description), open, without comments, attachments or subtasks.

README: a **Website Setup board** section under Starter data: what to click (Plugins → Fluent Boards → Add starter data), what an AI assistant runs over SSH (`wp seoprostack starters add fluent-boards`), connecting an AI client with Fluent Boards' own MCP settings, and why to set up SSH access for aidevops first.

## Files

- `includes/class-seoprostack-starters.php`: `fluentboards_tasks` type (TYPES, type_ready, label, exists, find, create, delete) and the format doc block.
- `starters/fluent-boards.json`: the Website Setup board and its tasks; `tested` 2.2.2.
- `README.md` (Starter data table, new section), `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `docs/presets.md`.
- `.wporg-links`: the Hostinger referral link is already listed (WordPress.org build replaces it in JSON too).

title: Fluent Forms by key: Form by key and Form modal blocks, keyed submissions, policy links in new tabs
body:
## What

Place a Fluent form by a portable key instead of its ID, in a panel or in a Kadence Blocks Pro modal, with blocks whose settings are in the block sidebar.

Form IDs differ on every site a page reaches: a template site, a copied subsite, an imported form. A page that names `[fluentform id="3"]` shows the wrong form, or none, after it is copied. Sites built from one template need the page to name the form by what it is (`contact`, `quote-request`), and each site resolves that to its own form.

This generalises code that one project carried in must-use plugins, so every site on the base stack (Kadence, Kadence Blocks Pro, Fluent Forms) gets it through plugin releases, including sites without hosting access.

## Scope

New feature `SEOProStack_Form_Keys` (Content tab, on by default; nothing changes without Fluent Forms):

- Form meta `seoprostack_form_key` holds the key. `wp seoprostack form-keys list|set|unset`, and `set --copy-from=<meta-key>` to adopt keys stored under another meta key. Starter data `fluentform_forms` items take an optional `key`.
- `seoprostack/form` block (Form by key): choose from the site's keyed forms; panel on/off; server-side preview in the editor. Shortcode `[seoprostack_form key="…" panel="1"]`.
- `seoprostack/form-modal` block (Form modal): key, modal ID, title, introduction; printed in the footer in Kadence Blocks Pro's modal markup, opened by any link to `#ID` (Kadence triggers or Modal links). Falls back to an in-place panel with the same ID without Kadence Blocks Pro. Shortcode `[seoprostack_form_modal …]`.
- Modal fixes (`assets/form-keys.js`): a press that starts in the panel and ends on the overlay does not close; an opened Choices.js list scrolls into view; Tab wraps on visible fields of multi-step forms.
- Base style (`assets/form-keys.css`) that any theme rule naming the classes overrides.
- `seoprostack_form_submitted` action (key, data, form, entry ID) on every keyed form submission, for CRM hand-offs in other plugins.
- Setting **Policy links in forms open a new tab** (on by default): privacy, cookie and terms links in Fluent form fields get `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener"`, class `seoprostack-new-tab` and screen-reader text. Paths filterable with `seoprostack_form_policy_paths`.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-form-keys.php` (new; pattern: `class-seoprostack-modal-links.php`, `class-seoprostack-fluentforms-colours.php`)
- `blocks/form/block.json`, `blocks/form-modal/block.json`, `blocks/form/index.js` (pattern: `blocks/related-posts/`)
- `assets/form-keys.js`, `assets/form-keys.css`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php` (FEATURES list), `includes/class-seoprostack-starters.php` (`key` on forms)
- README.md, readme.txt, changelog.txt

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php js phpcs phpstan`
- On a network site with Fluent Forms and Kadence Blocks Pro: `wp seoprostack form-keys set --copy-from=<old-meta-key>`, then a page with each block renders the form; links to `#ID` open the modal; submission fires `seoprostack_form_submitted`; editor preview matches the front end.

## What

A per-picture **Never watermark** box in Watermark pictures (Media): a ticked picture is skipped by upload marking, the row, bulk and whole-library actions and `wp seoprostack watermark-images`, and a picture already marked keeps its mark until **Remove watermark**. Stored as post meta `_seoprostack_watermark_skip` = `'1'` (`SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::SKIP_META`), so code that adds a site's own photographs can set it on `add_attachment`.

## Why

Sites keep their own page photographs (home page, information pages) free of the corner mark. title: Kadence query loops and theme mods: stop booting the REST API and decoding theme mods on every page
body:
## What

Two Kadence costs paid on every front-end page, fixed in **Fixes for other plugins** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`) through WordPress's and Kadence's own hooks:

1. **Kadence Blocks Pro query loop boots the whole REST API.** Its query children block (`Kadence_Blocks_Pro_Query_Children_Block::do_query()`, checked with Kadence Blocks Pro 2.8.20.1) runs `rest_do_request()` for `GET /wp/v2/kadence_query/query` while the page renders. The first `rest_get_server()` fires `rest_api_init` for every plugin, registering hundreds of routes the page never uses. Measured on a network site with WooCommerce, MCP Adapter, Fluent apps and Ultimate Multisite: the query block took 690-750 ms, of which `rest_api_init` was about 450 ms (MCP Adapter 172 ms, WooCommerce 116 ms, core routes 49 ms).
2. **Kadence theme decodes its theme mods about 1,400 times per page.** `Kadence\Styles\Component::action_enqueue_styles` calls `get_theme_mod()` 1,376 times; each call runs `get_option('theme_mods_{stylesheet}')`, which unserializes the whole option (37 KB, 253 keys) again. Measured: 249 ms for 1,376 calls, 187 ms of it in `unserialize`.

## How

1. While a Kadence query child block renders and no REST server exists yet (not a REST request; nothing booted one), set `$wp_rest_server` to a `WP_REST_Server` subclass holding only that route, with Kadence's own callback (`query`), `permission_callback` (`__return_true`) and args (`get_query_params()`), from `get_post_type_object('kadence_query')->get_rest_controller()`. Kadence's own `rest_do_request()` then dispatches there at its usual moment, with the usual `rest_pre_dispatch`/`rest_request_*` filters. The global is cleared as dispatch starts, and after the block, so any other REST use (in the callback or later in the page) boots the full server as before. Any other route or method goes to the full server.
2. `pre_option_theme_mods_{stylesheet}` (Kadence theme only): keep the decoded value per site, keyed by the stored serialized string in `wp_load_alloptions()`, and return it through the option's own `option_{name}` filters. A changed stored value (update, Customizer save, another site) decodes again; a non-autoloaded or missing option is left to WordPress.

## Not fixable here

Kadence Blocks 3.8.0's design tokens read `wp_kb_design_tokens` 268 times per page (`Token_Store::get_document()`/`get_version()`, no per-request cache; `Effective_Presets::section()`/`dormant()`, `Effective_Version::for_slug()`). `Token_Store` is `final` and the StellarWP DB layer has no short-circuit filter, so this needs a fix in Kadence Blocks.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` (php, phpcs, phpstan) passes.
- Web-SAPI profile of a page with a Kadence query loop, before and after: `rest_api_init` no longer fires, the query block's time drops, and the rendered HTML is identical apart from LiteSpeed's timestamp comment and dynamic form IDs (directory archive, page 2, a taxonomy archive, home page).
- `kadence_query` REST requests from the editor and front-end AJAX filters are unchanged (they are REST requests, so the full server is used).
- Customizer save then page load shows the new theme mod value.

title: t16: Media storage: count uploads in progress as waiting, not failed
body:
## Task


`wp seoprostack media-storage status`, and each picture's media-library label, report a picture as **failed** while its upload is still running. Pictures in progress should count as waiting (or as "uploading"). Only a finished attempt that actually failed, or one whose run died, should count as failed.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`wp seoprostack media-storage status`, and each picture's media-library label, report a picture as **failed** while its upload is still running. Pictures in progress should count as waiting (or as "uploading"). Only a finished attempt that actually failed, or one whose run died, should count as failed.

## Why

On a production multisite, during a business import that kept adding pictures, status showed `failed: 1`, then `failed: 2`, then `failed: 0` within minutes. Two pictures were involved, both new Street View images from the import. Each showed the `failed` state with no error message, and each became `uploaded` within minutes without help. One was served from the bucket (200, WebP) throughout. An operator spent time investigating a failure that wasn't one, and the media library label ("Upload failed; local files are served.") was wrong for that time.

## Evidence in the code (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`, 1.3.98)

- `upload()`, about lines 3853–3870: "Tried first: even a fatal error moves the queue forward and retries later." It sets `DONE` to `upload_marker()`, adds a retry job (`next` one hour ahead), then sets `META` state and `STATE` to `failed`, all before any network I/O.
- The successful end, about lines 1123–1130, sets `STATE` to `uploaded`.
- `counts()`, about line 4615: a picture whose `DONE` equals `upload_marker()` is counted by its `STATE`. During an attempt that is `failed`.
- The labels, about line 4791, map `failed` to "Upload failed; local files are served."

The "tried first" ordering is deliberate: a fatal error part-way through must still move the queue on and leave a retry. Keep that safety.

## How (suggested; verify the premise first)

1. Reproduce: start an upload of a large picture (or add a pause in a test copy), and run `status` from a second shell while it runs. Expected now: `failed` is counted.
2. Mark the attempt as in progress instead of failed. For example, use a `STATE` of `uploading`, counted and labelled as waiting ("Uploading"). Set it to `failed` only when the attempt ends in failure (the existing failure paths) or when its retry job is overdue (the run died). `retry_stranded()` and `--retry-failed` must still find pictures whose run died.
3. Check every reader of `STATE` and every `failed` comparison: lines 730, 2100, 3988, 4016, 4937, the media-library column and REST/health output. Make sure an in-progress picture is never treated as a failure, and never as uploaded (no serving from the bucket before every file is confirmed).

## Acceptance

- During an upload, `status` and the media-library label show the picture as waiting or uploading, not failed.
- A forced failure, for example a wrong secret key in a test bucket, still ends as `failed` with its error message, and `--retry-failed` still requeues it.

FluentCRM 3.2 draws the designer in an iframe of its own page (`post-new.php?fluent_crm_block_editor=1`, `FluentCrm\App\Hooks\Handlers\FluentBlockEditorHandler::renderPage()`). That page exits at `admin_init` (-1000), so `admin_enqueue_scripts` and `admin_head` never run there: neither the mode's `<head>` script nor `admin/css/seoprostack-whole-theme.css` reaches it. Its own stylesheet (`assets/guten-editor/index.css`) paints fixed light colours through `--fc-*` tokens on `:root`, `--fcrm-sidebar-*` on the sidebar panel and `--fcrm-compose-btn-*` on the header.

- `admin/js/seoprostack-whole-theme.js`: the parent screen keeps the designer's frame in step when the mode changes (as it already does for TinyMCE and `wp_die()` frames), loading the stylesheet there on the first switch to Dark.
- `admin/css/seoprostack-whole-theme.css`: a FluentCRM email designer section mapping FluentCRM's tokens to the `--sps-ui-*` palette and fixing its own light parts. The email itself (the canvas, its own frame) keeps the colours it is sent with, as the post editor's canvas keeps the theme's.

title: Plugin fixes: keep Fluent Boards Pro's per-request licence timestamp (__fbs_plugin_license_lc)
body:
## What

Fluent Boards Pro 2.2.2 as patched by GPL Vault runs `update_option('__fbs_plugin_license_lc', time())` in its main file on every load, so every request where the plugin is active writes the options table (and, with an object cache, rewrites the cached autoloaded options when the option autoloads). Nothing in Fluent Boards or Fluent Boards Pro reads that option: only the patch writes it. The licence state itself is in `__fbs_plugin_license` (`status` `valid`, `expires` a date string such as `2099-12-31 23:59:59`), which the patch saves with an identical value, so that write is already a no-op.

`SEOProStack_Option_Writes::KNOWN` already keeps the stored value of licence options that GPL Vault's patches save again with only a new timestamp, but its rules handle only array or object options whose licence state is in the same option, with a numeric expiry.

## How

In `includes/class-seoprostack-option-writes.php`:

- Allow a rule whose whole option is the timestamp (`time` `''`): keep the stored value when both stored and new values are numeric and the licence is valid.
- Allow the licence state to come from another option (`from`), here `__fbs_plugin_license`.
- Accept a date string in the `until` field (via `strtotime()`), still requiring it to be at least a week away.
- Add `__fbs_plugin_license_lc` to `KNOWN`.

Keeping works as today: "Ask before licence checks" on, started early by the must-use file of "Load plugins only where needed" (Fluent Boards Pro's folder sorts before SEO Pro Stack's).

Docs: Unreleased changelog entry (`changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md`). No version change in this PR; release on the owner's say.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` clean for the changed file.
- On a site with Fluent Boards Pro (patched) active and "Ask before licence checks" on: `__fbs_plugin_license_lc` stays unchanged across page loads (before: a new value on every load). With the licence option missing or not valid, the timestamp is saved as before.

title: Plugin fixes: Kadence Blocks design token reads once per request, not 1,900 times
body:
## What

Kadence Blocks 3.8.0 reads its design token library from the database every time a block asks for a preset or palette value, with no memo. One home page with Kadence query cards and Advanced Text blocks ran about 1,900 identical queries:

```sql
SELECT * FROM {prefix}kb_design_tokens WHERE slug = 'default'   -- 1,338 of them for the content alone
SELECT * FROM {prefix}kb_design_tokens WHERE slug = ''          -- 214
```

about 280 ms of a 1.6 s uncached render. The tables checked were all empty, so every read finds nothing.

`Token_Store` (`includes/resources/Design_Tokens/Database/Token_Store.php`) is `final`; `get_document()`, `get_version()` and `get_title()` each run `$this->qb()->where('slug', $slug)->get(ARRAY_A)`. The StellarWP DB query builder calls the global `$wpdb->get_row()` directly (`DB::__callStatic`), and its `stellarwp_db_pre_query` action cannot short-circuit, so the only seam is core's `query` filter.

## Fix (Fixes for other plugins)

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`, next to the Kadence theme_mods memo (GH#1020):

- `query` filter at `PHP_INT_MAX`, registered only with Kadence Blocks 3.8.0+ and when `$wpdb` is core's own `wpdb` class (not a `db.php` drop-in).
- A read matching `SELECT * FROM {prefix}kb_design_tokens WHERE slug = '…'` made through `wpdb::get_row()` (`$wpdb->func_call` names this exact SQL) is run the first time; its rows are collected as the next query starts, while still in `$wpdb`.
- Later identical reads get `$wpdb` set as running them would (flush, cloned rows, `last_query`, `num_rows`, `func_call`, `check_current_query` re-armed through a closure in `wpdb`'s scope), and `''` makes `query()` return before reaching the server.
- Any other statement on the table (save, delete) forgets every stored read. Direct `$wpdb->query()` calls are always run.

## Verification

- On a site's front page content (WP-CLI, separate processes): 1,612 → 62 queries; HTML identical apart from Fluent Forms' per-request line, which two runs without the fix also differ on.
- On a MySQL temporary table with a row: memoised `OBJECT` and `ARRAY_A` rows equal to fresh reads; empty results stay `null`; a caller changing a returned row does not change later reads; an `UPDATE` makes the next read query again and return the new document; `check_current_query` is `true` afterwards; a direct `query()` is run (returned 1).
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes.
- After release: web profile of the same page before and after deploy, home-page HTML parity, no new PHP log lines.

Upstream report to Kadence Blocks to follow; this fix can be removed once Kadence memoises `Token_Store` reads.

title: FluentCRM emails: dark mode setting per email (keep light or own dark colours) and per-app dark mode preview
body:
## What

Follow-up to #1030 (1.3.102: preview of mail apps' dark mode in FluentCRM's email designer).

Mail apps treat an email's colours in dark mode in two ways:

- **Apple Mail, Outlook for Mac, Thunderbird, HEY**: follow the email's own `<meta name="color-scheme">` and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` rules; with `color-scheme: light` they mostly leave it light.
- **Gmail apps, Outlook on Windows and the Outlook apps**: ignore both and recolour the email themselves.

FluentCRM 3.2.6's emails set neither (`app/Views/emails/*/Template.php`), and its designer has no dark colour settings.

1. **A setting per email**, in the designer's Style panel after Global colors: *In mail apps' dark mode*: **Let the mail app choose** (default, today's emails), **Keep light**, or **Use my dark colours**, with dark versions of Body background, Content background, Headings, Text and Links. Saved with the email's design settings (`settings.template_config`), so it goes with templates into campaigns, sequences and automations.
2. **The sent email** gets the matching `color-scheme` meta tags and, for dark colours, `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` rules.
3. **A preview per kind of mail app**: the designer's and Email Preview's dark-mode button chooses between **Apple Mail** (the email's own choice: its dark colours, light kept, or the app's own darkening) and **Gmail and Outlook** (the app recolours the email whatever it sets).

## How

- `includes/admin/class-seoprostack-admin-whole-theme.php` or a new class under `includes/` for FluentCRM email output: a filter on `fluent_crm/email-design-template-{block_editor,simple,plain,classic}` at priority 11 (after FluentCRM's CSS inliner, `app/Services/Libs/Emogrifier/Emogrifier.php`, which keeps only `@media` blocks) that adds the meta tags and a `<style>` with the dark rules before `</head>`, reading `$templateData['config']`. Rules use `!important` (FluentCRM inlines the light colours) and leave blocks with their own colours (`has-text-color`, `has-background`) as they are.
- Designer: `admin/js/seoprostack-mail-dark.js` adds the setting with `wp.element`/`wp.components` into `.fcrm-email-style-settings` and saves through FluentCRM's own `window._fcrmApplyDesignPreset()` (merges into its style config and posts `EDITOR_STYLE_CONFIG_CHANGE` to the screen around it, which merges into `campaign.settings.template_config`).
- Preview: the button becomes a menu (Off, Apple Mail, Gmail and Outlook). Apple Mail with dark colours: the designer canvas gets FluentCRM's colour properties (`--fcrm-body-bg`, `--fcrm-content-bg`, `--fcrm-headings-color`, `--theme-text-color`, `--fcrm-link-color`) in the dark values; Email Preview turns the email's own `prefers-color-scheme: dark` rules on or off whatever the computer's mode is.

## Verify

- Preview site, FluentCRM → Email Templates → a template with headings, text, a button, a coloured box and a picture: each setting saves and reloads; each preview mode shows as described in the designer and in Email Preview.
- The sent HTML (Send a test email, or the Email Preview frame) has the meta tags and rules for each setting, and none for *Let the mail app choose*.
- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh`, `scripts/plugin-check.sh`.

title: Load plugins only where needed: every LiteSpeed Cache purge resets what pages learned
body:
## What

**Load plugins only where needed** forgets the public map (`seoprostack_plugin_front`) whenever LiteSpeed Cache purges its page cache, so pages load every plugin until each page kind learns again. A purge does not change which plugins a page needs.

LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.2 saves `litespeed.purge.queue` or `litespeed.purge.queue2` (`LiteSpeed\Purge::DB_QUEUE`, `DB_QUEUE2`) on every purge: Purge All, `wp litespeed-purge`, and purges by post or address. Purge All also saves `litespeed.optimize.timestamp_purge_css` (`LiteSpeed\Optimize::ITEM_TIMESTAMP_PURGE_CSS`). From wp-admin, AJAX, REST or WP-CLI those writes count as setting changes (`record_write()` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`), so `forget_front()` runs.

## Evidence (1.3.102, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.2)

- On four sites, `seoprostack_plugin_front_forgets` was mostly `updated_option litespeed.purge.queue` (`kind: cli`), one per post-deployment purge; one site logged 8 in 3 minutes.
- Sites purged after a deployment held 0–3 learned page kinds, so most public pages kept loading every plugin.
- With the fix on a test copy, learning two kinds and then running `wp litespeed-purge all` and `wp litespeed-purge post_id <id>` left the map unchanged: same `learned`, same kinds, no new forget entry. Without it, the same Purge All emptied the map.

## Fix

`RECORD_OPTIONS` gains the prefix `litespeed.purge.` and the name `litespeed.optimize.timestamp_purge_css`, next to the existing `litespeed.task.` and `litespeed.crawler.`. LiteSpeed Cache's settings are `litespeed.conf.*` and still count as changes.

Files: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php` (`RECORD_OPTIONS` and its docblock), `README.md` (records list and changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- On a site with LiteSpeed Cache: let one page kind learn (a cache-miss visit), run `wp litespeed-purge all`, then check that `seoprostack_plugin_front` still has its kinds and that `seoprostack_plugin_front_forgets` has no new entry.

title: Load plugins only where needed: skip plugins that add to pages where a check render proves they change nothing
body:
## What

**Load plugins only where needed** skips few plugins on real sites. A plugin with any callback on a page hook (`FRONT_PAGE_HOOKS`, `FRONT_PAGE_PREFIXES`: `wp_head`, `wp_enqueue_scripts`, `the_content`, `body_class`, `pre_get_posts` and similar) is noted `pages`. `learn_front()` never makes such a plugin a candidate, whatever a page kind needs. Most plugins hook at least one of these, so they load on every public page.

Page-kind learning (`page_needs()`) already finds much smaller sets. On a site with 45 active plugins (1.3.102):

| | plugins |
|---|---|
| noted `pages` (load everywhere) | 36 |
| skippable at all (`candidates` plus plugins with no notes) | 13, of which 9 are skipped after dependencies |
| what `single:business` was learned to need (needs ∪ always ∪ core ∪ dependencies ∪ SEO Pro Stack) | 13 |

## Measured upside and why `needs` alone is not enough

A temporary must-use probe on a test copy limited `active_plugins` to that learned set of 13 for one listing page (cache misses, interleaved with full loads, 6 rounds):

- PHP time to `shutdown`: 1.0–1.6 s with 13 plugins, 1.2–2.2 s with 45; included files 3,802 vs 5,955; peak memory 32 MB vs 43 MB; queries 214 vs 280.
- The HTML was **not** the same: Rank Math's head tags (and the `<html prefix="og: …">` attribute) were missing, SEO Pro Cookie Consent's wrapper around a Google Maps iframe was missing, and WooCommerce's body class changed. So `needs` misses output that plugins print on page hooks, and the `pages` veto is protecting real output. Any change must prove a plugin's absence changes nothing.
- Kadence Blocks 3.8 reconciles design tokens at boot and rewrites `kadence_blocks_colors` and its sync marker when the set of loaded Kadence plugins changes. A request that skipped Kadence Pro or Kadence Blocks Pro would write options, and the next full request would write them back, forgetting the map each time. Kadence plugins are `always` today, which avoids this; keep it that way or treat their sync options as records.

## How (decision in the PR)

Verified skipping per page kind, as an extension of learning, not a new switch:

1. After a kind learns (`learn_front()`), schedule one verification for it: a cookie-free loopback GET of the same URL that skips the kind's proposed `pages` plugins (needs ∪ always ∪ core ∪ login ∪ dependencies kept). It uses a one-time signed request argument that `start_front()` honours only for that verification.
2. Compare it with the learned full render: response code, `Content-Type`, `Link`, `X-Robots-Tag` and cache headers, and the HTML normalised as tags and text (ignore asset `ver=` values, nonces, and IDs that change on every request). Only on an exact match store `verified` plugins for that kind; any difference stores nothing (and could narrow the set by bisecting a few times, if cheap).
3. `start_front()` adds a kind's `verified` plugins to what it skips, with the existing guards (cookie-free public GET, no auth, `always` and `core` notes, dependency closure). Everything that forgets the map forgets `verified` too.
4. If loopback requests fail (some hosts block them), times out, or the page is not cacheable, keep today's behaviour. Nothing may depend on one hosting setup.
5. README: explain `pages`, verified skipping, and what a visitor request may skip.

title: feat: Links skip redirects: internal links to a permanently redirected address point at its target
body:
## What

A new Links-tab feature, **Links skip redirects** (on by default). Links in posts, block widgets and menus to an old address that Rank Math permanently redirects to another page of the same site point straight at that page when the page is shown. The saved content is unchanged.

## Why

Renamed and moved pages keep their old address working through Rank Math → Redirections, but internal links still point at it. Every visit and crawl then takes an extra 301 step. One site does this today with a must-use plugin, which no plugin update reaches; it belongs in the stack as a generic feature.

## How

- New `includes/features/class-seoprostack-redirect-links.php` (`SEOProStack_Redirect_Links`, key `redirect_links`, tab `links`), listed in `SEOProStack_Setup`.
- Reads Rank Math's active, exact, 301/308 redirections whose target is on this site: one query, at most 500 rows, kept in a 10-minute transient. Temporary redirects and redirects to other sites (affiliate `/go/` links) are left alone. Nothing is cached on a request where Rank Math is not loaded.
- The transient is forgotten on `rank_math/redirection/post_updated`, `term_updated` and `deleted`.
- `the_content`, `widget_block_content` (`WP_HTML_Tag_Processor`) and `wp_nav_menu_objects`, at priority 20, front end only. Follows chains up to five hops and keeps fragments. Skips links with a query string. HTML that mentions no old address is not parsed.
- Filter `seoprostack_redirect_links` for redirects other plugins keep.

## Acceptance

1. On a site with a Rank Math 301 from `/how-it-works/` to `/for-my-property/`, a paragraph link and a menu item to `/how-it-works/` render as the new page's address; `/how-it-works/#x` keeps `#x`.
2. `/how-it-works/?x=1`, another host's `/how-it-works/`, `#login-drawer` and `mailto:` links are unchanged.
3. A 302 redirection, or one to another site, is not used.
4. `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes.

## Verification

`wp eval-file` on a review-copy site with the class loaded on its own, the map injected (no transient written). Then, after release, the rendered page HTML.

title: Load plugins only where needed: address checks reset by storage meta, stalled by a full queue, unstable under Rocket Loader and dated Expires
body:
## What

Follow-up to #1039 (released in 1.3.108). Fleet evidence after rollout showed per-address checks never finishing or being called unstable on several installs.

## Why

1. **Storage bookkeeping forgets learned pages.** A media storage pass writes `_seoprostack_storage*` post meta for thousands of attachments, from WP-CLI too (a "change" request). Each write ran `post_meta_changed()` → `forget_front()`; on one install the page revision changed every few seconds, so `SEOProStack_Front_Verify::run()` always found the map stale and no check finished.
2. **Full queue stops scheduling.** `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::queue_address()` returned before `wp_schedule_single_event()` when the queue held `QUEUE_MAX` (50). A run that stopped because the pages learned again left a full queue and no event; one install showed 50 queued, 0 checked, no `seoprostack_front_verify` event.
3. **Cloudflare Rocket Loader.** It rewrites each script `type` and inline handler with a per-response token (`TOKEN-text/javascript`, `data-cf-modified-TOKEN-`), named in `data-cf-settings`. One page changed 61 words per render (limit 50), so checks reported `unstable`.
4. **Dated Expires header.** A host sending `Expires` equal to the response date changed a compared header on every render (`unstable: changes on each render: expires: ...`).

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `RECORD_META_PREFIXES` (`_seoprostack_storage`, `_seoprostack_nextgen`, `_seoprostack_link_scan`, `_seoprostack_link_map`) skipped in `post_meta_changed()`, next to `RECORD_META`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: `queue_address()` schedules even when the queue is full.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-front-verify.php`: `normalise()` removes the Rocket Loader token; `render()` stores `expires` as minutes after `Date` (`expires()`).

## Verification

`scripts/lint.sh`; on an isolated review copy: storage-prefixed meta keeps `FRONT_REVISION` while a control key changes it; `queue_address()` with a full queue schedules the event; two captured Rocket Loader renders compare within the volatile limit after `normalise()`; a natural queue → verify run checks every queued address and a form page keeps its form plugin.

title: WebP and AVIF images: a conversion beside size generation records partial sizes, so their copies are never served or uploaded
body:
## What

**WebP and AVIF images** can mark a picture converted with a record that misses some of its sizes. **Media in cloud storage** uploads only the copies the record (`_seoprostack_nextgen`) lists, so those sizes' `.webp`/`.avif` copies stay on the server, never sent and never uploaded. With local removal on, the picture's other files leave and its storage drain never finishes.

## Why

WordPress saves an attachment's metadata after each size it makes (`_wp_make_subsizes()`), so another request that converts the picture meanwhile (a background batch beside an import, `wp media regenerate`, a watermark refresh) reads only the sizes made so far. `SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::convert_attachment()` then writes that record and `_seoprostack_nextgen_done`. `metadata_updated()` had deleted the done marker before the conversion finished, so nothing queued the picture again.

Seen on four pictures across three multisite installs during a bulk import with storage removal on: one stopped the import's storage drain; the others had current copies of sizes their records did not list (one record still flagged `incomplete`). They were repaired by converting again, after which audits found no unlisted copies and the bucket served the copies (HTTP 200).

Reproduced on a disposable WordPress 7.1.4 / PHP 8.3 site with 1.3.114: adding a size while `convert_attachment()` runs leaves the picture done with the new size missing from its record.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`
  - New post meta `_seoprostack_nextgen_generation`, changed by `metadata_updated()` on every metadata save.
  - `convert_attachment()` reads the generation before the sizes (from the database), and records only when the generation, attached file and file names are unchanged at the end; otherwise it leaves the picture waiting and returns `nextgen_changed`. The next conversion keeps the copies made (they are up to date) and lists every size.
  - `run_batch()` and `wp seoprostack convert-images` pass over pictures that stay waiting after an error, once per run, so neither loops on them.
  - New `record_unlisted()`: converts a converted picture again when up-to-date copies of its files are not in its record (records from before the fix, or none).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`: `upload_attachment()` calls `record_unlisted()` after bringing back removed files, and queues the picture for the next batch when it changed its record.

## Verification

- `php -l`, PHPCS on the changed files, PHPStan.
- Disposable site, same race script on 1.3.114 and the fix: 1.3.114 records the picture done without the new size; the fix leaves it waiting, then records every size on the next conversion. `record_unlisted()` lists a stale record's copy without re-encoding it, does nothing the second time, converts a picture with no record, and leaves a waiting picture alone.

title: Media in cloud storage: unique file names read every stored picture on each upload (seconds per picture on large libraries)
body:
## What happens

With Media in cloud storage removing local copies, every upload asks WordPress for a unique file name, and `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::unique_filename_files()` (filter `pre_wp_unique_filename_file_list`) answers by streaming **every** stored inventory of the site (`stored_records()`, pages of 100) and listing every stored name in the folder. The cost grows with the library, and it is paid more than once per picture (sideload, Resize uploads' temporary and converted names).

Measured on production stacks (read-only call of the filter for this month's folder, 30 October 2026):

| Site | Stored attachments | One call | Queries | Names returned | Peak memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lloydminster | 1,385 | 0.27s | 29 | 30,405 | 443 MB |
| West Sussex | 15,221 | 2.92s | 307 | 248,209 | 500 MB |
| Burnaby | 18,949 | 7.24s | 381 | 567,699 | 698 MB |

A transaction-rolled-back import profile on Lloydminster put pictures at 2.27s of 3.43s per listing, the inventory pages being the two slowest query shapes. West Sussex's import runs at 7–20s per listing, slowing as a part goes on; directory imports of a few thousand listings take tens of hours.

## Why only part of the list matters

WordPress 7.1 `wp_unique_filename()` uses the list only through `_wp_check_existing_file_names()` (`/^{fname}-(?:\d+x\d+|scaled|rotated){ext}$/i`) for the name it is numbering and its alternate-format names. Every name it tests starts with the file name's stem without a trailing `-N` number. Names that do not start with that stem can never change the result.

## Change

- `unique_filename_files()` keeps only names that start (ASCII case-insensitively, as the regex) with that stem, including the local `scandir()` names.
- Stored names come from the inventories whose serialized value contains `"{folder}/{stem}` (one `LIKE` in the database, also for the stem without `-scaled` for the virtual scaled sibling), instead of every inventory.
- Same result for WordPress; a stem that cannot be worked out falls back to the full list.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php` — `unique_filename_files()`, `stored_records()`/`inventory_ids()` pattern, `handover_records()`.

## Verification

- `composer`/project lint and PHPStan as the repository's checks require.
- On a stack with stored media: the filter's output for a stem equals the full list filtered by that stem; time per call is in milliseconds and does not grow with the library.
- An upload whose name matches an existing stored picture still gets a new number (GH#956 regression).

title: Fluent Support email by IMAP: tickets from the site's own mailbox, without Fluent's hosted relay
body:
## What

Fluent Support Pro only turns email into tickets through Fluent's hosted relay, which gives each business inbox a forwarding address and pushes every email to the site. The relay refuses a site without an active licence (`You don't have a valid license! Please make sure you activate the license first.`). The code that makes the ticket runs on the site, in Fluent Support Pro's own GPL code: `FluentSupportPro\App\Services\Integrations\FluentEmailPiping\ByMailHandler::processPayload()`, which the relay's push route calls.

Add an off-by-default feature, **Fluent Support email by IMAP** (Plugins tab), that reads the site's own support mailbox over IMAP and hands each new email to that local code. Then tickets need no relay, forwarding address or licence call. Fluent Support Pro's files are not changed.

## Why

Sites running our plugins send product reports by email to our support desk (Fluent Support). The intake has to work without a third-party relay.

## How

- New `includes/features/class-seoprostack-helpdesk-imap.php` (`SEOProStack_Helpdesk_Imap`), registered in `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`; cleanup in `uninstall.php`.
- Settings: `helpdesk_imap` (switch), `helpdesk_imap_host` (`host:993` SSL or `:143` STARTTLS, certificate always checked), `helpdesk_imap_user`, `helpdesk_imap_mailbox` (Fluent business inbox ID; 0 = the inbox whose address is the user name, else the default). Password only from `SEOPROSTACK_HELPDESK_IMAP_PASSWORD` in `wp-config.php` or the `seoprostack_helpdesk_imap_password` filter.
- Every 5 minutes (WP-Cron) and `wp seoprostack helpdesk-mail fetch|status`: reads by UID after the last one read (first run: the last day), up to 25 emails a run within 20 seconds, with `FT_PEEK`. Builds the relay's payload shape and applies Fluent's own `fluent_support_pro/email_piping_raw_data` filter. Fluent's own duplicate, reply and auto-reply checks still apply. Attachments stay in the mailbox and are named on the ticket.
- `phpstan-plugin.neon`: the existing `method_exists()` ignore for Fluent classes also matches PHPStan's shortened class names (`FluentSupportPro…`).

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`: all passed (PHP, JS, shell, workflows, PHPCS, PHPStan).

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Two site-identity standards that the owner's regional sites currently get from per-site scripts:

1. **Identity sync**: the site's name, logo (PNG) and social fallback image written to Rank Math's schema/Open Graph settings from one place (Site Identity plus a social image setting), kept in sync when they change; Pages default to `WebPage`, not `Article`.
2. **Copied-site health**: `wp seoprostack health` detects and repairs what a site copy breaks: font paths still pointing at the source site, and missing tables for active Rank Math modules.

## Today

Per-site scripts set Rank Math's organisation name/logo, the default social image and the Page schema type, and repair copied sites' font paths and Rank Math tables by hand. Two scripts write the same schema identity, so they can disagree.

## How

- Extend the existing Rank Math preset (`presets/seo-by-rank-math.json`) and the feature that applies presets; add an identity sync on `update_option_blogname`, `update_option_site_icon`, logo change and the new social image setting.
- Add both checks to `seoprostack health` (existing command, `add_command('seoprostack health'`), each with a dry-run report and a repair.

title: Detect a split object cache: scheduled tasks or WP-CLI use a persistent cache that page views don't
body:
## Problem

A site can have an object cache drop-in that only some PHP runtimes can use. Example: the web PHP lacks the Memcached extension, but the PHP that runs scheduled tasks or WP-CLI has it. Only those runtimes then use the persistent cache. Web writes never invalidate it, so scheduled tasks read old copies of every option.

Seen in #1071: Load plugins only where needed checked nothing for 80 minutes, because the scheduled run's copy of `seoprostack_plugin_front` had no page kinds. The same split serves other plugins' scheduled tasks old settings and an old cron list. That is likely part of what #1055 worked around.

Sites move between hosts, so SEO Pro Stack should detect this itself rather than rely on per-host notes.

## Proposal

- Record whether a persistent object cache is in use, per kind of request (web, cron, WP-CLI). `wp_using_ext_object_cache()` plus the drop-in's class are enough, saved as a small non-autoloaded record by each kind.
- When the kinds disagree, show it in Hosting needs or Site health: "Scheduled tasks use a persistent object cache that page views don't, so they can read old settings". Give the fix: turn the drop-in off, or give both runtimes the same PHP extensions.
- Optional: in the verifier, read `FRONT`, `FRONT_REVISION` and `FRONT_PAGES` fresh (like `fresh_queue()`) when the split is detected.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php` (or the Site health integration): detection and notice. The exact place is not yet chosen.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-front-verify.php`, `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php` for the optional fresh reads.

## Verification

On a test site, add a drop-in that reports a persistent cache only when `PHP_SAPI === 'cli'`. After a cron run and a page view, the notice appears; with no drop-in, it doesn't.

title: Load plugins only where needed: don't forget learned pages when an option write leaves its value unchanged
body:
## Problem

Load plugins only where needed forgets every learned page kind when a watched option is written, even if the write leaves the option's value unchanged.

Seen while diagnosing #1071 on a Kadence site: a WP-CLI command run with `--skip-themes` (an `eval-file` that only reads options) fires `updated_option` for `kadence_blocks_colors`. The site then relearns from scratch. The same command without `--skip-themes` does not. The option's hash was identical before and after such a run, so the request appears to change the value and change it back. Repeated diagnostic or maintenance runs kept the site learning: the log shows five resets in 90 minutes, each from a WP-CLI run.

## Proposal

When a watched option is written, record its value from the start of the request instead of forgetting at once. At `shutdown`, forget only if the option's final value differs from that start value. For writes that touch many options, store only a hash.

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `changelog.txt`

Implementation is confined to the feature; the existing loader forget/log path remains unchanged. Documentation paths keep the required user-facing changelogs in step. Verify with scoped PHPCS/PHPStan and real WordPress option writes (unchanged, reverted, changed, added/deleted, and ignored records).

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `record_write()` and `RECORD_OPTIONS`, where option writes trigger a forget.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: the forget path and the `seoprostack_plugin_front_forgets` log.

## Verification

On a Kadence site with learned kinds, run `wp eval 'get_option("kadence_blocks_colors");' --skip-themes`, or any command that reproduces the write. Learned kinds survive, and `seoprostack_plugin_front_forgets` gains no entry. Change a Kadence colour in the Customizer: kinds are forgotten as before.

title: Fixes for other plugins: Kadence Blocks Style Library colours stay light in Kadence Pro dark mode
body:
## What

With Kadence Blocks 3.8 and Kadence Pro's dark mode, a block colour chosen from Kadence Blocks' **Style Library** (for example Text (Adv) → Colour → Contrast → Strongest) stays the same in dark mode, while palette colours around it switch. Text then disappears on its own background in one of the modes.

Seen on a live client site (Kadence 1.5.2, Kadence Pro 1.2.7, Kadence Blocks 3.8.1, Kadence Blocks Pro 2.8.20.1): a Text (Adv) heading in synced pattern 1006 has Style Library "Strongest" text on a palette 8 background. In dark mode the background becomes `#273e49` and the text stays `#000000` (about 1.9:1).

**SEO Pro Stack's Fixes for other plugins** should make Style Library colours that come from the Kadence palette follow Kadence Pro's dark mode, as palette colours do. Neither plugin's settings or saved blocks change.

## Why

The block's CSS uses a primitive design token, not a palette variable:

```css
.wp-block-kadence-advancedheading.kt-adv-heading1006_24296b-48 { color: var(--kb-token--primitive--color--neutral--900); }
```

Kadence Blocks prints the tokens as fixed colours on `:root` (`<style id="kadence-blocks-global-variables-inline-css">`, selector `:root,:root:where(.kb-tokens)`):

```text
--kb-token--primitive--color--brand--primary:#007099     = light palette1
--kb-token--primitive--color--brand--secondary:#008fcc   = light palette2
--kb-token--primitive--color--neutral--900:#000000       = light palette3
--kb-token--primitive--color--neutral--700:#343a3c       = light palette4
--kb-token--primitive--color--neutral--600:#2a434e       = light palette5
--kb-token--primitive--color--neutral--500:#004766       = light palette6
--kb-token--primitive--color--neutral--100:#e5ebee       = light palette7
--kb-token--primitive--color--neutral--50:#f8f9fa        = light palette8
--kb-token--primitive--color--neutral--0:#ffffff         = light palette9
(neutral--200, neutral--300, brand--accent, brand--button(-hover), notice--* match no slot)
```

Semantic and preset tokens on the same `:root` rule read the primitives (`--kb-token--semantic--color--text:var(--kb-token--primitive--color--neutral--900)`, `--kb-token--preset--…:var(--kb-token--semantic--…)`), so they resolve on `:root` too.

Kadence Pro's dark mode changes only `--global-palette1`…`15` and `--wp--preset--color--theme-palette-N` on `body.color-switch-dark`. A token fixed on `:root` never sees that, so every Style Library colour keeps its light value. `STYLING.md` → Front-end styling and dark mode already records this trap: variables defined on `:root` from palette colours keep the light values.

SEO Pro Stack does not cause this: its existing Kadence Blocks 3.8 fix (#763, `kadence_palette_before/after` in the same class) only keeps the theme's colours when the **dark** palette is read, so the light/active palette, and with it the tokens, are unchanged.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`: add a fix next to the #763 one (file docblock paragraph, `boot()` hook, same `KADENCE_TOKENS_FROM` version gate, only when Kadence Pro's dark mode is on: `defined('KTP_VERSION')` and the theme's `dark_mode_enable`, as `SEOProStack_Kadence_Colour_Check::palettes()` reads it).
  - Work out which primitive colour token stands for which palette slot. Prefer Kadence Blocks' own mapping: `KadenceWP\KadenceBlocks\Design_Tokens\Projection\Kadence_Option\Palette_Filter` (on `kadence_palette_option`) already maps slots to tokens; read the installed Kadence Blocks source on the preview site and use its public API if one exists. Otherwise match each primitive's value to the active palette slot of the same colour, case-insensitively, and skip tokens that match no slot or more than one.
  - Print, after Kadence Blocks' global variables (for example `wp_add_inline_style()` on its `kadence-blocks-global-variables` handle, or the same hook Kadence prints it on), a `body.color-switch-dark { … }` rule that sets each mapped primitive to `var(--global-paletteN)`, and repeats the semantic and preset colour token declarations that read those primitives, so they resolve on `body` where the palette changes. Only colour tokens; spacing, type and other tokens stay on `:root`.
  - Colours on `body` follow dark mode; `:root` keeps the light values, so nothing outside `body` changes, and light mode is unchanged.
- `README.md` → Fixes for other plugins: one entry after "Kadence Blocks design tokens and Kadence Pro's dark mode"; `changelog.txt`: one Fix line naming this issue.

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- On a Kadence site with Kadence Pro dark mode and Kadence Blocks 3.8.x, with a Text (Adv) heading using Style Library "Strongest" text on a palette 8 background: in dark mode the heading's computed colour is the dark palette's palette 3; in light mode it is unchanged (`#000000` on the live example). Block colours chosen as palette colours, and Style Library colours that match no slot (Button, notices), are unchanged in both modes.
- The debug log stays clean with the fix on and with Kadence Blocks deactivated (no token CSS printed then).
- `STYLING.md` → Test: view the page in light and dark mode.

## Notes

- Workaround until this ships: pick a theme palette colour rather than a Style Library one, then check the block's CSS reads `var(--global-paletteN)`, which follows dark mode.
- Upstream: worth reporting to Kadence that Style Library colours seeded from the palette do not follow Kadence Pro's dark mode; this fix stands in until they do.

title: Fluent Support email by IMAP: save sent ticket emails to the mailbox Sent folder
body:
## What

With **Fluent Support email by IMAP** on, every email Fluent Support sends to a customer from that inbox should also be saved to the mailbox's Sent folder over IMAP, so the owner's mailbox keeps the support record, as a mail app would. Outgoing mail itself is unchanged: it still goes through the site's mail plugin (for example FluentSMTP with Amazon SES).

## Why

Replies go out through the site's mail plugin, not the mailbox's own server, so no copy reaches Sent. The owner wants the mailbox to be the record. This also follows the IMAP-only, no-vendor-relay policy in `AGENTS.md`.

## Scope

- Only customer emails Fluent Support sends from the IMAP feature's inbox: ticket created, agent reply, closed by agent, ticket created by agent, ticket created on the customer's behalf. Each passes `fluent_support/mail_to_customer_header`, with the ticket. Agent and admin notifications, FluentCRM and other site mail are not copied.
- The copy is the exact message sent: the global PHPMailer's `getSentMIMEMessage()` after `wp_mail_succeeded`, with core `wp_mail()` and FluentSMTP's alike. It is stored with the `\Seen` flag.
- Sent folder: a setting, or found by name (Sent, Sent Items, Sent Messages, INBOX.Sent …). Never created.
- The copy is saved at the end of the request. If it fails, it waits in a capped, non-autoloaded queue and the five-minute run tries again. `wp seoprostack helpdesk-mail status` shows copies saved, waiting and the last error. No addresses or message text appear in the log.

## Files

- `includes/class-seoprostack-helpdesk-imap-sent.php` (new): capture, queue and append.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-helpdesk-imap-connection.php`: folder list and append.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-helpdesk-imap.php`: settings (`helpdesk_imap_sent`, `helpdesk_imap_sent_folder`), boot, run and status.
- `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `README.md`.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`, PHPMD and `scripts/preflight-release.sh`.
- Live on the owner's support site, after the release: an agent reply on a test ticket shows up in the mailbox's Sent folder (counted over IMAP), and nothing goes to INBOX.

title: Review links block: copyable review and configured review short links after a feedback form
body:
## What

A **Review links** block (`seoprostack/review-links`) for a feedback page: placed after a keyed Fluent form (SEO Pro Stack's Form by key), it stays hidden until that form is submitted, then shows:

- a thank-you line;
- the visitor's comment in a read-only box with a **Copy review** button (Clipboard API, with a select-all fallback and an announced "Copied" status);
- buttons for the site's configured review short links — `/googlereview/`, `/facebookreview/`, `/trustpilotreview/` from Short links' starter review links — in that order. A link counts as configured when it is published and its target is no longer the starter placeholder (`https://google.com`, `https://facebook.com`, `https://trustpilot.com`, `SEOProStack_Short_Links::presets()`). With none configured, the block shows only the thank-you line.

Rating handling (owner decision, 31 October 2026): links are **never gated by rating**. 4–5 stars: the copy box and links lead ("Would you share this where others can find it?"). 1–3 stars: "Thanks — we'll be in touch to put things right" first, the links still offered below with neutral wording. Every rating is submitted by the form itself, so it reaches wherever the site's contact messages go.

Attributes: `formKey` (the Fluent form's SEO Pro Stack key, default `feedback-review`), `ratingField` (default `rating`), `commentField` (default `comment`), headings and button labels with translatable defaults. Server-rendered (render callback); front-end script listens for Fluent Forms' `fluentform_submission_success` on that form, reading the values captured on submit (Fluent Forms may reset the form).

## Why

Our website templates' feedback page needs this; review-gating by rating breaches Google's and Trustpilot's review policies, so links stay available for every rating.

## How

- NEW: `blocks/review-links/block.json`, `blocks/review-links/index.js` (editor: attributes panel, preview), `blocks/review-links/view.js`, `blocks/review-links/style.css`.
- NEW or EDIT: render in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-short-links.php` (it owns the review presets) or a small `includes/features/class-seoprostack-review-links.php` registered like `blocks/link-card` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-link-card-block.php:101`).
- Reuse `SEOProStack_Short_Links::presets()` and `link()` / `map()` for live targets; link to the short address (`url($slug)`), so clicks are counted.
- Kadence-compatible styling: theme palette variables, button classes like the Form block's; no inline colours.
- README and changelog; release as the next patch version.

## Acceptance

- After a 5-star submission: comment shown, copy works (keyboard and screen reader), only configured links shown.
- After a 2-star submission: follow-up message first, links still shown.
- Block hidden before submission; no output errors when Short links is off (then no links, thank-you only).
- `composer phpcs`/phpstan and the JS build clean.

## Verification

A template site with Short links on, after release deploy: submit 2 and 5 stars, check the page at desktop and mobile widths, check the entry arrived where contact messages go.

title: Support tickets from site email use Reply-To as the customer; MainWP Contact Support adds the client's Reply-To
body:
## Problem

Tickets created from site emails belong to the site's own sender address, not to the person who wrote them. Agent replies then go to that site address and never reach the person.

- Sites send through FluentSMTP with **Force From Email** on, which most providers (Amazon SES included) need. The person's address only survives as `Reply-To`, or not at all.
- **Fluent Support email by IMAP** (`includes/class-seoprostack-helpdesk-imap-message.php`, `payload()`) takes the ticket customer from `From:` only.
- Affected:
  - **Report a problem** (wpallstars-reports): it sets the sending administrator as `Reply-To`, but the ticket customer is the site's sender.
  - **MainWP Child "Contact Support"** (`admin.php?page=ContactSupport`, MainWP Branding extension): `MainWP_Utility::send_support_mail()` puts the client's typed address in `From:` and adds no `Reply-To`. FluentSMTP replaces that `From:`, so the client's address is left only in the message body.

## Change

1. **Intake** (`payload()`): when the email has exactly one `Reply-To` address, and it is not the inbox's own address, use it as the ticket customer (`from`). Otherwise keep `From:`. The original `From:` stays in the headers map. Document this in the setting description, README and changelog.
2. **Plugin fixes** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`, next to the existing MainWP Child branding footer fix): on `mainwp_child_contact_support_mail_headers`, add `Reply-To:` with the address the client typed, or their account email, when the headers have none. MainWP's settings are left alone.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`, `bash scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline`.
- Live: the MainWP Dashboard's global branding support email is set to the support inbox. Send the Contact Support form from a Property Services Directory stack. The ticket's customer is the client's address, and the ticket body names the site.

## Context

Owner decision (2026-10-31): MainWP Contact Support for all sites goes to the WPALLSTARS support desk. Customer replies must reach the person who wrote in.

title: Kadence icon picker: render icons on scroll or search; Dev tab line makes the sidebar tabs scroll
body:
## What

1. Kadence Blocks' Select Icon picker is still slow to open after #1087 (content-visibility). Measured on the preview site (dark mode): each warm open spends ~360 ms in script and ~370 ms recalculating style for 5,482 icons (22,376 elements), after Kadence's 100 ms debounce; the first open after selecting a block takes ~2.6 s. 3,806 of the icons are SEO Pro Stack's own Brand icons set (`admin/js/seoprostack-kadence-brand-icons.js`).
2. The block editor's settings sidebar shows a horizontal scrollbar under its tabs (Page/Block/Dev) while the Dev tab is open.

## Cause

1. Kadence's picker (`kadence-blocks/dist/*.js`, component with `kadence-icon-picker-pop-selection`) renders every icon of every set in "Show All", inside core `PanelBody`s. Its list comes from `applyFilters('kadence.icon_options_names', kadence_blocks_params.icon_names)` (memoised per picker mount) and is rebuilt only when the search text or the set filter changes; it calls `.map()` on each set's array.
2. `SEOProStack_Editor_Dev_Tab` (`admin/js/seoprostack-editor-dev-tab.js`, `underline()`) places the tab line under Dev with `offsetLeft`/`offsetWidth`, which round to whole pixels. The tab list is `overflow-x: auto`; when both round up, the line ends past the list (a forced 0.6 px made it scrollable on the preview site), so a scrollbar shows.

## Fix

1. Faster editor with Kadence Blocks (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-kadence-library.php`, new `admin/js/seoprostack-kadence-icon-picker.js`): a last `kadence.icon_options_names` filter gives each large set an array whose `.map()` goes through its first 100 icons while nothing is searched and Show All is chosen; scrolling near the end of a set shows more (Kadence's own set filter is changed and changed back in one task, so its list is rebuilt without a visible change). Searching, or choosing one set, covers every icon.
2. `underline()` uses fractional positions from `getBoundingClientRect()`, and the line never ends past the list.

## Verification

- Preview site, Playwright: icon picker open time and script/style metrics before and after (light and dark); search finds an icon past the first 100 and choosing it sets the block's icon; scrolling to the end of a set shows more icons and keeps the scroll position; choosing one set shows all of it.
- Dev tab open: the tab list is not scrollable (`scrollLeft` stays 0) at several tab widths.
- `scripts/lint.sh`.

title: Kadence icon picker still slow to appear: open on press, draw fewer icons first, no fade, skip popovers in menu fitting
body:
## What

The Kadence icon picker (Icon Settings → Select Icon) still takes a noticeable time to appear after a click, even with 1.3.124's incremental drawing (#1095).

## Evidence (preview site, dark mode, Text (Adv) block)

Timeline from the press, measured with Playwright and a Chrome trace:

- Kadence waits 100 ms after the click before it opens (its toggle is a `debounce(…, 100)`), and the press itself lasts ~90 ms before the click fires.
- React draws ~450 icon buttons (~2,100 elements); the style recalc for them costs ~90 ms (~33 µs per element, with ~540 stylesheets on the editor).
- The popover then fades in over 100 ms and slides for 200 ms (WordPress `Popover` motion); each frame recalcs ~1,000 elements.
- During that animation SEO Pro Stack's own observers add ~65 ms (`seoprostack-admin-menu.js` `flush()` checks every element added, with `getComputedStyle`) and ~40 ms (`seoprostack-whole-theme.js`).

Median press-to-visible: ~0.5–0.9 s.

## How to fix (SEO Pro Stack only)

- `admin/js/seoprostack-kadence-icon-picker.js`: open the picker on the press (pointerdown), like a native select, and drop the click that follows; draw fewer icons first (enough to fill the view), loading more on scroll as now.
- Show the popover at once (no fade) via the existing inline style in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-kadence-library.php`.
- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`: skip the contents of elements a script places (inline left/right/transform, as popovers), which move with them.

## Verify

Re-run the press-to-visible timing on the preview site; search, set filter, scroll loading and choosing an icon still work; keyboard (Enter/Space) still opens the picker.

## What

warn   size 10272 bytes; WordPress.org says over 10 KB may cause errors (keep the current changelog, move older entries to changelog.txt, trim the description)

- Aim for under 9.5 KB, so the next few releases' changelog lines fit.
- No version bump needed: a docs-only change can go out with the next release.

- `wc -c readme.txt` is under 10240.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh` no longer prints the size warning.
- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.

title: t23: Site templates: ship website templates in SEO Pro Stack and update unedited parts on plugin update
body:
## Task


A new SEO Pro Stack feature, "Site templates", that:

1. Ships template manifests as JSON in `site-templates/<slug>.json` (like `presets/` and `starters/`).
2. Records, per site, which template (slug + manifest version) it was made from, and per page the SHA-256 of each part as the template wrote it.
3. On a plugin update (stored version differs from `SEOPROSTACK_VERSION`), schedules a per-site update that replaces only parts whose current markup still has the recorded hash (unedited), adds new parts, and keeps and lists edited or removed parts.
4. Provides WP-CLI: `wp seoprostack site-templates list|status|diff|apply|undo [--url=…]` and a network-wide `--all-sites` mode, plus a per-site setting "Update unedited template parts automatically" (default on for template sites, on for client sites; network admins can turn it off per site).

<details>
<summary>Worker implementation contract</summary>

## Worker Guidance


Manifest format (produced by the agency's builder; SEO Pro Stack only consumes it). Keep the schema documented in the class docblock, as `class-seoprostack-presets.php` and `class-seoprostack-starters.php` do:

- `slug`, `name`, `version`, `updated`, `notes`
- `pages`: key, title, slug, template, `parts` (ordered list of key + block markup); page content is the parts joined
- `elements`: Kadence Pro Hooked Elements (`kadence_element` posts) with meta, matched by a stable key in post meta
- `custom_css` as base + site-owned remainder (replace only the leading base block when it is still the old base; keep whatever follows)
- `theme_mods`, `options`, `widgets`, `menus`: named-key merge as presets do; only keys the manifest names
- `images`: key, filename, SHA-256, placeholder flag; shipped under `site-templates/<slug>/images/`, imported once, never replaced once a site has swapped the attachment
- forms: reference a starter form by key (`SEOProStack_Form_Keys`), do not duplicate

Per-site record (option `seoprostack_site_template`): slug, applied manifest version, per page/element/part SHA-256 as written, last result (updated / added / edited-on-site / removed-on-site lists), and a backup of everything the last run changed for `undo`.

Update trigger: compare a stored version with `SEOPROSTACK_VERSION` as `includes/features/class-seoprostack-brand-icons.php:550-580` does; on change, schedule a single WP-Cron event per site (multisite: each site handles its own on its next request/cron run, so no network-wide loop in one request). Also hook `upgrader_process_complete` as `class-seoprostack-integrity-checks.php:125` does.

Ultimate Multisite: a site cloned from a template site inherits the option (it is copied with the tables), so client sites follow automatically. Clear nothing on clone.

Purge caches after a run that changed something (use the existing LiteSpeed/page-cache helpers: `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`, `includes/class-seoprostack-page-cache.php`).

### Files to Modify

- NEW: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-site-templates.php` (feature: settings, boot, update trigger, runner)
- NEW: `includes/class-seoprostack-site-templates-cli.php` (model on `includes/class-seoprostack-presets-cli.php`: list/diff/apply/undo)
- NEW: `site-templates/` (empty `README.md` describing the format until the first manifests are added)
- EDIT: feature registration where other features are registered (`includes/class-seoprostack.php`), CLI registration alongside the presets/starters CLI
- EDIT: readme/changelog per repository convention

### Hazards and Compatibility

- Never overwrite a part whose hash differs from the recorded one; never delete a page, element or attachment.
- A site with no record is never touched (only sites made from a template carry one).
- Placeholder images: replace only if the attachment is still the template's placeholder (hash match).
- Kadence Pro Elements and Fluent Forms may be inactive on a site: skip those sections and report.
- Bounded work per run; resume on the next event when a run is cut short.

### Files Scope

- includes/features/class-seoprostack-site-templates.php
- includes/class-seoprostack-site-templates-cli.php
- includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php
- site-templates/README.md
- readme.txt
- README.md
- changelog.txt
- uninstall.php

Integration evidence: current feature registration is SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES; CLI registration can live in the new feature boot method. The shared registry must stay unchanged. Repository standards require README.md, changelog.txt (CHANGELOG.md does not exist), and uninstall cleanup for all added options, cron hooks and ownership meta. No open PRs or starter-sync issues collide with these paths. Verification: scoped PHP lint/PHPCS/PHPStan, existing release preflight, and disposable WordPress runtime checks of apply, edited/removed parts, undo, and multisite isolation.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief


Target repository: wpallstars/seoprostack

## Origin

Owner request (interactive session, 2026-11-01): website templates (a One-page and a Multi-page local business website, built as Ultimate Multisite template sites on several multisite networks) should get later design tweaks "via theme/plugin updates", on every network and on client sites made from them, without overwriting what a client has edited.

## What

A new SEO Pro Stack feature, "Site templates", that:

1. Ships template manifests as JSON in `site-templates/<slug>.json` (like `presets/` and `starters/`).
2. Records, per site, which template (slug + manifest version) it was made from, and per page the SHA-256 of each part as the template wrote it.
3. On a plugin update (stored version differs from `SEOPROSTACK_VERSION`), schedules a per-site update that replaces only parts whose current markup still has the recorded hash (unedited), adds new parts, and keeps and lists edited or removed parts.
4. Provides WP-CLI: `wp seoprostack site-templates list|status|diff|apply|undo [--url=…]` and a network-wide `--all-sites` mode, plus a per-site setting "Update unedited template parts automatically" (default on for template sites, on for client sites; network admins can turn it off per site).

## Why

Today the manifests are applied from an agency's private repository over SSH, one site at a time, by a script that already implements the per-part rule (unedited part takes the new version; edited part is kept and reported). Fifteen template sites across five networks need about eight manual applies per change, and client sites made from the templates get nothing. SEO Pro Stack runs on every site and already updates from GitHub, so shipping the manifests in a release reaches every site.

## Tier

tier:thinking — a new feature with a data model, update safety (never overwrite client edits), multisite scheduling and undo.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With a test manifest in `site-templates/`, `wp seoprostack site-templates apply <slug>` on an empty site creates the pages, elements, CSS and settings, and records hashes; `status` then reports every part `same`.
2. After editing one part on the site and shipping a manifest with changes to that part and another, a version bump updates the unedited part, keeps the edited one, and `status` lists it as `edited-on-site`.
3. `undo` restores the site to its state before the last run.
4. A site without a record is untouched by a version bump.
5. On multisite, each site runs its own update via cron; `--all-sites` runs them sequentially from WP-CLI and stops at the first failure.
6. PHP lint and the repository's existing checks pass.

## Context & Decisions

- Chosen over separate child-theme repositories per template: template sites run the Kadence parent theme, and one plugin already on every site keeps one update channel.
- The agency builder stays the source of truth for manifests; this feature only consumes them. Exporting the builder's manifests into this format is a separate task in the agency's repository.
- Owner's sizing convention for later layout-library reuse: xs/s/m/l/xl/xxl tokens where possible.

</details>

title: Dark mode: Kadence typography popover in the Customizer is white
body:
## What

In Dark mode, the Kadence theme's typography popover in the Customizer (Colors & Fonts → Typography → Base Font → Font / Style / Size) opens with a white background behind dark fields and light text. The same white shows in Kadence's other popovers that carry `kadence-popover-color` (colour and background pickers).

## Why

Kadence's `inc/customizer/react/build/controls.css` (1.5.2) paints

```css
.components-popover.kadence-popover-color .components-popover__content { background: rgb(255, 255, 255); }
```

at specificity (0,3,0). The typography popover has that class too (`components-popover kadence-popover-color kadence-popover-typography kadence-customizer-popover`). The hand-written rule in `admin/css/seoprostack-whole-theme.css` (WordPress components, `html.sps-dark :is(… .components-popover__content …)`) is only (0,2,1), so it loses.

On the preview site the popover is dark only because the Dark mode fallback (`SEOProStack_Dark_Fallback`) has made its copy of `controls.css` in `uploads/seoprostack-dark/`. Wherever that copy is missing (first loads after a Kadence update, the per-request budget, an unwritable uploads folder, or the fallback filtered off), the popover is white. Reproduced on the preview site by blocking `uploads/seoprostack-dark/` requests in Playwright: `.components-popover__content` computes to `rgb(255, 255, 255)` on all three tabs.

## How

- `admin/css/seoprostack-whole-theme.css`, Customizer → Kadence's controls section (near the `.kadence-palette-popover-copy-paste` rule): add a hand-written rule for `.components-popover.kadence-popover-color .components-popover__content` behind `html.sps-dark` with the dark surface, text and the same edge and shadow as the WordPress components popover rule.
- Changelog lines in `changelog.txt` and `README.md` (Unreleased).

## Verify

- Preview site, Dark mode, Customizer → Colors & Fonts → Typography → Base Font: open Size, Style and Font with `uploads/seoprostack-dark/` blocked; the popover is the dark surface (`rgb(29, 35, 39)`), with no white panel behind the Reset buttons or fields.

title: Dark mode: Kadence typography preview in the Customizer is a harsh checkerboard
body:
## What

In Dark mode, the Kadence theme's typography preview in the Customizer (Colors & Fonts → Typography → a font setting → the arrow button on the right) shows the sample sentence "Design is not just what it looks like…" on a harsh light-and-black checkerboard, and the site's dark text colour is hard to read on it.

## Why

Kadence 1.5.2 (`inc/customizer/react/build/controls.css`, `.kadence-preview-font`) draws the box as `#ddd` squares over `transparent` ones, meant to sit on the light Customizer panel (a faint light-grey checkerboard). In Dark mode the panel behind is dark, so the clear squares turn near-black. The sample text uses the site's own font colour (for example `var(--global-palette4)`, meant for light pages), so it loses contrast. `admin/css/seoprostack-whole-theme.css` has no rule for `.kadence-preview-font`.

## How

- `admin/css/seoprostack-whole-theme.css`, Customizer → Kadence's controls section, next to the colour swatch rule (`html.sps-dark .components-button.kadence-color-icon-indicate`): give `html.sps-dark .wp-customizer .kadence-preview-font` a white `background-color` under Kadence's checkerboard, and a dark default `color` for settings without a colour (Kadence's inline `color` still wins when one is set). The preview then looks as it does in light mode: a small light "page" showing the site's real text colour. Darkening the checkerboard instead would leave dark site text unreadable.
- `changelog.txt`, `README.md`, `readme.txt`: entry.

## Verification

Preview site, Dark mode, Customizer → Colors & Fonts → Typography → Base Font → arrow: the box computes `background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255)` with the checkerboard over it, and the sample text is readable; a heading font without a colour shows dark text, not the panel's light text. Light mode unchanged.
