body:
## Task


Ship translation files with this release so a site whose WordPress locale is Dutch (`nl_BE`), German (`de_DE`) or French (`fr_CA`) shows every visitor-facing and admin string of this product in that language.

Owner decision 2026-11-01: sites run in their place's language, and use TranslatePress when they need more than one. Dutch and German sites are next; French follows.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Ship translation files with this release so a site whose WordPress locale is Dutch (`nl_BE`), German (`de_DE`) or French (`fr_CA`) shows every visitor-facing and admin string of this product in that language.

Owner decision 2026-11-01: sites run in their place's language, and use TranslatePress when they need more than one. Dutch and German sites are next; French follows.

## Why

The product declares its text domain and wraps strings, but ships no `.pot`, no translations and no `Domain Path` header (checked 2026-11-01), and it is not on wordpress.org, so WordPress cannot fetch a language pack for it.

## How

- Add `Domain Path: /languages` to the main file header and make sure the text domain is loaded for bundled files on the supported WordPress range (check the minimum WordPress version in the header; follow WordPress's just-in-time loading rules rather than loading early).
- Generate `languages/<text-domain>.pot` with `wp i18n make-pot`; add it to the build so it is refreshed each release.
- Add `nl_BE`, `de_DE` and `fr_CA` `.po` and `.mo` files. Block and script strings need `wp i18n make-json` files and `wp_set_script_translations()` for each registered script that has strings.
- Find strings that are not wrapped (visitor-facing output, block attributes' default text, emails, CLI output can stay English) and wrap them with the product's text domain.
- Translations must read naturally for the locale (Belgian Dutch, not Netherlands-only terms where they differ). Keep placeholders and HTML intact.

### Files Scope

- `languages/seoprostack.pot`
- `languages/seoprostack-nl_BE.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-de_DE.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-fr_CA.po`

A plugin-owned translation loader will register the PHP catalogue on init and supply bundled JSON fallback without editing shared starter files. The plugin-owned scripts/translations.sh will extract the POT and compile PO/MO/JSON catalogues. Compiled per-script JSON paths will be added when generated. No open PR touches these paths (the only open PR is #1133, site-template ownership). Verification: scripts/lint.sh, scripts/translations.sh, msgfmt --check and disposable-site locale switching on WordPress 6.2 and current WordPress.

title: Media in cloud storage: retry transient storage errors (500/503/SlowDown) instead of failing the upload or pausing removal for an hour
body:
## What

Media in cloud storage: retry transient storage errors (HTTP 500, 502, 503, 504, 429 and S3 `SlowDown`/`InternalError`) a few times with a short backoff before a request counts as failed.

## Why

Bulk imports on a Hostinger review copy (SEO Pro Directory resumable import jobs, wpallstars/seoprodirectory#334) hit single provider 500s twice in about five 120-row runs on 1 November 2026, with SEO Pro Stack 1.3.136:

- An upload got `Storage HTTP 500 (InternalError)`; the attachment was marked `failed` and the import job stopped ("Cloud upload failed; repair before resuming.").
- A removal check (`heads()` in `remove_local()`) got `Storage HTTP 500`. `local_step()` treats it as a service failure and sets `seoprostack_storage_local_wait` for an hour, so **every** local copy on the site stays on disk for an hour. A drain that waits on removal then exceeds its one-hour no-progress limit.

S3-compatible services document 500/503 as retryable; clients are expected to retry them. `includes/class-seoprostack-s3-client.php` has no retry: `request()`, `put_files()` and `heads()` return the first response.

## How

- `includes/class-seoprostack-s3-client.php`: in `request()` and in the concurrent paths (`put_files()`, `heads()`), retry a request whose status is 429 or 5xx, or whose S3 error code is `SlowDown`, `InternalError` or `ServiceUnavailable`, up to 3 attempts with jittered backoff (for example 0.5 s, 1.5 s). Honour the caller's `$deadline`: never sleep past it; return the last response when out of time. A PUT is idempotent here (same key and body), so retrying is safe; keep existing digest/size verification authoritative.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php` `local_step()` (around line 2538): after retries, a removal HEAD failure on one attachment should keep that attachment (`LOCAL` = `kept:` + signature, or a short per-attachment wait) rather than pausing removal for the whole site for `HOUR_IN_SECONDS`. Keep the site-wide pause for credential, configuration or repeated service errors.
- Reference pattern: the existing deadline handling in `remove_local()` (`storage_budget`) and `put_files()` byte/concurrency caps.

## Acceptance

- A mocked or real transient 500 on PUT or HEAD succeeds on retry without marking the attachment failed or setting `seoprostack_storage_local_wait`.
- Persistent 5xx still fails after the retry limit, with the same error messages as now.
- No retry sleeps beyond the batch deadline.
- `bash scripts/lint.sh` passes; README notes the retry behaviour under Media in cloud storage.

## Verification

Run a 100+ picture import on a temporary subsite of a review copy with Remove local copies on, and confirm `wp seoprostack media-storage status` (or `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::counts()`) ends with 0 failed and every local copy removed, and `seoprostack_storage_error` is empty.

title: Media in cloud storage: public per-attachment local-copy removal, so import slots do not all wait on the site-wide batch
body:
## What

Media in cloud storage: a public `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::remove_local_now($id, $deadline)` that removes one uploaded attachment's local copies under the same checks as the cron batch, so callers that upload a picture (SEO Pro Directory import jobs) can clear it themselves instead of waiting for the site-wide batch.

## Why

SEO Pro Directory resumable import jobs (wpallstars/seoprodirectory#334, GH#321) drain each part by waiting until its pictures have no local files. Local copies leave only through `local_copies()` in the cron batch: one site-wide lease, newest attachment first (`removable()` orders by ID descending), so a part's first picture is removed last.

Measured on a Hostinger review copy, 1 November 2026, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.136, 120 rows and 176 pictures:

- one slot: 1,216 s, every local copy removed;
- two slots: two parts in 965 s against 695 s for the same parts in one slot, slower, because both slots wait on the same removal batch.

The brief's target (two slots at least 1.6x one slot) cannot be met while removal is serial.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`: add `public static function remove_local_now($id, $deadline)` that takes the storage lease (`lease()`/`release()`, as `upload_attachment()` does), checks `local_mode()` is removing and the attachment is uploaded on this connection (`removal_record()`), then calls `remove_local($id, $deadline)` and maps its WP_Error the way `local_step()` does (attachment-only errors keep the attachment; service errors set `LOCAL_WAIT`). Return true, false (lease busy or not yet removable) or WP_Error.
- Keep every existing check: digest, HEAD confirmation, generation, `changed_meanwhile()`.
- Consider a per-attachment lease rather than the site-wide one, so two callers can remove different pictures at once; if the site-wide lease must stay, document that throughput stays serial.
- README: document the method under Media in cloud storage for plugins that upload pictures.

## Acceptance

- Calling it on an uploaded attachment removes its local copies, records `_seoprostack_storage_removed` and `_seoprostack_storage_local`, and the picture is served from the bucket.
- It refuses (returns false) while the attachment is not uploaded, removal is off, or the lease is held, and changes nothing.
- `bash scripts/lint.sh` passes.

## Verification

On a temporary subsite of a review copy, import 30+ listings with pictures, call the method for each picture from `wp eval`, and confirm `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::counts()` shows every local copy removed with 0 failed. Then SEO Pro Directory can call it from `drain_image()` (`includes/features/class-seoprodirectory-import-jobs.php`) and re-measure one against two slots.

Related: #1145 (retry transient storage errors).

title: Media in cloud storage waits forever on a watermark job whose cron event was lost
body:
## What happened

On an isolated regional review copy (SEO Pro Stack 1.3.136, `DISABLE_WP_CRON` with a host loop running `wp cron event run --due-now` every minute), Media in cloud storage stopped uploading for good after one new picture arrived.

- A WP-CLI script set the site icon (`site_icon` option, a new PNG attachment). `SEOProStack_Watermark_Images` started a one-picture `add` job (`seoprostack_watermark_job`: `ids` [the icon], `done` 0, `ended` 0).
- No `seoprostack_watermark_batch` event existed afterwards (`wp cron event list` showed only `seoprostack_media_storage_batch`). The likely cause is a WP-Cron race: the `wp cron event run --due-now` process in the loop loaded and saved the `cron` option around the CLI process that scheduled the watermark event, which lost the event.
- `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::run_batch()` returns early while `SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::job()` is unended (`if ($ready && $watermark && empty($watermark['ended'])) return 0;`), so every storage batch finished in about 0.01 s and uploads stayed at 52 of 489 until someone noticed.
- Running `SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::run_batch()` once by hand ended the job in a second, and the next storage batch uploaded 10 pictures again.

Region import jobs (`wp spd import job`) wait for their pictures to leave the host, so this silently stalls a whole regional import.

## Fix

In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php` `run_batch()` (and `media_storage status`), when the watermark job is unended and no `SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::HOOK` event is scheduled, schedule it again (or run one part, as the watermark batch takes the same media lease), instead of waiting forever. `SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::schedule()` (around line 2004 of `class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`) already does the scheduling. A watermark job with no progress for more than a few batch budgets should also show in `wp seoprostack media-storage status` as the reason uploads wait.

## Verify

On a test site with Media in cloud storage on and watermarks on: start a one-picture watermark job, delete its `seoprostack_watermark_batch` event (`wp cron event delete seoprostack_watermark_batch`), then run `wp cron event run seoprostack_media_storage_batch` twice. The watermark job ends and uploads continue; `status` names the stalled watermark job before that.

title: Media in cloud storage: --retry-failed uploads nothing while media jobs have work
body:
## What

`wp seoprostack media-storage upload --retry-failed` should upload the failed pictures it requeues, even while SEO Pro Stack's media jobs (watermark, next-gen conversion, originals) have work.

## Why

On a Hostinger review copy importing with SEO Pro Directory resumable jobs (2 November 2026, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.137), one upload failed with `Storage HTTP 500 (InternalError)` and the import job stopped ("Resolve failed media uploads before continuing the job."). Running `--retry-failed` twice reported `Success: Batch finished; remaining pictures continue in the background.` and left the attachment `failed`. Calling `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::upload_attachment( $id )` directly uploaded it on the first attempt in 5 seconds.

Cause, in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`:

- `cli()` (`--retry-failed`, around line 5121) requeues failed uploads (`retry_stranded()`, `queue()`), then loops `run_batch( $limit )` while it returns attempts.
- `run_batch()` (around line 2423) returns `0` before `upload_batch()` whenever `SEOProStack_Media_Jobs::run_batch()` did work. During an import, new pictures keep that queue busy, so the first batch returns 0 and the CLI loop ends with no upload attempted.

Cron has the same priority order, so a failed upload can wait a long time during a busy import, and every caller that relies on `--retry-failed` (the PSD import pump, runbooks) gets a false "success".

## How

- In the `--retry-failed` branch, after requeueing, upload the requeued attachments directly (`upload_attachment()` per ID, within the existing lease and a time budget), or pass a flag to `run_batch()` that skips the early return for media jobs on this call.
- Report how many were retried, uploaded and still failed, and exit non-zero (`WP_CLI::error`) when any requeued picture is still failed, so scripts can tell.
- Keep refusals (`collision_refused`, `removed_elsewhere()`) excluded, as now.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`

## Verification

- On a site with a busy media-jobs queue and one attachment in state `failed` (a transient 500), `wp seoprostack media-storage upload --retry-failed` leaves 0 failed and prints the counts.
- With a refusal present, the command reports it still failed and exits non-zero.
- `composer lint` / the plugin's PHP checks pass.

Related: #1145 (retry transient storage errors inside the client).

title: Language switcher feature: flag + code switcher beside Kadence dark-mode toggles (from PSD child theme)
body:
## What

A "Language switcher" feature in SEO Pro Stack: TranslatePress's languages as a compact flag + language-code button beside Kadence Pro's dark-mode toggle (top bar, mobile menu, footer), opening a list of the site's languages with flags and full names. It is the Property Services Directory child theme's switcher (`wpallstars/propertyservicesdirectory` `includes/class-psdtheme-languages.php`, `assets/css/languages.css`, `assets/js/languages.js`, 0.1.26–0.1.28) moved into the plugin, so sites on Kadence itself get the same one.

## Why

Owner review, 2 November 2026: the business templates (onepage/multipage, plain Kadence + Kadence Pro) show TranslatePress's own shortcode switcher, a wide box with the full language name, while the regional sites show the child theme's compact one: "the language selector style should match what i see on mission-viejo-us, which fits nicer". TranslatePress's markup has no language code, so CSS cannot turn one into the other. Sites made from the templates (client sites) need it too, and SEO Pro Stack is network-active on all of them.

Same review: in the footer the switcher sits below the toggle instead of to its right, because Kadence's `.footer-dark-mode-inner` is a block and the toggle's wrapper fills it. The owner wants it to the right of the toggle, with everything in that bottom footer row middle-aligned.

## How

- `NEW: includes/features/class-seoprostack-language-switcher.php`: modelled on `class-seoprostack-kadence-switch-palette.php` (bool setting, `content` tab, Kadence-only boot). Hooks `kadence_header_dark_mode`, `kadence_mobile_dark_mode`, `kadence_footer_dark_mode` at priority 20; renders only when TranslatePress publishes two or more languages. Steps aside when a theme already renders one (filter `seoprostack_language_switcher_active`, false to skip; the child theme returns false for its own until it defers).
- Flags: the theme's 27 3:2 SVGs in `assets/flags/`; any other locale falls back to TranslatePress's own `assets/flags/4x3/<locale>.svg`. English takes the site's country from `psdtheme_english_flag` (already set by the PSD setup script; JE on Jersey).
- `NEW: assets/css/language-switcher.css`, `assets/js/language-switcher.js`: the theme's files, plus the footer layout: `.footer-dark-mode-inner:has(> .seoprostack-languages)` as an inline flex row (toggle then switcher, centred vertically) and the bottom footer row holding it centred vertically (`.site-bottom-footer-inner-wrap:has(.seoprostack-languages) { align-items: center }`).
- Register in `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php` FEATURES after `SEOProStack_Translatepress_Colours`.

## Verification

On the onepage template (after the PSD setup script removes its TranslatePress shortcode items) and on a child-theme site: Playwright at 1440 and 390, light and dark; one switcher per place; the footer switcher right of the toggle and the bottom row's items centred; list opens upwards in the footer and mobile menu; `scripts/preflight-release.sh` clean; no new PHP log lines after install.

title: Translations for every published locale (es, it, pt, pl, ro, lv, et and country variants)
body:
## What

Bundle translations for every locale the multilingual sites publish, in addition to the existing `nl_BE`, `de_DE` and `fr_CA`: `fr_FR`, `fr_BE`, `es_ES`, `es_MX`, `it_IT`, `pt_PT`, `pt_BR`, `nl_NL`, `de_AT`, `de_CH`, `pl_PL`, `ro_RO`, `lv` and `et`.

## Why

Without a bundled translation for the page's locale, TranslatePress machine-translates the plugin's front-end strings one fragment at a time, without context, and picks the wrong sense of short labels. PR #1174 (issue #1171) corrected the German translation of `Terms` from "Bedingungen" (conditions) to "Begriffe" (taxonomy terms), which is right for the two taxonomy uses but now wrong for the licence link in the vulnerability report. Other locales have the same ambiguity: one translation must serve two meanings.

## How

1. In `includes/class-seoprostack-vulnerability-feed-report.php:216`, give the licence link its own context: `esc_html_x('Terms', 'licence terms link', 'seoprostack')`.
2. Add a `msgctxt "licence terms link"` / `msgid "Terms"` entry to each `languages/seoprostack-*.po` with the licence meaning (de_DE "Bedingungen", fr_CA/fr_FR/fr_BE "Conditions", nl_BE/nl_NL "Voorwaarden", and so on for every shipped locale), then recompile each `.mo` with `msgfmt --check --check-format`. No JSON change: the string is PHP-only.
3. Regenerate `languages/seoprostack.pot` the way the repo already does (see `DEVELOPMENT.md` for the translation commands) so the new context is in the template.

## Verification

- `msgfmt --check --check-format` passes for every changed PO; compiled MO files are reproducible.
- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- With a German site language, the vulnerability report's licence link reads "Bedingungen" and the Field content setting still reads "Begriffe".

### Files Scope

- `includes/class-seoprostack-vulnerability-feed-report.php`
- `languages/seoprostack.pot`
- `languages/seoprostack-*.po`
- `languages/seoprostack-*.mo`

title: Media in cloud storage: send several pictures together in a storage batch; far buckets drain 6-7 pictures a minute
body:
## What

Media in cloud storage uploads, and removes local copies of, one picture at a time inside a storage batch. Against a far bucket every picture then waits two to three round trips of about 2.2 s each, whatever its size. Let one batch send several pictures' requests together so that a draining import is bound by the number of pictures in flight, not by one picture's round trips.

## Evidence (a regional review copy, UK server to an R2 bucket near Perth, Australia, 1.3.143, 3 November 2026)

- Write latency probe using this plugin's S3 client: 18 PUTs of 40 KB as one concurrent group 2.24–2.32 s; as three groups of 6, 6.15–6.86 s. One round trip costs about 2.2 s however many files it carries.
- Sampling profile of one real `run_batch(25)` (26.0 s, 1,242 samples at 20 ms): 81% in `curl_multi_exec`, of which `put_files` 69% and `heads` (removal checks) 13%; single `WP_Http` requests 12%; `mysqli_query` 5.5%; `hash_file` under 1%.
- A batch moves about 4–5 uploads and 5–7 local-copy removals in its 25 s `BUDGET`. Drain rate over 33 minutes: 6–7 pictures a minute uploaded and as many removed, so a 1,213-picture import part takes about 3 hours to drain, against about 80 minutes to import its 661 rows.
- `run_batch()` clamps `$limit` to 10 (`min(10, (int) $limit)`), and `upload_batch()` calls `upload_attachment()` in sequence, so neither a larger limit nor the concurrency filter can raise throughput beyond one picture at a time.
- 28% of 400 recently uploaded pictures have 21–31 files, so at the default concurrency of 20 they pay two PUT rounds (the import driver on that site now sets the existing `seoprostack_media_storage_concurrency` filter to 32 as a stopgap).

## Suggested approach

Keep every per-picture safety rule in `upload_locked()` and `remove_local()` (durable attempted keys before PUT, collision rechecks, generation/`changed_meanwhile` checks, removal only after every HEAD confirms). Split each into a prepare phase (all database claims and checks), one shared network phase, and a finish phase per picture:

1. `upload_batch()`: prepare up to N waiting pictures (filterable, default about 5), send all their groups in one `request_multiple` call bounded by the concurrency and byte caps, then finish each picture with its own results. A failure stays scoped to its own picture, as now.
2. `local_copies()`: collect the removal files of up to N removable pictures and run one `heads()` call for all of them, then confirm and delete each picture whole as now.
3. Include the kept original's PUT (`retry_original()`, now a separate single request) in the same network phase.
4. Lift the `min(10, …)` clamp in `run_batch()` to a filterable cap.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`: `run_batch()` (about line 2395), `upload_batch()` (2477), `local_copies()` (2498), `remove_local()` (2735), `upload_locked()` (4137), `retry_original()`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-s3-client.php`: `put_files()` (119) and `heads()` (172) already take many keys; they may need to accept files from several attachments with per-key results.

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-s3-client.php`

## Verification

- `php -l` on the changed files and the repository's existing checks.
- On a site with a waiting queue and a far bucket: pictures uploaded and local copies removed per minute before and after, from `_seoprostack_storage_state` = `uploaded` and `_seoprostack_storage_local` counts sampled three minutes apart. Expect several times the current 6–7 a minute against a far bucket.
- `wp seoprostack media-storage status`: 0 failed, no mismatched or missing; sample public files of pictures from one batch answer 200 from the bucket and are gone locally.
- A picture whose upload fails in a shared batch is marked failed alone; the others in the batch finish.

title: Media in cloud storage: concurrent requests spin a CPU core while waiting (Requests has no curl_multi_select)
body:
## What

Every concurrent storage request group keeps a CPU core busy while it waits on the network. `SEOProStack_S3_Client::request_multiple_once()` uses `WpOrg\Requests\Requests::request_multiple()`, and WordPress's bundled transport (`wp-includes/Requests/src/Transport/Curl.php`, WordPress 7.1.4, lines 272–277) loops on `curl_multi_exec()` with no `curl_multi_select()` between calls, so the loop spins until the slowest response arrives.

## Evidence (a regional review copy with a far R2 bucket, 1.3.143, 3 November 2026)

- One real `run_batch(25)`: 27.1 s wall, 12.7 s user+system CPU, 2.3 s database (1,269 queries). A sampling profile of another batch put 81% of the time in `curl_multi_exec`, against a far bucket where one round trip takes about 2.2 s.
- A media-draining WP-CLI process uses about half a core all the time it drains; the shared host showed a load average of 17–19 while one regional import ran. Host load is what limits how many regional sites can import at the same time.

## Suggested approach

Run the S3 client's parallel requests on its own `curl_multi` loop that waits with `curl_multi_select($mh, $timeout)` (and a short `usleep` when it returns -1), keeping today's request building, signing, `complete` callback, timeouts, `max_bytes` and CA bundle. Optionally reuse one multi handle per batch so connections stay open between groups; measure whether that changes wall time to R2 (TLS ends at a nearby Cloudflare location, so the gain may be small).

## Files

- `includes/class-seoprostack-s3-client.php`: `request_multiple()` (201) and `request_multiple_once()` (235); the response shape callers expect from `put_files()` (119) and `heads()` (172) must stay the same.

### Files Scope

- `includes/class-seoprostack-s3-client.php`

## Verification

- `php -l` and the repository's existing checks.
- The same batch on a site with a waiting queue: CPU (user+system) per batch from `getrusage()` before and after, with wall time and uploads per batch unchanged or better. Expect CPU well under the 12.7 s of a 27 s batch.
- `wp seoprostack media-storage status` afterwards: 0 failed; sampled public files answer 200.

title: Media storage: a kept-original delete job for another originals connection stalls the originals pass
body:
## What happens

A kept-original **delete** job (`seoprostack_storage_job_original_<hash>` with `delete => true`) whose `record['original_signature']` belongs to another originals connection can never run: `original_client()` refuses it with `storage_original_config` ("Set the original private bucket connection again…"). Refusing is correct and must stay. But the originals pass in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php` (the loop around line 4095, `$result = self::delete_original($record)`) then sets `self::ERROR`, rewinds the cursor to the previous job and stops. So the same foreign job is retried first on every turn and blocks every originals job after it, and the storage status keeps showing the error.

## How sites get there

A whole-network copy of a site that still had delete jobs queued, which then gets its own private originals bucket. Seen on three copied stacks running 1.3.144: each had exactly 30 such jobs, all signed for the source site's originals connection, while the source site (whose own connection did run them) had none left. The same thing happens on one site when its originals connection is changed while deletes are queued.

## Expected

A delete job signed for a different originals connection is left out of the pass (not retried as an error). Its object lives behind the other connection and cannot be reached from here, so it must never be sent through the current client. Options:

- skip it like the "changed attachment's old inventory" branch (`continue`), and count it in `media-storage status` as e.g. `originals deletes for another connection: N`; and/or
- `wp seoprostack media-storage forget-foreign-deletes [--dry-run]` to remove them after the admin confirms the other connection no longer needs them.

Keep jobs whose signature matches, and jobs with no signature, unchanged.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`: the originals job loop (about lines 4090–4128), `original_client()` (about 3686), `delete_original()`, and the `media-storage status` output (about 5920).

## Verification

1. On a test site, add a delete job option whose `record['original_signature']` differs from `original_signature()`, ahead of a normal keep job.
2. Run `wp seoprostack media-storage upload --limit=10`: the normal job finishes, the cursor moves past the foreign job, no request is made through the current originals client for it, and `seoprostack_storage_error` is not set by it.
3. `wp seoprostack media-storage status` reports the foreign delete count.

Workaround used meanwhile: back up those exact options as JSON, then delete only the ones that are still foreign delete jobs.

title: feat: Keep pages cached: warm the page cache after purges (LiteSpeed Cache, WP-Optimize, multisite)
body:
## What

Keep pages cached after purges, so visitors (and the owner, during rapid development) stop getting uncached pages after every update.

Seen on the owner's LiteSpeed hosting (LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.2, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.144): after each plugin, theme or core update the whole cache is purged, and pages stay uncached until someone visits them.

## Why (evidence)

- LiteSpeed Cache's crawler, which the LiteSpeed Cache preset turns on daily (#588), starts again from the top after a Purge All only on its next full crawl: up to the crawl interval (1 day) later. `SEOProStack_Litespeed_Crawler::purged()` already detects this, but only offers a manual **Crawl now**.
- The preset leaves `purge-stale` (Serve Stale) off, so after a purge every first visitor waits for WordPress.
- Multisite subsites never get the crawler (preset `when` is `single_site`), and a daily crawl of dozens of subsites would be heavy anyway.
- WP-Optimize purges everything on `upgrader_overwrote_package`, theme switches, menus and the Customizer, but only preloads after its own Purge button (`WPO_Page_Cache::maybe_set_preload_cron_job()`), and its 3.7.0 update turned `auto_preload_purged_contents` off on existing sites.
- `SEOProStack_Page_Cache::after_update()` purges again on the first request after an SEO Pro Stack update, even when LiteSpeed Cache already purged for that same upgrade (`purge-upgrade` on), which can restart a warm-up that had already begun.

## How

New feature **Keep pages cached** (Speed tab, `keep_pages_cached`, on by default at the owner's request: it only requests the site's own pages, in WP-Cron, in small batches).

1. `presets/litespeed-cache.json`: add `litespeed.conf.purge-stale` = `"1"` (Serve Stale) with the same `when` as `cache` and a `settings` entry; update `notes`, `tested`.
2. `presets/wp-optimize.json`: add `wpo_cache_config.auto_preload_purged_contents` = `true` (its "Automatically preload content after it is purged" switch; saved through WP-Optimize's own code by `SEOProStack_WP_Optimize::save_through_plugin()`).
3. After a full purge (`litespeed_purged_all`, `wpo_cache_flush`), schedule one warm-up two minutes later (debounced, so several purges in an update run once):
   - LiteSpeed Cache with its crawler on: start it as **Crawl now** does (`\LiteSpeed\Task::async_call('crawler_force')`), reusing `SEOProStack_Litespeed_Crawler`.
   - WP-Optimize with its page cache on: its own `wpo_page_cache_run_preload` event, when its preload after purge or scheduled preload is on.
   - Otherwise (LiteSpeed without the crawler, multisite subsites): SEO Pro Stack requests a bounded list itself: home page, posts page, published pages and terms in the site's menus, and the newest published posts and pages, at most 60 addresses, 10 per cron run with a time budget, continuing every minute until done.
4. After a post is published or updated, warm that post, the home page and its first category page once its cache was purged (LiteSpeed Cache; WP-Optimize does this itself when its preload after purge is on).
5. Warm-up requests go straight to this server when LiteSpeed Cache's Server IP is set (CURLOPT_RESOLVE, as `reaches_server()` does), so a CDN in front does not answer or time out.
6. `SEOProStack_Page_Cache`: skip its own purge for a version when LiteSpeed Cache already purged for that upgrade (`upgrader_process_complete` for SEO Pro Stack with `purge-upgrade` on and LiteSpeed Cache loaded).

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php` (new), registered in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-page-cache.php`, `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed-crawler.php` (start method reusable)
- `presets/litespeed-cache.json`, `presets/wp-optimize.json`
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `AGENTS.md` (on by default), `uninstall.php` (queue option, cron hooks)

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh`.
- Throwaway LiteSpeed site: Purge All in LiteSpeed Cache, wait for cron, check `wp cron event list` and that the crawler summary restarted; `curl -sI` the home page shows `x-litespeed-cache: hit` without a manual visit.
- Multisite subsite: Purge All, run cron, home and menu pages answer `hit`.
- WP-Optimize site (not LiteSpeed): update a plugin, `wpo_page_cache_run_preload` is scheduled and pages are cached again.
- Debug log: no new messages mentioning `seoprostack`.

title: feat: Keep recommended settings: presets and changed defaults reach every site, hand changes kept
body:
## What

An opt-in **Keep recommended settings** switch, so a site (or every site of a network) keeps SEO Pro Stack's plugin presets and its own on-by-default features without anyone applying them by hand, and picks up changes to them in later SEO Pro Stack releases, while settings someone changes by hand stay as they set them.

## Why

The owner runs dozens of sites (single sites and multisite subsites on LiteSpeed hosting) and has no time to apply every preset and setting on each one, or again after each release. Today:

- Presets apply only when someone clicks Apply preset (Plugins screen) or runs `wp seoprostack presets apply`; a changed preset reaches nobody.
- A changed SEO Pro Stack default reaches new installs only (`STANDARDS.md` → Structure, #404), so features turned on by default since (#404, #806, #807, …) are off on older sites.

## How

Child setting of Plugin presets (Plugins tab): `plugin_presets_keep`, off by default (it writes other plugins' settings, so someone has to ask by switching it on; networks can apply it to every site from Network Admin).

- Runs in WP-Cron: after it is switched on, after each SEO Pro Stack update, after a plugin with a preset is activated, and daily.
- Presets: for every installed plugin with a preset, apply the settings that differ, through `SEOProStack_Presets::write()` (so each plugin's own save code, undo copy and `seoprostack_plugin_preset_changed` still run). Remembers, per setting path, the value it last wrote (`seoprostack_presets_kept`, not autoloaded). A setting whose stored value no longer matches what was written was changed by hand: it is left alone from then on. A preset value that changes in a later release is applied where the setting is still as last written.
- Settings visitors see are never applied automatically: a new preset key `manual` lists setting paths or option names (a path matches its children) that stay for Apply preset. Marked now, at the owner's choice: AI Engine's chatbot (`mwai_chatbots`, `mwai_options`), Turnstile on Fluent Forms (`cfturnstile_fluent`), Readabler's button and popup (`mdp_readabler_open_button_settings`, `mdp_readabler_modal_popup_settings`), Tutor LMS's course rules (`tutor_option` except `enable_gutenberg_course_edit`), Rank Math's page schema (`rank-math-options-titles.pt_page_default_rich_snippet`) and WooCommerce order attribution (`woocommerce_feature_order_attribution_enabled`).
- SEO Pro Stack's own settings: remembers each setting's default (`seoprostack_defaults_kept`). When a default changes in a release, a setting still at the old default gets the new one; one changed by hand keeps its value. On the first run, switches whose default is on but are off here are switched on (features that became on by default after the site was set up).
- WP-CLI: `wp seoprostack presets keep [--dry-run]` runs it now and lists what changed or would.

## Files

- `includes/class-seoprostack-presets-keep.php` (new), `includes/class-seoprostack-presets.php` (`manual` key in `validate()`; wanted values by path)
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-presets.php` (setting, cron hooks), `includes/class-seoprostack-presets-cli.php` (`keep` command)
- `presets/ai-engine.json`, `presets/simple-cloudflare-turnstile.json`, `presets/readabler.json`, `presets/tutor.json`, `presets/seo-by-rank-math.json`, `presets/woocommerce.json` (`manual`)
- `docs/presets.md` (`manual` key), `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `uninstall.php`

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh`; `scripts/preflight-release.sh` (preset checks).
- Throwaway site: install Antispam Bee and Readabler unconfigured, switch Keep on, run cron: `wp seoprostack presets diff antispam-bee` shows no differences, Readabler's analyzer settings applied and its button and popup unchanged. Change one Antispam Bee setting by hand, run again: it stays.
- Set an on-by-default feature off in `seoprostack_options`, delete `seoprostack_defaults_kept`, run: it is on. Turn it off again, run: it stays off.
- Debug log clean.

title: feat: Used CSS: each page's CSS in the page for Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Fluent Forms and block styles, on the site's own server
body:
## What

**Used CSS**: for Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Fluent Forms and WordPress's block styles only, put the CSS each page uses in the page and load those stylesheets without blocking the first paint. Everything works on the site's own server: no cloud service, no licence.

## Why (evidence)

A user (Kadence, Fluent Forms, Cloudways, WP-Optimize page cache) measured:

- FlyingPress 4 (removes unused CSS on the server): PageSpeed mobile 100, first paint 1.1 s.
- SEO Pro Stack + WP-Optimize: 87, first paint 2.7 s, TBT 0 ms, server response ~0.2 s. About 20 Kadence and Fluent Forms stylesheets block the first paint.
- Adding Debloat (free, removes unused CSS on the server): 100, first paint 1.3 s. He had to exclude whole Kadence header and Fluent Forms phone-field stylesheets (~45 KiB heavier) because JavaScript changes those parts after load.

FlyingPress 5 and LiteSpeed Cache now do this only through paid cloud services. The owner approved a narrow version (2026-11-04) where SEO Pro Stack can do better without supporting other themes and plugins: it amends the "no CSS and JS optimisation" rule in `AGENTS.md` for exactly these sources.

## How

New feature **Used CSS** (Speed tab, `used_css`, off by default until the owner turns it on by default).

- Front end only, GET, people not logged in, HTML responses; not for the Customizer, previews, feeds, REST, AMP or pages listed under Troubleshooting.
- Output buffer: for each `<link rel="stylesheet">` whose file is local and comes from the Kadence theme, Kadence Blocks (Pro), Fluent Forms (Pro) or `wp-includes/css/dist/block-library/`, put a `<style>` with the rules this page can use in its place, and keep the link right after it, loaded without blocking (`media="print"` switched back on load, with a `<noscript>` copy). Rules stay in their stylesheet's place, so the cascade is the same as before; once the full files load, every rule applies again, as before.
- A rule is used when every class, ID and element its selector needs is in the page (as Debloat checks, not full selector matching; pseudo-classes, attribute selectors and `:not()`/`:is()`/`:where()`/`:has()` contents are not required). Classes that Kadence and Fluent Forms scripts add after load (menu toggles, drawers, sticky header, tabs, accordions, the phone field's `iti`, Choices, flatpickr, error states) count as present, so those parts look right before the full files arrive. `@font-face`, `@keyframes`, `@import`, `:root` and `html`/`body` rules are kept; `@media`/`@supports` are filtered inside.
- `url()` paths are rewritten to absolute, as the CSS moves into the page.
- Each stylesheet is parsed once per version (path, size and modified time) into a cache file under `uploads/seoprostack/used-css/`, so a page costs only the matching. Old cache files are removed; uninstall removes the folder.
- Switching the feature on or off, or changing its bypass lists, purges the page cache (LiteSpeed Cache, WP-Optimize) through `SEOProStack_Page_Cache`, so cached pages rebuild; Keep pages cached warms them again.
- Troubleshooting bypasses: pages to leave alone, and stylesheets to keep whole (handle or file name).

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-used-css.php` (new), registered in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-page-cache.php` (public purge of all pages)
- `AGENTS.md` (amend the CSS rule), `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `uninstall.php`

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh`; `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (time per page with the feature on).
- Kadence test site with Kadence Blocks and a Fluent form with a phone field: PageSpeed mobile before and after; screenshots in light and dark mode identical before and after, with the menu, mobile drawer, sticky header and phone field opened.
- View source: no Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Fluent Forms or block-library stylesheet blocks rendering; inline `<style>` sizes are a fraction of the files.
- Debug log clean.

title: Media in cloud storage: uploads stop while a watermark job is open, and imports keep it open; mark, convert and upload in parallel
body:
## What

While a watermark job is open, Media in cloud storage uploads nothing, and during a directory import the job never closes: each imported picture joins it. Uploads then wait for the whole import, local copies pile up, and the import's own safety stops (upload disk-growth budget, one-hour drain limit) end it. Separately, WebP/AVIF conversion converts the newest pictures before they are marked, and marking rewrites their files, so each is converted twice.

Make the three stages (mark, convert, upload) work on different pictures at the same time, and let marking use more than one worker per site.

## Evidence (two regional review copies, UK server to UK R2 buckets, 1.3.144, 4 November 2026)

- An import job (`wp spd import job`, `--parallel=2` on one site, `--parallel=1` on the other) driven by WP-CLI, cron off. The media process loops the watermark batch, the WebP/AVIF batch, then `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::run_batch(25)`.
- Over five minutes (02:40 to 02:45Z) on the first site: `media-storage status` "uploaded" stayed at 169 while "waiting" rose from 1,965 to 2,131; "Uploads wait for watermark job add" moved from 141/328 to 161/360 (the job grows as pictures are imported). The import added about 50 pictures a minute.
- Each media cycle took about 42 s: about 20 s in the watermark part (`BUDGET` 20), about 20 s converting (`BUDGET` 20), and the storage batch returned at once. That is 20 pictures marked in about 147 s, about 7 s a picture, so marking gives about 4 pictures a minute per site.
- WebP/AVIF "waiting" rose from 1,163 to 1,216 on the same site: conversion runs newest first (`SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::waiting()`, `ORDER BY p.ID DESC`), so it takes pictures still queued for marking.

## Why (code, 1.3.144)

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php` `run_batch()` (about line 2406): `if ($ready && $watermark && empty($watermark['ended'])) { ...; return 0; }`. The whole batch stops while any watermark job is open, although `waiting()` (about line 2249) already skips each picture still queued for marking (`SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::mark_queued()` / `remark_pending`).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php` `run_batch()` (about line 2094): one part at a time per site (`self::LOCK`), holding the media storage lease (`SEOProStack_Media_Storage::lease()`) for the whole 20 s part, so one picture is marked at a time per site.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php` `run_batch()` / `waiting()` (about lines 889 and 943): no check for pictures queued for marking; a copy older than its source is made again (`filemtime`, about line 557).

## How

1. Storage batch: while a watermark job is open, keep giving it its bounded turn (the lost-wake-up guard for #1147), then go on with uploads of pictures that are not queued for marking, under the same lease, instead of returning 0. The per-picture skip in `waiting()` stays the guard.
2. Conversion: skip pictures still queued for marking (in `waiting()`, or before `convert_attachment()` in `run_batch()`), so each picture is converted once, after its mark.
3. Marking: let several runners mark different pictures at once (a per-picture claim, such as an atomic `add_post_meta(..., true)` or an `UPDATE ... WHERE` claim, instead of one site lock), and hold the storage lease only around the steps that need it (bringing files back, writing the record), not the whole part. Profile one `apply()` first: about 7 s a picture, with 21-31 files per picture on these sites, so check which sizes are marked and re-encoded.
4. Keep every existing guard: a picture's clean sizes are never uploaded or published, and a stopped PHP leaves no picture half marked.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`
- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`
- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`

## Verification

- On a site with Watermark pictures and Media in cloud storage on, import pictures continuously (a running `wp spd import job`, or repeated `wp media import`) and drive the batches from WP-CLI with cron off. "uploaded" in `wp seoprostack media-storage status` must rise while "Uploads wait for watermark job add" is shown; no picture without its mark reaches the bucket (spot-check object keys against the watermark record); each picture's `_seoprostack_nextgen_done` is set once.
- With two marking runners on one site, the marked-a-minute rate roughly doubles and no picture is marked twice (watermark record `done` count equals the number of pictures).
- PHPUnit and PHPStan as configured in this repository.

## Context

title: Keep pages cached on large networks: plan fills in steps, per-subsite Server IP
body:
## What

Keep pages cached (#1192, PR #1195) on large networks: plan a network-wide fill in steps across batches, past the 1,000-page queue cap, and open each subsite's pages through that subsite's own LiteSpeed Server IP.

## Why

CodeRabbit's review of PR #1195 found three limits that only matter on networks with many sites or several origins (single sites and small networks are unaffected, so they were left out of #1195):

- `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Pages::to_open(true)` (network) walks up to `NETWORK_SITES` sites in one go, before the batch's 20-second budget is checked. On a big network, planning alone can use the whole batch, and as the queue stays marked `full`, the next batch plans again from the start.
- The queue keeps at most `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Pages::MAX` (1,000) addresses and keeps no position, so with about 25 pages per site, sites after roughly the 40th never get pages opened after a network purge.
- `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::resolver()` reads LiteSpeed Cache's `server_ip` on the site running the batch, not the site owning each address, so a subsite on another origin is sent to the wrong server.

## How

- Store the next site ID in the queue (`SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue`, option `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_queue`) while planning a network fill; plan sites until the batch budget is spent, keep `full` set with the position, and continue from it in the next batch. Clear the position when a new network purge arrives (start again from the first site).
- Open addresses in queue order, and only plan the next sites when fewer than `MAX` are waiting, so every site is reached.
- Keep each queued address's blog ID next to it (network fills only), and resolve `server_ip` (and the page cache check) inside `switch_to_blog()` for that blog; restore afterwards.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php` (position, per-address blog)
- `EDIT: includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php` (`to_open()` / network planning in steps)
- `EDIT: includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php` (`resolver()` per blog)
- `EDIT: includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php` (`run()` passes the budget to planning)
- `EDIT: README.md`, `EDIT: changelog.txt`

### Files Scope

- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php`
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`

## Reference

- Review threads on PR #1195 (comments on `run()`/`network_pages()`, the queue cap, and `resolver()`).
- Batch budget pattern: `SEOProStack_Feature::more_time()` as used in `SEOProStack_Keep_Pages_Cached::run()`.

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh phpcs phpstan`.
- `scripts/test-site.sh up --multisite`, create 60 sites (`wp site create`), turn on WP-Optimize's page cache network-wide, purge, then run `wp cron event run seoprostack_keep_pages_cached` repeatedly: every site's home page is opened (check `wp option get seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_queue` as it advances), no batch exceeds about 20 seconds, and `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_last` records the total.
- Debug log clean.

title: perf: set the AVIF encoder speed for next-gen copies (JPEG sources encode at libheif's default 6, not WordPress's 7)
body:
## Problem

Next-gen copies made from JPEG/PNG/WebP sources are encoded as AVIF at libheif's default speed (6), not the speed WordPress intends (7).

`WP_Image_Editor_Imagick::set_quality()` (WordPress 7.1.4, `wp-includes/class-wp-image-editor-imagick.php`, `case 'image/avif'`) sets `heic:speed 7` only when `$this->mime_type` is `image/avif`, the type of the picture the editor *opened*. `SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`, the `wp_get_image_editor($path, array('output_mime_type' => $mime))` / `$editor->save($temp, $mime)` block) opens the JPEG, so that branch never runs, and `_save()` only changes the format.

## Evidence (Hostinger shared host, ImageMagick 7.1.2-34, quality 60, 4 November 2026)

Per picture (original plus core sizes), AVIF was about 88% of conversion time: WebP 0.47-0.67 s, AVIF 3.66-5.20 s.

Full-size encodes, compared with the source JPEG:

| heic:speed | Time | Size | PSNR |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (= 6) | 0.57-0.96 s | 29-115 KB | 25.14-27.74 dB |
| 7 | 0.32-0.38 s | 27-111 KB | 25.00-27.62 dB |
| 8 | 0.16-0.31 s | 46-178 KB (erratic) | 24.82-27.47 dB |
| 9 | 0.07-0.10 s | 31-112 KB | 24.95-27.40 dB |

The default and speed 6 produced byte-identical files. With speed 7 set for every AVIF write (a site-level editor subclass as a stop-gap), three sites importing directory pictures went from a growing conversion queue to one falling by about 95 pictures a minute in total. That matters because the storage batch keeps local copies while any picture waits for conversion.

## Proposed change

In `SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images`, before `$editor->save()` for AVIF, set the encoder speed. `WP_Image_Editor_Imagick` keeps `$image` protected, so either:

- use a small `WP_Image_Editor_Imagick` subclass, chosen through `wp_image_editors`, whose `_save()` calls `$this->image->setOption('heic:speed', ...)` when `get_output_format()` returns `image/avif`; or
- convert with `Imagick` directly for the AVIF branch when Imagick is the chosen editor.

Default the speed to 7, matching WordPress, and expose it through a filter such as `seoprostack_nextgen_avif_speed` (0-9). A setting is optional. Keep the speed out of `quality_key()` so existing copies are not made again. GD (`imageavif()`) takes a speed argument too (default 6), so the GD path can use the same value.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`
- ADD: `includes/image-editors/class-seoprostack-nextgen-imagick.php`
- ADD: `includes/image-editors/class-seoprostack-nextgen-gd.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`
- EDIT: `readme.txt`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`

## Verification

- Convert one JPEG through the plugin's path with the filter at 7 and at 6: speed 7 is several times faster and its output differs from speed 6's.
- On a site with a conversion queue, `SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::waiting()` falls faster than before.
- Existing copies keep their records (no re-conversion).

Once released, the stop-gap mu-plugin can be removed. WordPress core's own limitation (speed only when the source is AVIF) could be reported upstream separately.

title: Keep pages cached: get past LiteSpeed's bot protection (crawler user agent), deliver waiting purges, back off when refused
body:
## What happens

Production testing of Keep pages cached (#1192, 1.3.145) on Hostinger (LiteSpeed, Cloudflare in front) found two failures when the host's LiteSpeed bot protection is active:

1. **Fill requests are challenged.** For pages that are not cached, LiteSpeed answers requests from the site's own server with its reCAPTCHA page ("Bot Verification", HTTP 403), so the fill gets 403 for every page it should fill (seen on `wp seoprostack keep-cached` for a whole site). Each failed challenge also counts towards the server's limit, after which the server's own address gets a plain LiteSpeed `403 Forbidden` for a while, even for cached pages.
2. **Purges from WP-CLI and cron wait.** LiteSpeed Cache stores a purge made from the command line (WP-CLI, or a host cron job that runs `php wp-cron.php`) and, as the run ends, opens `admin-ajax.php` so the server applies it (`\LiteSpeed\Core::kick_purge_queue()`). That request goes with WordPress's user agent and gets the same 403, so the purge waits for the next visitor who reaches PHP. Keep pages cached's batch, 90 seconds later, then opens pages that are still in the cache (`hit`), and the cache empties afterwards with nothing filling it. Seen: `do_action('litespeed_purge_all')` in WP-CLI left `litespeed.purge.queue` = `X-LiteSpeed-Purge: public,6f9_` and the kick answered 403; the home page stayed at its earlier cached copy until a later run delivered it.

Requests whose user agent starts with `lscache_runner` (LiteSpeed Cache's crawler, `\LiteSpeed\Crawler::FAST_USER_AGENT`) are let through: from the same client, a page that is not cached answered 404 (WordPress) with `lscache_runner …` and 403 with a browser user agent. LiteSpeed Cache already treats that user agent as its crawler (`\LiteSpeed\Vary::can_change_vary()` leaves the vary alone), which is what a fill wants.

## Change

- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php`: on a LiteSpeed page cache, user agents start with `lscache_runner ` as LiteSpeed Cache's crawler does (desktop and phone; the phone one still matches the mobile vary rule). If the server answers 428 (host turned the crawler off), open the page again with the plain user agent.
- Same file: say whether an answer means the server refused for now (403, 429, 503).
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php` `run()`: on a LiteSpeed page cache, deliver a waiting purge first; stop the batch at the first refused page and try again later, so the fill neither opens pages before the purge reaches the cache nor keeps failing challenges.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php` `done()`: count batches stopped in a row and wait longer each time (1, 2, 3… minutes); give up after five and leave the rest to LiteSpeed Cache's crawler.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-page-cache.php`: from the command line, at the end of the run, if LiteSpeed Cache's purge is still waiting (its kick was refused), open `admin-ajax.php` again as LiteSpeed Cache's crawler. Read the queue options from the database, not the object cache, since the kick runs in another request.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed-crawler.php` `reaches_server()`: send the same crawler user agent, so the Server IP check is not refused by the protection.

## Verification

- `composer lint` / `php -l` on the changed files; `scripts/preflight.sh` as usual for a release.
- On a Hostinger site: `wp eval 'do_action("litespeed_purge_all");'` then `wp option get litespeed.purge.queue` gives `-1` and the home page is a `miss` then `hit` with a new "Page cached by LiteSpeed Cache … on" time; `wp seoprostack keep-cached` lists `200 miss`/`200 hit` (or `404`), not `403`.
- With the protection active (curl with a browser user agent to an uncached address answers 403 "Bot Verification"), the fill's requests still answer 200.

Files: the five above. Reference pattern: LiteSpeed Cache's own crawler (`src/crawler.cls.php` `_get_curl_options()`, `src/core.cls.php` `kick_purge_queue()`).

title: perf: watermark run_batch() gives up whenever the media lease is busy, so the background job never catches up during bulk uploads
body:
## Problem

Under sustained media work, the background watermark job falls behind new uploads and never ends. Next-gen conversion and local-copy removal both wait for it, so they stall too.

- `SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::after_generate()` queues a new upload for the background job (`queue('add', ...)`) whenever `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::lease()` is busy.
- `SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::run_batch()` takes the lease with `lease()`, which does not wait, and returns at once when another request holds it.

With several processes uploading (storage batches, import-job drains), the lease is held most of the time, so most new uploads are queued *and* most watermark turns do nothing. On a regional import (4 November 2026, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.145), one site's job marked about 8 pictures a minute while about 10 were imported: 316 of 700 after 40 minutes. A site-side change that made the batch wait for the lease (`lease_wait()`, then `run_batch()`, which re-enters the held lease) and run back-to-back finished the remaining 394 in about 4 minutes.

## Proposed change

In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php` `run_batch()`, take the lease with `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::lease_wait()` (it already bounds the wait: 60 s in WP-CLI/cron, 5 s for page requests) instead of `lease()`. When a job is open and work remains, reschedule the next batch immediately rather than at the normal interval, until the job ends.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`

## Verification

- With a storage batch holding the lease in another process, `wp eval 'SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::run_batch();'` waits and marks pictures instead of returning with `done` unchanged.
- During a bulk import with three upload processes, the watermark job's `done` keeps pace with `total` and the job ends.

title: LiteSpeed: a command-line purge is lost when the delivery request times out on a busy server
body:
## What happens

On a busy LiteSpeed server, a purge made from the command line (WP-CLI, or WP-Cron run by a host's cron job) can be lost: LiteSpeed Cache's queue is emptied, but cached pages stay as they were.

LiteSpeed Cache stores a command-line purge in its queue options (`litespeed.purge.queue`, `litespeed.purge.queue2`). The first web request that loads PHP takes it, sets the queue to `-1` and sends the purge as a response header (`LiteSpeed\Core::__construct()`). `wp litespeed-purge all` opens `admin-ajax.php` for that (`Core::kick_purge_queue()`, `wp_safe_remote_get()` with WordPress's 5-second timeout). When the server takes longer than that to answer, the request has already emptied the queue, but the client has gone, so the server never applies the purge header.

SEO Pro Stack 1.3.146 (#1202) delivers a purge that is still waiting at the end of a command-line run (`SEOProStack_Litespeed::deliver_purge()`), but here nothing is waiting any more, so it does nothing.

## Evidence (Hostinger, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.2, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.146, load average 16 to 18)

Probe: store a purge all with `LiteSpeed\Purge::purge_all()` from WP-CLI, deliver it once, then check the home page's `x-litespeed-cache` (SEO Pro Stack's shutdown delivery removed for the probe):

| Delivery | Answer | Queue after | Home page after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wp_safe_remote_get()`, 5 s (LiteSpeed's own) | `cURL error 28` after 5.02 s, 0 bytes | `-1` | `hit` (purge lost) |
| `wp_safe_remote_get()`, 30 s | `400` after 5.59 s | `-1` | `miss` |
| crawler user agent, 10 s | `400` after 0.60 s | `-1` | `miss` |

`admin-ajax.php` timed from the same server took 0.4 to 6.3 s for both user agents (busy shared server), so the cause is the timeout, not the user agent. `wp litespeed-purge all` answered `Error: Could not notify the web server to purge.` three times out of four, and each time the page stayed cached with the old content.

## Change

In `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php` (command line, LiteSpeed server only):

1. Remember each purge LiteSpeed Cache stores during the run (`add_option_` / `update_option_` hooks for the two queue options).
2. Give the request that delivers it (`admin-ajax.php`) a longer timeout (`http_request_args`), so LiteSpeed Cache's own delivery waits for a busy server.
3. Count a purge as delivered only when a request to `admin-ajax.php` got an answer (`http_api_debug`, a status below 500). When the queue is empty but no request got an answer, store the purge again and deliver it as the crawler (`deliver_purge()`), which Keep pages cached and `wp seoprostack keep-cached` already call.

Store the purge again through `update_option()` after dropping this process's cached copy of the option, so a persistent object cache stays right.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- On a LiteSpeed site: `wp litespeed-purge all` succeeds and the home page answers `x-litespeed-cache: miss` straight after; with LiteSpeed's timeout forced short (a 0.01 s `http_request_args` filter at a later priority in a probe), the purge is still delivered at the end of the run.
- A purge from a web request (the admin's Purge All) is unchanged: nothing here runs outside the command line.

Ref #1202

title: bug: a busy kept original (storage_original_busy) pauses local-copy removal for the whole site for an hour
body:
## Problem

A momentary lock conflict on one picture's kept original pauses local-copy removal for the **whole site for an hour**.

`SEOProStack_Media_Storage::local_result()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`) sets `LOCAL_WAIT` to `time() + HOUR_IN_SECONDS` for any removal error that `SEOProStack_S3_Client::retryable()` does not accept, and `retryable()` accepts only `storage_http` errors with `retryable` data. `storage_original_busy` ("The kept original is in use by another request. Try again shortly.", returned near lines 3659 and 3832 in 1.3.145) is a transient lock conflict, not a service failure, but it falls through to the hour-long pause.

Seen on a regional import, 4 November 2026 08:51: the error paused removal, `remove_local_now()` returned false for every picture, and both draining import parts stopped one picture short with an empty conversion queue until the pause was lifted by hand. After `delete_option('seoprostack_storage_local_wait')`, the same picture was removed at once.

## Proposed change

In `local_result()`, treat `storage_original_busy` like a per-attachment retry: leave that attachment's files local for the next pass (do not mark it `kept:`, so it is revisited) and return `true` so the batch goes on, without setting `LOCAL_WAIT`. Optionally cap consecutive busy results per request, as `$service_failures` does for HTTP errors.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`

## Verification

- Hold the kept-original lock for one attachment in one request and run a removal pass in another: the pass skips that attachment, `seoprostack_storage_local_wait` stays unset, and the next pass removes it.
- Existing removal and restore behaviour is unchanged for real service failures (non-retryable HTTP errors still pause).
- A site-side stop-gap in the import pump lifts this pause only when this message caused it. It can go once this is released.

title: Speed: load Fluent Forms' Turnstile when a form comes near, not with the page
body:
## What happens

On a page with a Fluent Forms form that has Cloudflare Turnstile, Fluent Forms loads Turnstile's `api.js` on every page load and renders each widget right away, even when the form is far down the page or in a closed modal. Each widget loads a Cloudflare challenge document of about 213 KB, plus `api.js` (about 28 KB), all competing with the first screen.

Evidence, pilot site (Kadence, Kadence Blocks, Fluent Forms 6.2.17, LiteSpeed), PageSpeed mobile, home page with two forms (IDs 3 and 7, both with Turnstile) below the first screen:

| Run | Turnstile bytes before LCP | Lighthouse LCP |
|---|---|---|
| before #1204 | 482 KB | 8.7 s |
| #1204, run 1 | 453 KB | 6.5 s |
| #1204, run 2 | 28 KB | 5.8 s |
| #1204 + eager change | 243 KB | 6.5 s |

The observed LCP was about 1.0–1.2 s in every run. Lighthouse's simulated LCP charges every byte that started before it, and Turnstile is the largest share left after #1204 (the hero picture is already a preloaded 235 KB AVIF).

## How Fluent Forms loads it (6.2.17)

- `fluentform/app/Services/FormBuilder/Components/Turnstile.php`: when a form with Turnstile renders, it enqueues the script handle `turnstile` (`https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js?render=explicit`, in the footer, `data-cfasync="false"`), and prints `<div class="ff-el-turnstile cf-turnstile" id="fluentform-turnstile-{form}-{instance}" data-sitekey=…>`.
- `fluentform/assets/js/form-submission.js`: on form init, if `window.turnstile` exists, `turnstile.ready()` renders each `.ff-el-turnstile.cf-turnstile`. The form also binds `fluentform_first_interaction` with `.on()`, which runs the same render; it fires once on the first focus of a field. Rendering skips a widget that already has a token. On `lity:open` it calls `turnstile.remove()` and renders again.

## Change

A Speed-tab feature in SEO Pro Stack (new `includes/features/class-seoprostack-…php`, registered like the other features; see `STANDARDS.md` → Structure). Fluent Forms only, following the owner's scope rule (`AGENTS.md` → Features).

title: perf: mark new uploads inline behind the QUEUED_META barrier instead of queueing whenever the media lease is busy
body:
## Problem

During a bulk import, almost every new picture goes to the background watermark job instead of being marked when it is made, and next-gen conversion and storage uploads wait for that job. So the site's whole media pipeline runs at the pace of a single lease-serialised marker.

`SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::after_generate()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`, 1.3.145) calls `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::lease()`. When another process holds the storage lease, it sets `QUEUED_META` as a barrier and calls `queue('add', ...)`. With import slots, a storage batch and drains on one site, the lease is held nearly all the time. It already has a path that marks a new upload without the lease (`after_generate_locked(..., true)`, "a new upload no batch can take") but uses it only when queueing fails.

Measured on a regional import, 4 November 2026 (South Hampshire, three slots):

- One `run_batch()` turn: 11 s waiting for the lease, then 22 s marking 18 pictures (about 1.2 s each). Meanwhile the job's total rose from 473 to 517 as new uploads were queued.
- While the job is open, the import pump's converter makes no WebP/AVIF copies (converting before marking is wasted: marking rewrites the files). One draining part then had 729 of 904 pictures unconverted and 691 not uploaded, and its slot imported nothing (see wpallstars/seoprodirectory#403).
- The account used 277% of 600% CPU: the work is serialised, not CPU-bound.

## Proposed change

For a new upload (`'create' === $context`, no watermark record, `watermark_images_new` on), always set the `QUEUED_META` barrier and mark inline with `after_generate_locked($metadata, $attachment_id, $context, true)` instead of queueing. The barrier already keeps a running storage batch from taking the picture mid-mark. Clear the barrier when marking finishes, as the queued path does. Keep the queue for `'update'` contexts and refreshes, which may touch files a batch owns.

This moves marking into the importing processes, which run in parallel, and leaves the background job for real backlogs.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`

## Verification

- With a storage batch holding the lease in another process, `wp media import <file>` produces a marked picture immediately (record present, `QUEUED_META` cleared) and no watermark job is opened.
- During a bulk import with three slots, `SEOProStack_Watermark_Images::job()` stays ended (or empty) and conversion keeps running.
- A storage batch running at the same time never uploads a picture whose `QUEUED_META` barrier is set (existing behaviour).
- Related: #1206 (run_batch lease wait) still applies to real backlogs.

title: Used CSS: Kadence's local fonts stylesheet and Kadence Pro's dark-mode script still hold up the first paint
body:
## What happens

With **Load the CSS each page uses first** (Used CSS, #1194) on, a Kadence site still has render-blocking requests that Used CSS leaves alone, and the first paint waits for the slowest of them. PageSpeed Insights (mobile, Lighthouse `render-blocking-insight`) on a live Kadence + Kadence Pro + Kadence Blocks pilot running 1.3.148, estimated saving 400 ms on FCP:

| File | Size | From | Handled here |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wp-content/fonts/<hash>.css` (handle `kadence-fonts-gfonts`) | 2 KB | Kadence theme, Load Google Fonts locally | this issue |
| `wp-content/plugins/kadence-pro/dist/dark-mode/dark-mode.min.js` (handle `kadence-dark-mode`) | 2 KB | Kadence Pro dark mode, in the head, not deferred | this issue |
| SEO Pro Cookie Consent's `spcc.css` | 5 KB | that plugin | its own issue |
| the child theme's `assets/css/theme.css` | 4 KB | child theme | its own starter's issue |

They load in parallel, so the saving only comes once all four are gone; this issue covers the two that belong to the stack SEO Pro Stack supports.

Why Used CSS misses them:

- The Kadence theme prints its local Google Fonts stylesheet itself, at `wp_head` priority 89 (`inc/components/styles/component.php`, `frontend_gfonts()` → `frontend_gfonts_logic()`: `wp_register_style('kadence-fonts-' . $gfonts_type, …)` then `wp_print_styles()`), from `WP_CONTENT_DIR . '/fonts/'`, which is outside the folders `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Links::sources()` handles (block library, `PLUGINS`, the parent theme's folder). Core's own inlining (`wp_maybe_inline_styles()`, `wp_head` priority 1) has already run by then, so `wp_style_add_data(..., 'path', ...)` cannot reach it.
- Kadence Pro enqueues `kadence-dark-mode` in the head on purpose (`dist/dark-mode.php`, `wp_enqueue_script('kadence-dark-mode', KTP_URL . 'dist/dark-mode/dark-mode.min.js', array(), KTP_VERSION, false)` plus `wp_localize_script`), so the colour scheme is set before the first paint. It must stay synchronous; it can be in the page instead of a request. The file does not use `document.currentScript`.

## Change

Owner's scope (#1194): only the Kadence theme and Kadence Pro, nothing wider.

1. Used CSS also handles the Kadence theme's local fonts stylesheet: a link whose handle is `kadence-fonts-gfonts` (or another `kadence-fonts-*` the theme prints) and whose file is under `WP_CONTENT_DIR/fonts/`, only while the Kadence theme is the parent (`SEOProStack_Used_Css::kadence_theme()`). `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Parser` always keeps `@font-face`, so the whole file goes into the page and the link loads without blocking, as for the other handled sheets. Prefer matching that one handle and folder in `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Links` over adding the whole `fonts/` folder to `sources()`, which other themes' font loaders share.
2. While Used CSS is on, for the same visitors and pages it handles, Kadence Pro's `kadence-dark-mode` script is printed with its file's contents in the page instead of `src`, keeping its `id`, its position after its `-js-extra` data, and no `async`/`defer`: for example a `script_loader_tag` filter for that handle that reads the local file (only when it maps to a readable file under `WP_PLUGIN_DIR/kadence-pro/`, and only up to a small size such as 8 KB). Steps aside when `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Policy` steps aside (a content security policy that blocks inline code), as Used CSS does.
3. Docs: the Used CSS description in `settings()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-used-css.php`), its file header, README.md → Features and `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- `composer` lint/PHPStan/PHPCS checks the repo runs in CI, and Plugin Check (`DEVELOPMENT.md`), pass.
- Test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`) with the Kadence theme (Load Google Fonts locally on), Kadence Pro dark mode on and Used CSS on, as a visitor: the page has no `<link>` to `wp-content/fonts/…css` that blocks (only the non-blocking one) and no `<script src=…dark-mode.min.js>`; the fonts still load and the dark-mode toggle still works, with no flash of the light scheme when the browser prefers dark (Playwright `colorScheme: 'dark'`: the dark palette is on `<html>` at first paint).
- Screenshots before and after on desktop and phone match.
- Logged-in visitors and pages Used CSS skips are unchanged.

### Files Scope

- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-links.php`
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-used-css.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-used-css-page.php` (only if the script is handled in the page rewrite instead of a filter)
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`

title: bug: inline marking (#1211) races the storage batch: the QUEUED_META barrier only holds while a watermark job is open
body:
## Problem

PR #1215 (#1211, released in 1.3.147/1.3.148) marks a new upload inline without the media lease and relies on the `QUEUED_META` barrier to keep the storage batch away. But the barrier is honoured only while a watermark job is open:

```php
// includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php, mark_queued()
$job = self::job();
if ($job && empty($job['ended']) && 'remove' !== $job['op']) {
    return true;
}
delete_post_meta((int) $id, self::QUEUED_META);
return false;
```

With no open job (the normal case once uploads are marked inline), a storage batch on another process that reaches the new upload sees `mark_queued()` return false, deletes the barrier, and copies the files while they are being marked. WordPress saves the attachment metadata after each sub-size (`wp_create_image_subsizes()`), so the batch can see the attachment before `wp_generate_attachment_metadata` runs.

Evidence (4 November 2026, before 1.3.147): a site-side hook doing the same unleased inline mark (see the correction comment on #1211) caused `storage_changed` failures ("The local picture changed while being copied. It will be retried.") on three importing stacks within 20 minutes. One stack's import job stopped three times on "Resolve failed media uploads before continuing the job". Waiting for the lease instead (`lease_wait()`, then the leased `after_generate_locked()`) stopped the failures. That site-side hook runs before the plugin's (priority 94), so the 1.3.148 path has not run on those stacks during imports. Ordinary uploads made while the lease is busy still take it.

## Proposed change

Either:

1. In `after_generate()` for a `'create'` upload, try `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::lease_wait()` before marking, and mark through the leased path. Fall back to `queue('add', ...)` only when the wait runs out. Or:
2. Make the barrier hold on its own: in `mark_queued()`, treat a `QUEUED_META` set within the last few minutes (for example `time() - $set < 300`) as a barrier whether or not a job is open, and only clear stale ones.

Option 1 matches what was measured to work; option 2 avoids the wait.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-watermark-images.php`

## Verification

- While a storage batch runs in another process (for example `wp seoprostack media-storage upload --limit=25` in a loop) and no watermark job is open, import 50 pictures with `wp media import`. No attachment ends with `_seoprostack_storage_state` = `failed` / `storage_changed`, and every one has a watermark record.
- Existing queued-job behaviour is unchanged for `'update'` contexts.

title: Image loading: the Kadence hero background comes at the size each screen needs, never less sharp
body:
## What happens

Image loading preloads the background picture of the Kadence Blocks row a page opens with (#1204), and every screen gets that picture at the size the row names, usually the full upload. On a live Kadence pilot (1.3.148) the home page's slider picture is the full 2048×1536 upload, 234 KB as AVIF, on phones too. It is the page's largest paint (LCP 5.1 s, PageSpeed mobile).

Measured with `background-size: cover` (painted width = the larger of the box's width and its height × the picture's width/height, times the device pixel ratio):

| Screen | Box (CSS px) | Pixels needed | Smallest copy that is enough |
|---|---|---|---|
| PageSpeed's phone (412 wide, DPR 1.75) | 412×369 | 861 | 1024×768, 34 KB AVIF |
| iPhone 15 (393 wide, DPR 3) | 393×422 | 1688 | the full one, as now |
| Desktop (1350 wide, DPR 1) | 1350×991 | 1350 | 1536×1152, 83 KB AVIF |

The row has no minimum height (its content and padding set it), so the server cannot know the box: only the browser can.

## Change (owner's decision: never less sharp than now)

For the row `kadence_preload()` already picks (first row, same background on every device), when its picture has smaller copies of the same proportions:

- The browser measures the row once it is parsed and takes the smallest copy at least as wide as the pixels it paints (10% headroom for fonts and late styles), else the picture as now. If the row later grows (fonts, rotation, a wider window), a larger copy replaces it; never a smaller one.
- Only `background-size: cover` and `contain`; anything else keeps the picture as now. Every slide of a background slider, each with its own picture's copies.
- The chosen copy is preloaded at high priority, as its AVIF or WebP copy when pages name copies (`SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::first_copy()`), and set as an inline background, with image-set() of its copies.
- Until then the row's background waits (a class on `<html>` hides it), so the full picture is not fetched as well. Without JavaScript, or if the scripts do not run, nothing is hidden and the picture loads as now.
- Copies come from the attachment's metadata (proportional sizes smaller than the one the row names), through Media in cloud storage's address mapping (`SEOProStack_Media_Storage::attachment_url()`) when it serves the picture, and only when the file is there.
- A `seoprostack_kadence_hero_sizes` filter turns it off.

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-image-loading.php` (`kadence_preload()`, a `render_block_kadence/rowlayout` filter after the row)
- `includes/class-seoprostack-kadence-hero.php` (new: copies, the head script and style)
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php` (a public helper for a background's CSS value)
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`

## Verification

- Repository lint, PHPStan, PHPCS and Plugin Check pass.
- Test site (`scripts/test-site.sh`), a page opening with a Kadence row with a 2048 px background slider, and one with a normal background; Playwright at 412×823 DPR 1.75, 393×852 DPR 3, 768×1024 DPR 2 and 1350×940 DPR 1: the requested copy is at least as wide as the pixels needed, the full picture is not requested when a copy was taken, and the background shows.
- JavaScript off: the full picture loads and shows, as before.
- Window widened after load: a larger copy (or the full picture) replaces the smaller one.
- Live pilot after deploy: PageSpeed mobile LCP and bytes before and after.
