title: Media storage: remove local copies of many pictures in one pass (remove_local_many)
body:
## Problem

During bulk imports SEO Pro Directory's job waits for each part's pictures to leave local storage ("draining") before the slot takes the next part. With WordPress cron off, the only path that removes local copies at once is `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::remove_local_now($id, $deadline)`, one picture per call. Each call takes the lease, checks that picture's files in the bucket (`heads()`, concurrent within the picture), deletes them, and runs `purge_pages()` in its `finally`.

Measured on a Hostinger site with an R2 bucket (4 November 2026, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.148), with nothing else wanting the lease (three import parts draining, none importing), a process calling `remove_local_now()` back to back removed **about 0.65 pictures a second (about 1.5 s each)**: 198 and 170 pictures in two 5-minute windows. All 13,382 pictures were already uploaded, so this alone held the import: three slots drained for over 50 minutes with no rows imported. With the lease shared with importing slots, 10-second turns gave 108-128 per 5 minutes.

Each picture's time is mostly one HEAD round trip to the bucket for its ~10-20 files (original, sizes, WebP, AVIF). The client already runs up to `seoprostack_media_storage_concurrency` (default 20) requests at once, but a single picture rarely fills that, and pictures are done one after another.

## Proposed change

Add a public batch form, for example `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::remove_local_many(array $ids, float $deadline): array` (ID => true|false|WP_Error, same meaning as `remove_local_now()`), that:

1. takes the lease once;
2. collects the files of every eligible picture (same checks as `remove_local_now()`: uploaded, removal record, not waiting for WebP/AVIF, not `kept:`);
3. checks them with one `heads()` call over all their keys at the configured concurrency;
4. deletes each picture's local files whose remote copies matched, records the result per picture as now;
5. purges pages once at the end, not per picture.

`remove_local_now()` can become `remove_local_many(array($id), $deadline)[$id]`.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php` (`remove_local_now()`, `remove_local()`, `heads()` caller near line 2862)

## Verification

- With 300 uploaded pictures whose local copies remain, `wp eval 'var_dump(count(array_filter(SEOProStack_Media_Storage::remove_local_many($ids, microtime(true) + 60))));'` removes at least 5x more than calling `remove_local_now()` in a loop for the same 60 s.
- A picture whose remote copy is missing or differs is kept and reported exactly as `remove_local_now()` reports it today.
- `purge_pages()` runs once per call.

Consumer: the PSD import pump (`scripts/import-pump.php`, `psd_pump_drain_assist()`) would switch to it when the method exists.

title: Keep pages cached: open the header menu, then the footer menu, then the home page's links, then the rest
body:
## Problem

After a purge, **Keep pages cached** opens the home page, the posts page and the items of every assigned menu location (in whatever order `get_nav_menu_locations()` returns them, so a footer menu can come before the header's), at most 20, then the newest pages and posts up to 50 where no crawler covers the rest. Two gaps against how visitors arrive:

- The header's links are what most visitors click first, then the footer's, then the links on the home page. The fill does not rank them that way, and leaves out links that are on the home page but in no menu (Kadence buttons, info boxes, post lists).
- Where nothing covers the rest of the site (WP-Optimize without its preload, LiteSpeed Cache with its crawler off), only the newest 50 pages and posts are opened; every other page stays uncached until a visitor builds it.
- WP-Optimize's preload is started 30 s after its purge, so it runs at the same time as the fill instead of after the main pages.

Owner's order (interactive session, 4 November 2026): header menu links, then footer menu links, then links from the home page, then the rest of the site.

## Proposed change

`includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php` (`of_site()`, `menu_urls()`):

1. Home page first (the logo and usually the first menu item link to it).
2. Header: the items of menu locations whose slug does not contain `footer` (registered order: Kadence's `primary`, `secondary`, `mobile`, then Kadence Pro's extra ones), plus the links inside the site header in the home page's HTML (`<header id="masthead">` / `.site-header` in Kadence, `<header class="wp-block-template-part">` in block themes), in document order.
3. Footer: the items of `footer` locations, then the links inside the site footer (`<footer id="colophon">` / `.site-footer`, `<footer class="wp-block-template-part">`).
4. The posts page, then the other links in the home page, in document order.
5. The rest: where LiteSpeed Cache's crawler or WP-Optimize's preload is on, they start after these pages (as the crawler already does). Otherwise SEO Pro Stack opens the rest itself: published pages, then posts, then other public post types, newest first, up to the queue's 1,000 addresses.

The home page's HTML is read once per fill, with the request that opens it (LiteSpeed's crawler user agent first; when LiteSpeed answers `201` because it already holds the page, once more as a visitor from the cache), parsed with `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor` (WordPress 6.2, the plugin's minimum), relative links made absolute, and passed through `clean()`. On a network fill each site keeps the menu order without reading its home page (25 pages per site, #1197).

`MAIN_MAX` rises from 20 to 50 so a large header plus footer plus home page still fits where a crawler covers the rest. `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php` `wp_optimize_purged()` and `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php` `done()`: start WP-Optimize's preload when the fill ends (as LiteSpeed's crawler is started), not 30 s after the purge.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php`
- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php` (read a page's HTML)
- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php`, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php` (WP-Optimize preload after the fill; setting description)
- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-cli.php` (`--dry-run` reads the home page to list its links)
- EDIT: `README.md` (Keep pages cached section, changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`

## Verification

On a disposable site with Kadence, a header menu (primary), a footer menu, a home page with links that are in no menu, and WP-Optimize's page cache on without preload:

- `wp seoprostack keep-cached --dry-run` lists the home page, then the header menu's pages, then the footer menu's, then the home page's other links, then the remaining pages and posts; no address twice, no query strings, files or other hosts.
- With WP-Optimize's preload after purge on, the list stops after the home page's links, and `wpo_page_cache_run_preload` is scheduled only when the fill's queue is empty.
- After a Purge All and the WP-Cron batches, every listed page is in WP-Optimize's cache folder; the debug log has no new messages.

title: Media storage: one transport error pauses all local-copy removal for an hour
body:
## What happened

One failed connection to the bucket pauses every local-copy removal on the site for an hour.

During a regional import with SEO Pro Stack 1.3.150, `remove_local_many()` met one `storage_transport` error ("Attachment 47230: The storage service could not be reached.") at about 21:59 UTC on 4 November 2026. Uploads before and after it succeeded. `seoprostack_storage_local_wait` was set to an hour ahead, and every later `remove_local_many()` call returned `false` for every picture at its first check (`(int) get_option(self::LOCAL_WAIT, 0) > time()`). The import job's three draining parts (about 2,100 pictures, all uploaded and converted) made no progress for the whole hour.

## Why

- `SEOProStack_S3_Client::retryable()` is true only for `storage_http` with `retryable` data, so a transport error (dropped connection, DNS or TLS failure) is never retryable. Deadline cut-offs are already marked separately with `at_deadline`.
- `remove_now_error()` starts with `$failures = 1` and calls `local_result()`. The keep-one-picture branch needs `retryable()` and `++$service_failures < 2`, so neither holds, and `local_result()` sets `LOCAL_WAIT` to `time() + HOUR_IN_SECONDS`.
- The storage batch's removal path behaves the same way for a transport error.

## Suggested change

Handle a single transport error (not `at_deadline`) on removal like a retryable one: leave that picture's files local, and retry it on the next pass or call, without pausing the site. Pause only when transport errors repeat in a pass, or after N within a few minutes. The pause could also be shorter (for example 5 minutes, doubling while the service stays unreachable), since nothing is lost by checking again. `storage_original_busy` already shows the pattern.

Files: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php` (`local_result()`, `remove_now_error()`, `remove_local_many()`), `includes/class-seoprostack-s3-client.php` (`retryable()`, `at_deadline()`).

## Verification

Make one HEAD fail with a transport error, for example by blocking the host for one request or using a filter in a test. Then:

- `remove_local_many()` should still remove the other pictures in the call.
- A second call should retry the failed picture.
- `seoprostack_storage_local_wait` should stay unset unless failures repeat.

## Current workaround

The consuming import pump lifts the pause once it has stood 5 minutes, when the stored error is the unreachable message. If the service is still down, the next removal fails and pauses again.

title: Keep pages cached: fill the cache again after it is emptied from outside the site (another site's Empty Entire Cache, the host's panel)
body:
## Problem

**Keep pages cached** fills the page cache again when the site's own WordPress empties it (LiteSpeed Cache's `litespeed_purged_all`, WP-Optimize's `wpo_cache_flush`) or a post changes. On LiteSpeed shared hosting the cache can also be emptied from outside the site, and then nothing fills it again:

- another site on the same hosting account sends Empty Entire Cache (`X-LiteSpeed-Purge: *`). `wp litespeed-purge all` sends it on a multisite network, and it reaches every site that shares the account's cache storage. `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` already purges network sites one at a time (`litespeed-purge blog <id>`) for this reason;
- the host's control panel or the server itself (a cache purge, a configuration change).

None of these run the site's WordPress, so `litespeed_purged_all` never fires there. LiteSpeed Cache's crawler doesn't help either: after a finished crawl it waits for its next full crawl, which is a day away at the preset's Crawl Interval of 86400 seconds. Visitors then get uncached pages until each one is visited.

## Evidence

On 4 November 2026: two single sites on one LiteSpeed shared hosting account, both running Kadence with Keep pages cached and LiteSpeed Cache's crawler on, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.150. Times are UTC.

- The fills after the 1.3.150 update finished at 21:01:36 and 21:05:27, opening 50 pages each (`seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_last`). LiteSpeed Cache's crawler, started when each fill ended, began its run at 21:07:04 and 21:10:58. It found 107 of 110 and 98 of 99 desktop pages missing (`wp-content/litespeed/crawler/meta.data`).
- Every warming-list page opened again at 22:25 was missing by 22:32 on both sites. Copies made at 22:32 and 22:37 were still held at 22:52. (A cached page's `expires` header gives the time LiteSpeed Cache built it.) The hosting panel created six cron jobs for other sites on the account between 22:27 and 22:29.
- In both windows no post was saved, no comment arrived and neither site's WordPress ran Purge All: no fill was queued, and `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_last` kept its 21:0x time. The two sites ran different hourly WP-Cron tasks in the window.
- The fill itself works. A fresh address opened by `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::open()` was a cache hit afterwards for desktop and phone visitors. Its work was emptied with nothing to fill it again.
- No purge happened between 22:39 and 23:01 on either site or on a third site on the account. So the emptying comes in events, not continuously.

## Proposed change

Add a cheap check that notices an emptied LiteSpeed page cache, wherever the purge came from, and starts the fill a Purge All starts:

1. A recurring WP-Cron event, every 5 minutes, scheduled while Keep pages cached is on and the page cache is LiteSpeed's (`SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::page_cache()` is `litespeed`). It is cleared when the feature is off or the plugin is deactivated, and in `uninstall.php`. Register the interval through `cron_schedules`, as `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::verify_schedule()` does.
2. Each run does nothing while a fill is queued (`SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue::get()` has addresses or `full`). Otherwise it opens the home page once with `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::open(home_url('/'), false)`, as LiteSpeed Cache's crawler. When LiteSpeed holds the page it answers `201` without running PHP, so a cached site costs one light request. A miss also caches the home page again.
3. It stores the answer in a non-autoloaded option (`held` true or false, and the time). It calls `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue::fill_later(...)`, as `litespeed_purged()` does, only when the answer is `miss` and the previous run found the page held. A home page LiteSpeed never caches, so missed on every run, never sets off fills. That covers excluded pages, admin-only sites with no front end, and a home page that redirects. Redirects (3xx), refusals (`SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::refused()`) and errors count as neither held nor emptied.
4. On a network the check runs on the main site only (`is_main_site()`), and a detected emptying fills every site (`fill_later(true)`): Empty Entire Cache empties them all. Subsites do not schedule it, so a large network sends one request every 5 minutes, not one per site.
5. WP-Optimize is unchanged. Its cache folder is emptied only through its own code, which already fires `wpo_cache_flush`, or by its cache lifespan, which its scheduled preload covers.

When the home page's own TTL runs out, the check fills the site again too (once a day at LiteSpeed Cache's default front-page TTL). Pages still held answer the fill's crawler requests with `201`, so that refresh is cheap.

Update the setting's description in `settings()` and the feature's file header to say it also notices a cache emptied from outside the site. Update README.md (Keep pages cached), readme.txt and changelog.txt.

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php` (schedule, check, description, header)
- `EDIT: includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php` (option constant, clear it in `clear()` if it fits there)
- `EDIT: uninstall.php` (new option and hook)
- `EDIT: README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php`
- `uninstall.php`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `changelog.txt`

## Verification

On a site with LiteSpeed Cache on a LiteSpeed server, with Keep pages cached on:

- `wp cron event list` shows the check every 5 minutes. With the feature off, or WP-Optimize as the page cache, it is not scheduled.
- With the home page cached, a run sends one request, which gets `201`, and queues nothing.
- Empty the cache without WordPress: LiteSpeed Cache's Empty Entire Cache from another site on the same account, or a request carrying `X-LiteSpeed-Purge: *`. The next run gets `miss` and queues a full fill (`wp option get seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_queue`). After the batches, `wp seoprostack keep-cached --dry-run` pages answer `x-litespeed-cache: hit` for desktop and phone visitors.
- On a site whose home page redirects or is never cached, runs never queue a fill.
- On a network, only the main site schedules the check, and an emptied cache fills every site.
- The debug log has no new messages. `scripts/lint.sh phpcs` and `scripts/lint.sh phpstan` pass.

title: Fixes for other plugins: cron writes land on the stored list, recurring events stop piling up copies, AI Engine stops rescheduling from page loads
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->
## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `wp-cron duplicate events AI Engine could_not_set DISABLE_WP_CRON` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: 0 open PRs / 0 open claimed issues touch `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`; last change there GH#1138
- [x] File refs verified: 4 refs checked, all present at `eef4cf23`
- [x] Tier: `tier:thinking` — the change touches how every site writes its cron list, under concurrency
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — design is in this brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-11-05
- **Created by:** ai-interactive, at the owner's request ("might also need an seoprostack fix if that's a common problem we need to solve for sites with our recommended plugins")
- **Conversation context:** a plugin rollout flagged new PHP log lines on one site; they were WordPress cron "could not be saved" errors from duplicated AI Engine tasks. An audit of every WordPress install on the same Hostinger account found duplicated recurring events on most of them. Removing them by hand did not last (trace below).

## What

Under **Fixes for other plugins** (`plugin_fixes`, on by default), make each site's cron list stop losing changes and piling up copies:

1. **Writes land on the stored list (all requests).** Add a `pre_update_option_cron` filter (receives `$value`, `$old_value`). Work out what this request changed: the events in `$value` but not `$old_value` (added), and the reverse (removed). Each event is keyed by timestamp, hook and `md5(serialize(args))`; skip the `version` key. Read the stored list fresh from the database (`$wpdb`, not the request's cached copy), apply those changes to it, and return that. When the stored list equals the request's view (the usual case), return `$value` unchanged. Only cron writes pay the one query; reads are unchanged.
2. **No second copy of a recurring event.** While applying additions in 1, skip a recurring event (`schedule` set) when the stored list already has one with the same hook, args **and** schedule at another timestamp. Also add a `pre_schedule_event` filter that returns `true` (already scheduled) for the same case, so a request that can already see the copy adds nothing. A different schedule still goes through, so a plugin can change an interval.
3. **Clean up existing copies in cron.** When WordPress cron runs (`wp_doing_cron()`), on `wp_loaded` (before `wp-cron.php` reads the due list, line 84), remove extra copies of recurring events with the same hook, args and schedule, keeping the earliest. Use one write, and only when something is removed. Single events, and copies whose args or schedule differ, are left alone.
4. **AI Engine (Meow Apps) task runner, with `DISABLE_WP_CRON`.** `Meow_MWAI_Modules_Tasks::ensure_cron_scheduled()` runs on `init` for every request, front end included. When `mwai_tasks_internal_run` is more than 300 seconds overdue, it calls `wp_clear_scheduled_hook()` and then `wp_schedule_event()`. A server cron job every 5 minutes (the usual Hostinger set-up, and WP Crontrol's advice) regularly leaves it that late, so visitor page loads keep rewriting the list. With `DISABLE_WP_CRON` set, outside cron and REST requests, and while AI Engine's dev mode is off: return `0` from `pre_clear_scheduled_hook` for `mwai_tasks_internal_run` when an event for it is queued (nothing cleared). Item 2 then makes its `wp_schedule_event()` a no-op. AI Engine's dashboard **Reset** (a REST request) and switching dev mode on (which clears this hook) must keep working. Read `dev_mode` the way AI Engine does (`$this->core->get_option('dev_mode')`, from its options array).

Update the setting description (`settings()`), `README.md` → Features, `readme.txt` and `changelog.txt` in the plugin's usual wording.

Decide in the PR, with evidence, whether 1 belongs under `plugin_fixes` or its own on-by-default setting on the Server tab (it is not specific to one plugin).

## Why

WordPress keeps every scheduled event in one autoloaded option, `cron`. Each request reads it once and writes the whole list back from that copy (`_set_cron_array()` → `update_option()`). WordPress refuses a duplicate **single** event (`wp_schedule_single_event()`) but not a duplicate **recurring** one (`wp_schedule_event()`, checked on WordPress 7.1.4).

Evidence from a temporary trace on one site (a `pre_update_option_cron` logger comparing the stored list, the writer's view and the new list, 5 November 2026, 01:22–01:32 UTC):

- One cron run of the main site takes about 90 seconds (01:27:03–01:28:30) and writes the list about 30 times, every write built from the copy it read at the start.
- Two minutes after the duplicates were removed by hand, a visitor page load (`/<listing>/`) cleared and rescheduled AI Engine's runner (item 4).
- Between two traced writes the stored copies went from 1 to 3 (`mwai_tasks_internal_run`) and from 4 to 5 (`wpil_*`). The only writer in that window was the cron run that had started before the hand removal: it wrote its old list back over it. A first hand removal came back the same way within 4 minutes, one copy with its old timestamp.

So copies come from two things: check-then-schedule races between requests, and long requests writing old lists back. When one request removes an event while another works from an old list, `wp-cron.php` logs "Cron reschedule/unschedule event error … could_not_set … The cron event list could not be saved" (lines 132–179). Old-list writes can also undo other plugins' scheduling.

Audit of 24 WordPress installs on one Hostinger account (all `DISABLE_WP_CRON` with a server cron job):

| Hook | Plugin | Copies found |
|---|---|---|
| `mwai_tasks_internal_run` (every minute) | AI Engine Pro 3.9.0 | 2–5 on 9 sites; copies 1–5 s apart |
| `wpil_action_queue_cron` (5 min), `wpil_email_cron` (hourly) | Link Whisper Premium | 2 each on 12 sites |
| `fs_data_sync_*` (daily) | Freemius SDK in several plugins | 2 on 4 sites |
| `mainwp_child_cron_*_health_check_daily` | MainWP Child | 2–3 on 3 sites |

Recent "could not be saved" errors are mostly `mwai_tasks_internal_run`, plus `fluentcrm_scheduled_five_minute_tasks` and SEO Pro Stack's own single event `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached`. That last one is the harmless case: a purge moved the batch (`SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue::save()`) while cron ran.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:thinking`

**Tier rationale:** item 1 changes how every site stores its scheduled tasks under concurrent requests; the merge rules, edge cases and failure fallback (return `$value` unchanged on any read or decode problem) need care.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`: register in `boot()` after the `enabled()` check, next to the `host_cron_schedules` block (~line 521). Keep each callback cheap: check the hook name or `wp_doing_cron()` first. Pattern: `host_cron_schedules()` (~line 749) reads `_get_cron_array()` once per request and caches per site.
- Same file, `settings()` (~line 454): extend the description, e.g. "Scheduled tasks are no longer lost or copied when requests overlap, extra copies (AI Engine, Link Whisper, Freemius, MainWP Child) are removed, and, with a server cron job, AI Engine stops rescheduling its task runner from visitor page loads."
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`: as for other fixes.
- Read `AGENTS.md` and the files it lists (STANDARDS.md, DEVELOPMENT.md, RELEASING.md) first.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`
- EDIT: `readme.txt`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`

## Acceptance criteria

- Two overlapping processes: A reads the list and sleeps; B schedules event X and removes event Y; A then schedules Z. The stored list ends with X and Z and without Y.
- After duplicates are removed, a process that read the list earlier and writes later does not bring them back.
- One cron run (`php wp-cron.php`) on a site with duplicated recurring events leaves one copy of each, the earliest. Single events, and events whose args or schedule differ, are untouched. Nothing is written when there is nothing to remove.
- `wp_schedule_event()` with the same hook, args and schedule as a queued event returns `true` and adds nothing. A different schedule still adds, as in core.
- With `DISABLE_WP_CRON` and AI Engine active, an overdue `mwai_tasks_internal_run` is not cleared or rescheduled by page loads, and still runs from cron. AI Engine's Reset and dev-mode switch still work.
- With the setting off, nothing changes. No new PHP messages in the debug log; `scripts/lint.sh` passes.

## Verification

- Preview site (`DEVELOPMENT.md` → preview site), `DISABLE_WP_CRON` true. Overlap test: `wp eval '$c=_get_cron_array(); sleep(20); wp_schedule_single_event(time()+900,"spsx_z");'` in one shell; within 20 s in another, `wp eval 'wp_schedule_single_event(time()+900,"spsx_x");'`. Then `wp cron event list --fields=hook | grep spsx_` lists both.
- Duplicates: `wp eval '$c=_get_cron_array(); $c[time()+40]["spsx_d"][md5(serialize(array()))]=array("schedule"=>"hourly","args"=>array(),"interval"=>3600); $c[time()+50]["spsx_d"][md5(serialize(array()))]=array("schedule"=>"hourly","args"=>array(),"interval"=>3600); _set_cron_array($c);'`. Item 2 may keep only one here, which is also correct. Otherwise run `php wp-cron.php` and confirm one `spsx_d` remains.
- AI Engine: make `mwai_tasks_internal_run` 6 minutes overdue, load the home page, confirm its timestamp is unchanged; run `php wp-cron.php` and confirm it runs and moves on. The Tasks screen's Reset still clears and re-adds it.

## Rollout

Release and rollout to sites need the owner's separate go-ahead (releases are not part of this task). After release, one cron run on each site removes the copies already there.

title: Keep pages cached: the outside-emptied check misses the first check after an update and a home page visitors re-cached
body:
## What

Keep pages cached's check for a LiteSpeed cache emptied from outside the
site (#1229, 1.3.151) misses two cases. Close both, so a site whose cache is
emptied from outside is always filled again within about five minutes.

1. **First check after an update.** The check starts a fill only when the
   home page goes from held to missing. Its first check has nothing stored,
   so if the cache was emptied between the end of the post-update fill and
   that first check, it only records "missing" and nothing fills the cache.
2. **Visitors re-cache the home page first.** The check looks at the home
   page, which visitors and bots open all the time. When the whole cache is
   emptied and someone opens the home page before the next check, the check
   finds it held, and every other page stays uncached.

## Evidence (Hostinger, 5 November 2026, UTC)

- Site A (single site): the fill finished at 01:55:18 (50 pages). The first
  check, at 02:00:12, found the home page missing and only recorded it. At
  about 02:07, four header-menu pages were all misses, with no fill queued.
- Site B (single site): the fill finished at 01:43:29. The first check, at
  01:48:09, recorded "missing" (no fill). No fill had run by 02:07.
- Site C (single site): the fill finished at 01:56:20 (50 pages), and the home
  page was held at 02:02:00. At 02:05, four header-menu pages were misses for
  the fill's own request, and visitors got hits only after that request
  cached them again.
- Where the check did see held change to missing (three other single sites,
  at 01:48:07, 01:51:57 and 01:53:55), it queued a full fill, and the pages
  were cached again within about ten minutes.

## How

- Check a page only the check opens: the home page with its own query string
  (`/?seoprostack-held=1`). LiteSpeed caches it apart from the home page
  (tested: miss, then hit; 200, no redirect), and visitors never open it.
  Where it does not answer 200 or 201 (a redirect, or refused), use the home
  page as now.
- When a fill finishes, open that page, and once more if LiteSpeed built it.
  Only when the second request is a hit, store it as held. Then the next
  check that finds it missing fills the cache. A page LiteSpeed never caches
  (excluded, a site with no front end) is still never stored as held, so it
  never starts fills.
- After a post is saved, the purge drops that page too. The fill of the
  saved post's page and the home page runs before the next check (the check
  waits while anything is queued), and that fill opens the page again.

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `changelog.txt`
- `seoprostack.php`

## Verification

On a Hostinger LiteSpeed site after deploy: the stored state reads held
after the post-deploy fill. Then empty the site's cache from outside
WordPress (for example a request whose response sends
`X-LiteSpeed-Purge: public,<prefix>_` for that site only). Within one check
(five minutes), a full fill is queued and the header pages are hits again.

title: Keep pages cached: batches from the host's cron job run 20 seconds in five minutes, so fills take hours on a network
body:
## What

Keep pages cached fills the cache in batches of about 20 seconds, a minute
apart (`SEOProStack_Keep_Pages_Cached::BUDGET`, `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue::GAP`).
Where the host runs WP-Cron from a cron job (`DISABLE_WP_CRON`, common on
LiteSpeed hosts), each batch waits for the next run of that job, often every
five minutes. So a fill works 20 seconds in every five minutes, and a cache
emptied from outside the site stays mostly empty for a long time:

- A 50-page single site: 2 to 6 batches, so 10 to 30 minutes.
- A network (11 sites, 25 pages each): 15 to 25 batches, so one to two
  hours. A network-wide purge meanwhile starts it again from the first site,
  and the check for an emptied cache (#1229) waits while a fill is pending.
  So the later sites of a busy network may never be filled.

Give a batch run from the command line (WP-Cron run by the host's cron job,
or WP-CLI) a longer time: no visitor waits on it, and there is no web server
time limit.

## Evidence (Hostinger, 5 November 2026, UTC)

- Every site's WP-Cron runs from an hPanel cron job every five minutes
  (`*/5 * * * *`); a network's runs through a runner that runs each site's
  WP-Cron in turn and stops a cycle after 240 seconds (about 50 seconds for
  11 sites when idle).
- One network's main site: a network fill queued since 4 November 11:43,
  26 network purges counted, 2,811 pages opened, and still pending at 02:38;
  its last finished fill was 4 November 09:20. One of its subsites showed
  uncached pages at 1 to 3 seconds each.
- A single site: a 50-page fill took two batches of 20 seconds (28, then 22
  pages, at about 0.6 seconds each); on slower sites (1 to 3 seconds a page)
  a batch opens 7 to 20 pages.

## How

- `run()`: a batch from the command line (`'cli' === PHP_SAPI`) gets 90
  seconds (new `CLI_BUDGET`), a web request's (WP-Cron from a visit) keeps 20.
  90 seconds keeps a network's cron cycle well under the runner's 240 and the
  five-minute interval, and pages are still opened one at a time.
- README: say that batches from the host's cron job run longer.

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`

## Verification

On a Hostinger site with WP-Cron from a cron job: after a purge, the first
batch run from that cron job opens up to 90 seconds of pages (the queue's
`opened` count and `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_last`), so a 50-page site
is filled in one or two runs.

title: Keep pages cached: network fills plan only the main site (next_site() always returns the first site)
body:
## What happens

A network fill in **Keep pages cached** only ever plans the main site's pages. Subsites are never filled after the main site finds the cache emptied from outside; they fill only after their own purges.

`SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Pages::next_site()` (`includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-pages.php:291`) narrows `get_sites(array('number' => 1, 'orderby' => 'id', ...))` with a `sites_clauses` filter (`blog_id >= $after`). `WP_Site_Query::get_sites()` caches results by its query vars, and the `sites_clauses` filter runs only in `get_site_ids()`, on a cache miss. Every call after the first in a request has the same query vars, so it gets the first call's cached result. That happens with WordPress's own in-request cache, without a persistent object cache.

## Evidence (an 11-site network on Hostinger LiteSpeed, 1.3.152, 5 November 2026)

- Through reflection, `next_site(1)`, `next_site(2)`, `next_site(5)`, `next_site(19)` and `next_site(23)` all return `1` (`wp_using_ext_object_cache()` false).
- `plan_network(true, 1, microtime(true), 90, 0)` returns 1,000 addresses, but only 25 distinct ones, all blog 1's (`blogs: {"1": 25}`), with `site: 1` and `done: false`: `network()` planned blog 1 forty times, until the `MAX` (1000) check stopped it.
- The queue option stays at `urls: 0, blogs: 0, full: true, network: true, site: 1` after each main-site turn of the host's multisite cron runner. Its `opened` count grew by 25 per turn (3,060 to 3,085 at 04:21–04:22 UTC), and its `since` (first purge not yet worked out) is still 4 November 11:43, 28 purges ago. `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_last` is still 4 November 09:20.
- Seen from outside: a subsite (blog 19) answered LiteSpeed misses after account-wide cache emptying until its own purge (the 1.3.152 deploy's `litespeed-purge blog 19`) queued its own fill.

Introduced in GH#1197 (PR #1200, commit f70931f1).

## Same pattern elsewhere

`SEOProStack_Security_Headers::cleanup_sites()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-security-headers.php:708`) pages through a network 50 sites at a time with the same `sites_clauses` cursor (`blog_id > $after`). It makes one call per POST, so it works without a persistent object cache. With one (Redis, Memcached), the cached first batch can come back for every later batch, so sites after the first 50 would never be cleaned.

## Fix

In both, ask `get_sites()` for all of this network's active site IDs (`'fields' => 'ids'`, `'number' => 0`, `'network_id' => get_current_network_id()`, ordered by ID). That query is cached correctly and refreshed when a site changes. Then pick the next ID, or the next 50, in PHP. Drop the `sites_clauses` filters.

## Verification

- `php -l`, PHPCS and PHPStan on the two files.
- On a live network: through reflection, `next_site(2)` returns 2, `next_site(6)` returns 7, and `next_site(23)` returns 0. `plan_network(true, 0, ...)` returns `done: true` with addresses for every site LiteSpeed caches.
- After the deploy, the main site's next runner turns record a finished fill (`seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_last` updated, queue option gone), and subsites' header and footer pages answer `x-litespeed-cache: hit`.

title: Keep pages cached: a purge during a batch is lost; network subsites hold the cron runner for 90 seconds
body:
## What happens

Two problems found on the Hostinger sites after 1.3.154 was deployed (5 November 2026).

### 1. A purge while a batch runs is lost

`SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Queue::done()` and `plan()` re-read the queue "as it is now (a purge or a saved post may have changed it meanwhile)", but `get()` uses `get_option()`, which returns this request's cached copy of a non-autoloaded option. A batch run from the command line lasts up to 90 seconds (#1236). A purge in another request during that time (`fill_later()`, or a saved post's `add()`) writes the database, but the batch's `done()` still sees the queue it read itself. It then deletes the option, or writes the old copy back, and the new fill is gone.

`hold()` then opens the check page again at the end of that batch, so the five-minute check never sees the cache emptied. The site stays unfilled until the next outside emptying.

Live evidence, the main site of an 11-site network:

- the deploy updated the network from 05:05:44 and purged site 1 (`wp litespeed-purge blog 1`) early in that window;
- the network's cron runner ran site 1's batch from 05:06:26 to 05:07:56; `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_last` = 05:07:53, held since 05:07:55;
- at 05:39, 24 of the 25 first pages (header and footer menus) were LiteSpeed misses taking 1–5 s, the queue was empty and `last` had not moved since 05:07:53.

GH#1232 fixed the same thing for the cron list (`SEOProStack_Cron_List::stored()` reads past the option caches).

### 2. Network subsites hold a sequential cron runner for 90 seconds each

Networks' WP-Cron is usually run from the command line one site after another (`wp site list` piped to `wp cron event run --due-now`, or a runner script). Since #1236 every site with a fill takes up to 90 seconds a turn. The deploy, and other tools since they stopped emptying the whole server, purge each site separately (`litespeed-purge blog <id>`), so every site gets its own fill.

On the 11-site network, a runner that stops starting sites after 240 seconds got through 5 sites in 353 s (one site took 142 s), and the next five-minute cycle was skipped. Each site got a turn about every 20–30 minutes, and other sites' scheduled tasks waited as long. With 20-second turns, every site's home, header and footer pages are opened in the first round, about 5 minutes.

## Fix

- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-queue.php`: `get()` forgets this request's copy of the option first (`wp_cache_delete()` on the option, and its entry in `notoptions`), so every read, and `update_option()`'s comparison, uses the stored queue.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-keep-pages-cached.php` `run()`: the command-line budget (`CLI_BUDGET`) only on a single site or a network's main site, which has the network fill and the check. Other network sites keep `BUDGET` (20 s).
- Release notes in `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md`.

## Verification

- `php -l` and PHPCS on both files; `scripts/lint.sh phpstan`.
- Live: start a batch from WP-CLI on a test site with a queue, run `wp litespeed-purge all` on it in a second shell during the batch, and check that `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_queue` is still `full` afterwards and a batch is scheduled.
- After the deploy: the network runner's `last-run.json` gets through more sites per cycle, and first-visit probes of each site's header and footer pages are hits within one runner rotation of a purge.

title: Load plugins only where needed's page checks take 90 s of each network site's cron turn and run while Keep pages cached fills
body:
## What happens

After 1.3.155 was deployed (5 November 2026, 06:36–07:08 UTC), the subsites of an 11-site network were still mostly uncached 16 minutes after their purge: on a first visit, 9 of 30 first pages were cache hits on one subsite and 10 of 25 on another. The main site, with 90-second batches, had 25 of 25.

The network's WP-Cron is run by a server cron job that starts each site's `wp-cron.php` from the command line, one site after another, and starts no site after 240 seconds. Its 06:55 cycle got through only 3 of the 11 sites in 243 s; one site took 94 s for 18 callbacks. So each subsite got one 20-second Keep pages cached batch in its first 20 minutes after the purge.

Timing every due event on one subsite (`wp cron event run --due-now`):

- `seoprostack_front_verify`: **89.8 s**
- `seoprostack_keep_pages_cached`: 22.9 s
- the 9 others: under 1 s each

`SEOProStack_Front_Verify::run()` (Load plugins only where needed, page checks) starts more addresses until `RUN_BUDGET` (50 s), and the last check can run up to `BUDGET` (60 s) plus a render's `TIMEOUT`. It repeats every 3 minutes while addresses wait.

Why addresses were waiting everywhere:

- every SEO Pro Stack version learns again (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loading::boot()`, GitHub issue #481); `seoprostack_plugin_front_forgets` shows one `seoprostack_updated` reset per release on each site (10 in the last 24 hours, 1.3.145 to 1.3.155);
- the deploy purges each site; Keep pages cached's fill requests are plain public GETs, so each page it opens that has no check result yet is queued (`queue_page()`, up to `QUEUE_MAX` 50);
- straight after the deploy, front-verify queues were 29–50 on the single sites checked, and 10–46 on the network's sites, with 0–8 addresses checked.

So the checks' uncached test renders run at the same time as the fill, on every site, right when the cache is empty. On a network run one site after another, they take most of each site's turn.

## Fix

- `includes/class-seoprostack-front-verify.php` `run()`:
  - **cache first:** while Keep pages cached has pages to open on the site (its queue has addresses, or the whole cache is to be filled), a run checks nothing and waits for its next turn. The task stays scheduled. The checks only make uncached renders of unchecked pages load fewer plugins; a saved post resets them anyway.
  - **short turns on a network from the command line:** when `'cli' === PHP_SAPI && is_multisite()`, a run starts no address after 15 s (`NETWORK_RUN_BUDGET`) instead of 50 s. A check, once started, is not cut short, so results are the same; they come in more turns.
- Release notes in `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md`; version 1.3.156.

Not changed: learning again on every SEO Pro Stack version (#481). It costs one round of checks per release, which is noticeable only while releases are many a day.

## Verification

- `php -l`, PHPCS and `scripts/lint.sh phpstan` on the changed file.
- On a network subsite from the command line: with Keep pages cached's queue non-empty, `wp cron event run seoprostack_front_verify` returns in under a second and the event stays scheduled; with the queue empty, the run stops starting addresses after 15 s.
- After the deploy: the network runner's `last-run.json` processes all 11 sites in a cycle, and first-visit probes of the subsites' first pages are cache hits within one or two cycles of their purge.

title: Keep pages cached and page checks go straight to this server behind a CDN when Server IP is empty
body:
## What

SEO Pro Stack's own requests to the site (Keep pages cached, purge delivery, the page checks of Load plugins only where needed) go straight to this server when the site sits behind a CDN, even while LiteSpeed Cache's **Server IP** is empty. Today they do only when Server IP is set, which takes an admin's click in **Hosting needs**, a fix that is not offered at all when LiteSpeed Cache is network-activated.

## Why (evidence, 2026-11-05)

On a Hostinger account with 25 installs behind Cloudflare, the server's own requests that went out through Cloudflare were answered by the origin's LiteSpeed with `403 Forbidden: Access to this resource on the server is denied!` (`x-turbo-charged-by: LiteSpeed`). This happened for minutes at a time, on every site and user agent tried (`lscache_runner`, WordPress's own and a desktop browser's). In one six-minute sample, 21 of 30 requests through Cloudflare were refused. The same requests sent straight to the server (`curl --resolve host:443:<server IPv4>`) were answered every time. Visitors outside the server were not affected.

- 24 of the 25 installs had Server IP empty. Their fills, purge deliveries, page checks and LiteSpeed Cache's own crawler all went through Cloudflare and were refused, so purged pages stayed uncached.
- In the same window the page checks saved addresses as needing every plugin, for a week. #1242 fixes that, and routes the checks through `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::resolver()` like the fills.
- With Server IP set by hand on one site, `wp seoprostack keep-cached` opened all 50 pages (`201 hit`), while the same request through Cloudflare at the same moment got `403`.
- Server IP was then set by hand on 32 sites (#1242 rollout). Without a plugin change, every new site and every other user's site behind a CDN still starts with it empty.

## How

Files:

- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php`, `resolver()`: today it returns a callback only when `SEOProStack_Litespeed::conf('server_ip')` is a valid IPv4. When that is empty, fall back to an origin address SEO Pro Stack has learned and verified itself.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed-crawler.php`: `origin()` already works out this server's public IPv4 from `$_SERVER['SERVER_ADDR']` on web requests, when the host name resolves elsewhere, and `reaches_server()` tests it. Store the address in SEO Pro Stack's own option, re-checked only when it changes, so command-line runs (WP-CLI, a host's cron job), which have no `SERVER_ADDR`, can use it. Never write LiteSpeed Cache's settings for this (`AGENTS.md`: other plugins' settings change only through presets, starters or a click).
- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed-crawler.php`, `save_origin()`: the one-click fix saves through `\LiteSpeed\Conf::update_confs()`. When Server IP changes, that runs `Cloud->init_qc_cli()`, a QUIC.cloud REST echo with a 60-second timeout. Check whether `Conf->update('server_ip', …)` (direct save, with LiteSpeed Cache's own IPv4 check) is enough, since Server IP is read at run time and written to no file. Also consider offering the fix on network-activated LiteSpeed Cache, where Server IP is per site and subsites follow the main site under **Use Primary Site Configuration**.
- If a direct request fails to connect (WP_Error: the address moved after a host migration), forget the learned address and use DNS until a web request learns it again.

Reference pattern: `SEOProStack_Litespeed::deliver_purge()`, `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::open()` and `page_html()` already add and remove the resolver around each request.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php`
- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed-crawler.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`
- EDIT: `readme.txt`

## Acceptance

- On a LiteSpeed site behind a CDN with Server IP empty, after one web request reaches PHP, Keep pages cached's batches, purge delivery and page checks from WP-CLI connect straight to the server. LiteSpeed Cache's own options stay unchanged.
- Where the host name resolves to this server, or the learned address does not reach LiteSpeed, nothing changes.
- README.md (Keep pages cached; Hosting needs → Server IP) and changelog say so.

## Verification

- `php -l`, `vendor/bin/phpcs`, `scripts/lint.sh phpstan`.
- On a CDN-fronted LiteSpeed test site with Server IP empty: open one page as a visitor, then run `wp seoprostack keep-cached` and see each page answer `201 hit`/`200`. From the server, `curl` the site through DNS for comparison.
- Point the learned address at an unused IP: the next batch falls back to DNS and the address is forgotten.

title: Server IP read ignores LiteSpeed Cache's Use Primary Site Configuration on networks
body:
## What

On a network where LiteSpeed Cache is network-active with **Use Primary Site Configuration** on, SEO Pro Stack reads LiteSpeed Cache's Server IP from the subsite's own option, which LiteSpeed Cache ignores there. The subsite's own option is usually empty, so:

- page checks and Keep pages cached requests (`SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::resolver()`, added in #1242) go through the CDN instead of straight to this server, and get the origin's 403 refusals described in #1242 and #1243;
- the LiteSpeed crawler notice (`SEOProStack_Litespeed_Crawler::origin()`) says Server IP is empty when LiteSpeed Cache already uses one.

## Evidence (a production network on LiteSpeed hosting, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.3)

On subsite A:

- `get_site_option('litespeed.conf.use_primary_settings')` = `'1'`
- `get_site_option('litespeed.conf.server_ip')` = `NULL`, `get_option('litespeed.conf.server_ip')` = `''`
- `\LiteSpeed\Conf::cls()->conf('server_ip')` and `apply_filters('litespeed_conf', 'server_ip')` return the primary site's IPv4 address
- `SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::resolver(home_url('/'))` returns `null` (DNS), while subsite B, with its own value set, returns the direct resolver.

LiteSpeed Cache works out the effective value in `Conf::_try_load_site_options()` / `load_options()`: primary-site settings, minus `$single_site_options`, then network overrides and `LITESPEED_CONF` constants. Copying those rules would drift; LiteSpeed Cache's public `litespeed_conf` filter (`src/api.cls.php`) returns the value it uses.

## How

- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`: add a read of the effective setting through `apply_filters('litespeed_conf', $id)` when LiteSpeed Cache has registered it (`has_filter('litespeed_conf')`), falling back to `SEOProStack_Litespeed::conf()`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php` `resolver()` and `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed-crawler.php` `origin()`: read `server_ip` through it.
- Changelog, README and readme.txt note; patch release.

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh` (PHP lint, PHPCS, PHPStan) clean.
- On a network with Use Primary Site Configuration on and Server IP set on the primary site only, after deploy: `wp eval 'var_dump((bool) SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::resolver(home_url("/")));' --url=<subsite>` is `true`; page checks on subsites stop failing with 403; the network cron cycle still reaches every site.
- Single sites with their own Server IP behave as before.

For #1242. Ref #1243.

title: Fix: 1.3.157 fatal error on single sites: ms_is_switched() is multisite-only (Keep pages cached, page checks, Hosting needs)
body:
## What

1.3.157 (#1245) added `SEOProStack_Litespeed::server_ip()`, which starts with `!ms_is_switched()`. WordPress defines `ms_is_switched()` in `wp-includes/ms-blogs.php`, which `wp-settings.php` loads only on multisite. On every single site, the first call is a fatal error:

```
Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to undefined function ms_is_switched()
  in includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php:574
#0 includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php(274): SEOProStack_Litespeed::server_ip()
#1 includes/class-seoprostack-keep-cached-requests.php(126): SEOProStack_Keep_Cached_Requests::resolver()
```

## Effect on single sites with LiteSpeed Cache (seen on a Hostinger account after deploying 1.3.157)

- **Keep pages cached**: every batch and the five-minute check end in the fatal error, so the cache is never filled again after a purge. Visitor probe 30 minutes after the deploy's purge: 1 hit in 30 pages on each of three single sites (home, header and footer pages all missed); before 1.3.157, one of them answered 15 of 15 from the cache.
- WP-Cron run from the host's cron job (`php wp-cron.php` or WP-CLI) dies at that event, so later events in the same run wait for the next run. The fatal is not written to the site's PHP error log there, so the deploy's log check did not see it.
- **Load plugins only where needed**' page checks (`SEOProStack_Front_Verify::render()` → `resolver()`) and `SEOProStack_Litespeed::deliver_purge()` fail the same way.
- **Hosting needs** (`SEOProStack_Litespeed_Crawler::advice()` → `state()` → `origin()` → `server_ip()`): Site Health and the Server tab's LiteSpeed row fail with the same error.
- Networks are unaffected (`ms-blogs.php` is loaded), which is why #1245's checks on an 11-site network passed.

## Fix

`includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`, `server_ip()`: `(!is_multisite() || !ms_is_switched())`. No other call in `includes/` or `admin/` uses a multisite-only function without an `is_multisite()` guard: `get_blog_option()` on the next line sits behind `network_active()`, which returns false on a single site first.

## Verification

- `wp eval 'echo SEOProStack_Litespeed::server_ip();'` on a single site with LiteSpeed Cache: the Server IP, no error. On a network: unchanged, the main site's value on subsites through `switch_to_blog()` as in #1245.
- `wp eval 'SEOProStack_Litespeed_Crawler::advice();'` on a single site: no error.
- After deploy: `wp cron event run seoprostack_keep_pages_cached_check` fills after a purge, and the visitor probe finds header and footer pages cached.
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.

Files: `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php` (`server_ip()`), version and changelog files for release 1.3.158.

body:
## What

Compared with the starter at [wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding@2580267](https://github.com/wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding/commit/2580267d5a1ec47607cd3b8f61880ae9fc7f61ad): 4 of 83 core files differ from the starter. Run scripts/sync-core.sh, or change the starter first. Core files are the same in every plugin made from the starter, apart from the names (STANDARDS.md → Structure).

- `scripts/deploy-sites.sh` (differs, behind)
- `scripts/lib/deploy-remote.sh` (differs, behind)
- `scripts/update-test.sh` (differs, behind)
- `RELEASING.md` (differs, behind)


## How

1. Next to this repository: `git clone https://github.com/wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding.git` (or `git -C ../wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding pull`).
2. Here, on a branch: `scripts/sync-core.sh --from ../wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding`, then review `git diff`.
3. Each file's class says what a sync does with it (DEVELOPMENT.md → Starter sync): **behind** and **missing** files are updated or added. A file **changed here** holds a change this plugin made that no starter version has: it goes into the starter first (a pull request, or an issue there with this plugin's case); sync after it is merged there, with `--discard-local`. Never keep a plugin-only change in a core file: move it to this plugin's own files or its own blocks. A **newer** file has a starter version the starter's default branch does not contain: sync from a starter ref that does. While a file is changed here or newer, a sync writes nothing.
4. Read the starter's `changelog.txt` since this plugin last synced, for changes that need work in this plugin's own files (its Setup class, `phpstan-plugin.neon`, `.distignore` entries, README or readme.txt sections).
5. `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass; add a changelog line; open a pull request.

The daily Starter sync workflow (`.github/workflows/starter-sync.yml`) updates this issue while files differ and closes it once they match.

## Verification

`scripts/sync-core.sh --check --from ../wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding` reports that all core files match the starter.

title: perf: Media in cloud storage keeps its URL index as one wp_options row per file (107,444 rows on a 4,600-listing stack)
body:
## What

Media in cloud storage keeps its URL index as one `wp_options` row per stored
file: `update_option(self::URL_INDEX . hash('sha256', $config['signature'] .
$key), $id, false)` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`,
`URL_INDEX = 'seoprostack_storage_url_'`, written near lines 1232 and 5056 and
read near 5287 and 5621 in 1.3.158). Every file of every picture adds a row,
so a directory stack's `wp_options` grows by about 12 rows per picture.

## Evidence

East Sussex stack, 5 November 2026 (SEO Pro Stack 1.3.158), about 4,600
listings and 9,000 pictures, import still running:

- `wp_options`: **118,302 rows**, of which **107,444**
  `seoprostack_storage_url_*` and 9,017 `seoprostack_storage_job_*`
  (9.6 MB).
- Anything that scans `wp_options` pays for them. Rank Math's sitemap cache
  clear (`DELETE … WHERE option_name LIKE '_transient_sitemap_%'`, on every
  saved post) took **456 ms each** during the import. Backups, search-replace
  and option-table maintenance grow the same way.
- A 30,000-listing region (Portland, DC/Maryland/Virginia, Orlando are
  importing or queued) would reach about 700,000 such rows.

## How (suggested)

Move the URL index to its own table, keyed by the SHA-256 of signature and key
(binary(32) primary key, attachment ID), like `wp_seoprostack_media_claims`.
Read the table first and fall back to the option during a batched migration
that moves existing rows and deletes the options (resumable, bounded batches,
WP-CLI command plus cron). Drop the table on uninstall. Consider whether the
`seoprostack_storage_job_*` per-picture rows can move too.

## Verification

- Every lookup that resolved before resolves after migration (sample 1,000
  stored URLs: same attachment ID).
- `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wp_options WHERE option_name LIKE
  'seoprostack_storage_url_%'` reaches 0 after migration; uploads during and
  after the migration index into the table.
- Rank Math's sitemap clear on a migrated stack takes milliseconds, not
  hundreds.

title: perf: Media in cloud storage keeps kept originals' inventories as one wp_options row per picture (9,522 rows on a 9,000-picture stack)
body:
## What

Media in cloud storage keeps each kept original's inventory as one
`wp_options` row: `seoprostack_storage_job_original_<sha256(original_signature . backup)>`
(`includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`: inserted by
`remember_original()` (atomic `INSERT IGNORE`, so a deletion tombstone is never
overwritten), tombstoned by `delete_original()`, read by `finish_original()`,
`original_counts()` and `original_jobs()`, names paged through
`jobs(…, '', 'original_')` with the `JOB . 'originalcursor'` cursor).
That is a recovery inventory kept outside attachment meta on purpose (core
deletes meta), so the table must keep the insert-only and tombstone rules.
That is one row of about 1 KB per picture with a kept original, so a directory
stack's `wp_options` still grows with its library after #1251 moved the URL index
(about 12 rows per picture) into `{prefix}seoprostack_media_urls`.

## Evidence

East Sussex stack, 5 November 2026 (1.3.159), about 9,000 pictures:
`seoprostack_storage_job_original_*` = **9,522 rows, 10 MB**, non-autoloaded
(`originaluse_*` 88 rows; everything else under `seoprostack_storage_job_` is single rows).

## How (suggested)

Follow the #1251 pattern (`url_store()`, `url_lookup()`, `build_urls()`):

1. A `{prefix}seoprostack_media_originals` table keyed by the same SHA-256
   (`binary(32)` primary key), with the serialized inventory and the fields
   `original_jobs()` pages by, so its cursor (`JOB . 'originalcursor'`) can page the
   table instead of `option_name`.
2. Read the table first and fall back to the option until this version has moved
   them; move in bounded batches from `run_batch()` (with `index_due()`), and in
   the WP-CLI `url-index` action or a sibling.
3. Drop the table in `uninstall.php`; keep the state option under
   `seoprostack_storage_job_` so uninstall removes it.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`
- EDIT: `uninstall.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`

## Verification

- `wp seoprostack media-storage status` originals counts are the same before
  and after the move on a stack with kept originals.
- `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wp_options WHERE option_name LIKE 'seoprostack\_storage\_job\_original\_%'`
  reaches 0; a new upload's kept original is recorded in the table, drains to the
  originals bucket and is removed locally as before.
- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan` passes.

title: Licence checks: requests for the site's own pictures are held when the file name contains "Licensed"
body:
## What happens

"Ask before licence checks" holds any outgoing call whose address contains `licenc` or `licens` (`SEOProStack_Licence_Calls::is_licence_call()`, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-licence-calls.php:231`). Media file names often come from business or product names, so requests for the site's own pictures are held as licence checks, for example:

```
https://<media-storage-host>/2026/11/<hash>-<Business>-Licensed-Associate-Real-Estate-Broker-Featured-Photo.jpg?v=<version>
```

The held call returns `WP_Error http_request_failed: SEO Pro Stack held this licence check until the site owner allows it.`

## Impact (observed 5 November 2026, 1.3.160)

SEO Pro Directory's region import fetches each part's first drained picture from the bucket (`SEOProDirectory_Import_Jobs`, "The bucket sample did not return HTTP 200.") and stops the job when that fails. On a US regional site the job stopped three times in 15 minutes. The cause was found only by logging `pre_http_request`: the held call never reaches `http_api_debug`, so it looks like a network failure. "Licensed" is a common word in US trade names ("Licensed Plumber", "Licensed & Insured"), so any import or plugin that fetches such a picture is affected.

## Fix

In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-licence-calls.php`:

1. `exempt_host()`: also exempt SEO Pro Stack's own media storage hosts, meaning the host of `SEOProStack_Media_Storage::config()['url']` and the storage endpoint host when one is configured. These are the site's own files, like `home_url()`, which is already exempt.
2. `is_licence_call()`: do not treat a path ending in a media or document extension (`jpe?g|png|gif|webp|avif|svg|ico|bmp|tiff?|mp4|webm|mov|pdf`) as a licence call. A real licence check calls an endpoint, not a picture.
3. Optional: match `licen[cs]` only in path segments and query keys or values, not inside a file name.

- `wp eval 'var_export( SEOProStack_Licence_Calls::is_licence_call( "https://example.com/edd-sl/check_license", array() ) );'` still prints `true`.

title: Media storage: WebP/AVIF copies written after a picture's removal stay local, unrecorded and never uploaded
body:
## What happens

A picture can end up recorded as removed and marked done (`_seoprostack_storage_local` = the connection signature, `_seoprostack_storage_done` set, `_seoprostack_storage_removed` present) while WebP/AVIF copies made after the removal are still on disk. Those copies are not in the removal record and not in the bucket (HEAD 404). The storage batch treats the picture as finished, so nothing ever uploads or removes them.

Observed on 1.3.160 (5 November 2026), two pictures on two sites, during a SEO Pro Directory region import with the media batch and WebP/AVIF conversion running in separate WP-CLI processes:

- Picture A: the removal record held the 4 JPEG files (original + 3 sizes). Six `.jpg.avif`/`.jpg.webp` copies were on disk, all written in the same second, after the removal. `_seoprostack_nextgen_done` = `avif:60s,webp:80s`.
- Picture B: the same pattern, 4 recorded JPEG files and 7 local format copies.
- A read-only scan of about 52,700 removed pictures on four sites found only these two, so it is a rare race.

## Impact

- SEO Pro Directory's import drain (`local_files()`) waits on the picture for ever, so the part never finishes and the job stops at its one-hour no-progress limit ("The part did not drain within the one-hour safety limit."). Resuming only restarts the hour.
- The page may name format copies that the bucket does not have.

## Cause (not confirmed)

The conversion wrote the copies after the files were removed, without starting a new storage generation (the done marker stayed set). Candidates, unverified:

1. The conversion process read the JPEG before removal and wrote its copies after it. `remove_local_now()` and the batch check `SEOProStack_Nextgen_Images::is_waiting()` before removing, but the check and the conversion's write are not atomic.
2. A worker wrote the done marker after the conversion's `queue()` (the comment in `queue()` mentions this race for generation changes).

## Recovery that worked (SEO Pro Stack's own calls)

```php
SEOProStack_Media_Storage::restore_attachment( $id );       // bring the 4 JPEGs back (sets kept:)
SEOProStack_Media_Storage::queue( $id );                    // new generation, clears done
delete_post_meta( $id, '_seoprostack_storage_local', 'kept:' . SEOProStack_Media_Storage::config()['signature'] );
SEOProStack_Media_Storage::upload_attachment( $id );
```

Within 90 seconds the batch had uploaded and removed all 11 files. The record then listed every format copy, each one answered 200 from the bucket, and no local file was left.

## Suggested fix

In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php` and `class-seoprostack-nextgen-images.php`:

1. When the conversion writes a format copy for a picture that is removed, or whose done marker is set, call `queue()` after the write, so the copy is uploaded and removed with the rest.
2. Self-heal in the batch or `health --repair`: for a picture recorded as removed whose local files are not in its removal record, start a new generation and upload it again, as above.
3. Optional: hold the picture's storage lease while it is converted, so the removal cannot run between the conversion's read and its write.

## Verification

- With a picture in this state, `wp seoprostack health --repair` (or the next batch) uploads the extra copies and removes them, and the removal record lists them.
- `wp seoprostack media-storage status` counts no removed pictures with local files.
- Region imports run to the end without a one-hour stop caused by this.

title: Speed: put SEO Pro Stack's own small stylesheets (form keys, post reactions, iframe block) in the page instead of render-blocking links
body:
## What

SEO Pro Stack's own small front-end stylesheets block the first paint as separate requests. Put them in the page instead, through WordPress's own inlining of small styles (`wp_style_add_data($handle, 'path', $file)`, which `wp_maybe_inline_styles()` inlines within `styles_inline_size_limit`), or print them inline where that budget is already used.

## Why (evidence, PageSpeed Insights mobile, 2026-11-05)

Each one shows up in Lighthouse's render-blocking list, about 150 ms each in its estimate:

- `seoprostack/assets/form-keys.css` (1.9 KB): the home pages of two Kadence multisite network sites with Fluent Forms.
- `seoprostack/assets/post-reactions.css` (4.4 KB): the same two pages.
- `seoprostack/blocks/iframe/style.css` (1.3 KB): the home page of a Kadence single site. This is registered from `block.json`, so core already knows its path, but it was still printed as a `<link>`. Find out why (for example, the inline budget already used by other styles) before choosing a fix.

They are loaded only on pages that use them, and in the head on purpose so nothing shows unstyled (`SEOProStack_Form_Keys::assets()`). Inlining keeps that while removing the request.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-form-keys.php`, `enqueue_style()` (around line 207): after `wp_enqueue_style()`, add `wp_style_add_data(self::HANDLE, 'path', SEOPROSTACK_DIR . $css)`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-post-reactions.php`, `register()` (around line 297): the same after `wp_register_style()`. It has an inline colour style (`wp_add_inline_style`), which core keeps when it inlines.
- `blocks/iframe`: check a page head with the block. If the budget is the cause, consider a small `styles_inline_size_limit` allowance for SEO Pro Stack's own handles only. Never raise it for other plugins' styles.
- Leave the admin (`is_admin()`) and block editor paths as they are.

Reference pattern: core's block style inlining (`wp_maybe_inline_styles()` in `wp-includes/script-loader.php`).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-form-keys.php`
- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-post-reactions.php`
- EDIT (if needed): `includes/features/class-seoprostack-iframe-block.php`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`, `README.md` (changelog lines)

## Acceptance

- On a page with a Fluent Forms form (form keys), a post-reactions block and the iframe block, no `seoprostack/` stylesheet is a `<link rel="stylesheet">` in the head for a visitor who is not logged in. The same rules are in a `<style id="...-inline-css">` instead.
- Forms, the reactions panel and iframes look the same as before on first paint.

## Verification

- `php -l`, `vendor/bin/phpcs`, `scripts/lint.sh phpstan`.
- On the preview site, after a purge: `curl -s <page URL> | rg "seoprostack/(assets|blocks)/.*\.css"` finds no `<link>`.
- PageSpeed Insights mobile on the same page: the `seoprostack/` entries are gone from "Render-blocking requests".

title: Speed: keep Tutor LMS's styles and scripts (and React) to pages that use Tutor
body:
## What happens

Tutor LMS 4.2.0 and Tutor LMS Pro load their styles and scripts on every front-end page, including pages with no course, lesson, dashboard, Tutor shortcode or Tutor block. On a Kadence home page with no Tutor content (checked 5 November 2026, served from the LiteSpeed cache) the page carried:

- styles: `tutor/assets/css/tutor-icon.min.css`, `tutor.min.css`, `tutor-front.min.css`, `tutor/assets/blocks/cart-button/index.css`, `tutor-pro/assets/css/front.css`, `tutor-pro/assets/lib/codesample/prism.css`, and the Kadence theme's `assets/css/tutorlms.min.css` (handle `kadence-tutorlms`, enqueued by `themes/kadence/inc/components/tutorlms/component.php` whenever Tutor is active);
- scripts: `tutor/assets/js/tutor.js`, `tutor-front.js`, `tutor/assets/lib/SocialShare/SocialShare.min.js`, `tutor-pro/assets/js/front.js`, `tutor-pro/assets/lib/prism/prism.min.js` and `script.js`, and through `tutor-script`'s dependencies (`wp-element`, `wp-i18n`, `wp-date`) React, ReactDOM, moment, `element`, `date`, `hooks`, `i18n`, `escape-html` and `deprecated` from `wp-includes/js/dist`.

The HTML had no element with a `tutor-` class or ID other than those asset tags and the body class `tutor-lms`. PageSpeed (mobile, 5 November) showed Tutor's stylesheets among the render-blocking requests on 11 of 15 measured home pages, about 75 KB of CSS each, before the JavaScript.

`TUTOR\Assets` (`tutor/classes/Assets.php`) enqueues `common_scripts()`, `frontend_scripts()` and `enqueue_scripts()` on `wp_enqueue_scripts` for every page; only its dashboard and learning-area files are conditional.

## Why Load plugins only where needed keeps Tutor on these pages

Seen in the learned map (`seoprostack_plugin_front`) of a network subsite and a single site:

1. Tutor's notes are `always, content, pages, login, bar`. `always` comes from one callback on `determine_current_user`: `TUTOR\RestAuth::api_auth()` (`tutor/restapi/RestAuth.php`), which returns the user unchanged unless the request path holds `/wp-json/tutor/`. Plugins on that hook always load (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loading::FRONT_ALWAYS_HOOKS`), and `login` keeps a plugin out of `front_propose()`.
2. Its assets on every page make `page_needs()` (via `asset_owners()`) list Tutor as needed by the front page kind, so even a check (`SEOProStack_Front_Verify`) could not prove the page renders the same without it.

So the plugin cannot be skipped on those pages, and its assets are the real cost on cached pages. Skipping the PHP is a separate, smaller gain for uncached pages (follow-up below).

## Change

New Speed feature, on by default (safe on any site: it only dequeues, on pages without Tutor content), modelled on `SEOProStack_Woo_Light` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-woo-light.php`):

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-tutor-light.php`, class `SEOProStack_Tutor_Light`, setting `tutor_light`, label "Lighter Tutor LMS pages", tab `speed`. Registered in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES` after `SEOProStack_Woo_Light`, and in `SEOProStack_Speed_Plan::items()` defaults (`isset($active['tutor'])`).
- Tutor pages keep everything: Tutor's post types (from `tutor()`: course, bundle, lesson, topics, quiz, assignment, announcement, enrollment, Zoom and Google Meet), their archives and taxonomies, the query vars Tutor registers (`course_subpage`, `lesson_video`, `tutor_dashboard_page`, `tutor_dashboard_sub_page`, `tutor_profile_username`), `tutor_utils()`' dashboard, learning area, course list and course details checks, the pages named in `tutor_option` (dashboard, registration, cart, checkout and other `*_page`/`*_page_id` entries), and singular posts whose content, or a synced pattern in it, has a `[tutor_…]` shortcode or a `tutor…/` block. Filter `seoprostack_tutor_light_page` for anything else.
- Elsewhere, at `wp_enqueue_scripts` `PHP_INT_MAX`: dequeue styles and scripts whose file is in the `tutor` or `tutor-pro` plugin folder, and `kadence-tutorlms`. Their dependencies (React and the rest) then load only if something else needs them.
- If a Tutor shortcode or block renders anyway (a Kadence Element, a widget), the dequeued handles are enqueued again at that moment; WordPress prints them in the footer.
- Left alone while the admin bar shows (Tutor adds toolbar items), and in the admin.
- README.md (Features list and a section under Speed, with the filter in the hooks list), readme.txt and changelog.txt.

## Follow-up (separate issue)

Let Load plugins only where needed skip Tutor on pages without Tutor content, as it does for WooCommerce (`woo_can_skip()`): treat `TUTOR\RestAuth::api_auth` on `determine_current_user` as known and harmless for page requests, and keep Tutor on its own pages and pages (`woo_pages`-style list from `tutor_option`).

## How to check

1. `scripts/lint.sh php`, `scripts/lint.sh phpcs`, `scripts/lint.sh phpstan`.
2. On a site with Kadence, Tutor LMS 4.2 and Tutor LMS Pro: a logged-out home page with no Tutor content has no `plugins/tutor/`, `plugins/tutor-pro/` or `tutorlms.min.css` asset and no `react.min.js` (unless another plugin needs it). A course page, the dashboard, the cart and a page with `[tutor_login]` keep them all and work (enrol button, login modal, dashboard menus).
3. Screenshot comparison of the home page before and after shows no change.
4. PageSpeed mobile on the home page: fewer render-blocking requests, lower total JavaScript.

title: Speed: Load the CSS each page uses first covers every recommended plugin and theme, and the classes their scripts add
body:
## Why

Owner's decision (5 November 2026, superseding the limit recorded in #1194): **Load the CSS each page uses first** should cover the stylesheets of every plugin and theme SEO Pro Stack recommends, as they may be used on some page at some point, so Kadence sites with the recommended stack get the whole speed gain.

A survey of 15 sites' home pages (logged out, 5 November) found these render-blocking stylesheets that Used CSS does not handle today: Tutor LMS and Tutor LMS Pro (9 sites), Syndication Links (8), Readabler (8), IndieWeb and Webmention (5), SEO Pro Stack's own (2), AI Engine Pro (2), Fluent Cart, TranslatePress, WP Grid Builder and Bookly (1 each), and Kadence child themes (2).

## Pilot findings (Used CSS on two Kadence sites: a single site and a network subsite)

Screenshot comparison (`compare.mjs`: feature off vs on, and on with the full stylesheets blocked, so only the used CSS applies), 128 shots over desktop, mobile and both colour schemes, menus, drawers, forms, accordions and footers:

- Network subsite: no CSS difference (two differences came from lazy images loading at different times).
- Single site's home: with only the used CSS, the Kadence row background slider showed a list bullet and 40 px of list padding. Kadence Blocks' `kb-splide-init.js` adds the `kb-splide` class after load, and `.kb-splide .splide__list{margin:0!important;padding:0!important}` and `.kb-splide .splide__slide{list-style-type:none!important}` need it; `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Match::CLASSES` has `splide*` but not `kb-splide`.

An audit of the supported plugins' front-end scripts (`classList.add/toggle`, `addClass`) found more classes added after load that `CLASSES` lacks, for example Kadence Blocks Pro's AOS animations (`aos-init`, `aos-animate`: elements with `data-aos` keep `opacity:0` until the full stylesheet arrives), slick and tiny-slider carousels, Kadence Blocks forms (`kb-form-*`, `kb-adv-form-*`), Fluent Forms' conditional fields (`ff_cond_v`) and steps, and Fluent Forms Pro's accordion and tabs. A hand-kept list goes stale with each plugin update, and every new source adds its own.

## Change

1. **Classes the page's scripts add count as present.** New `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Scripts`: for each `<script src>` (or `data-src`) on the page served from this site, read once per file version (cache file next to the stylesheets' in `uploads/seoprostack-used-css`), and for inline scripts, collect the class names the code adds or tests: `classList.add/remove/toggle/replace/contains(…)`, jQuery `addClass/removeClass/toggleClass/hasClass(…)`, `className =`/`+=`, `setAttribute('class', …)` and `class="…"` in HTML strings; a literal ending in `-` or `_` followed by `+` or `${` is a prefix. `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Match` adds them to the page's tokens. `CLASSES` stays as the baseline (adding `kb-splide`, `aos-*`, `slick-*`, `tns-*`), and the filter stays.
2. **Sources.** `SEOProStack_Used_Css_Links::PLUGINS` lists the recommended plugins with front-end stylesheets (`admin/data/free-plugins.php`, `pro-plugins.php`), their Pro add-ons, Kadence's other plugins and the integrations SEO Pro Stack supports (Readabler, IndieWeb, WP Grid Builder), plus SEO Pro Stack's own folder; a Kadence child theme's folder counts with the parent's. The `seoprostack_used_css_sources` filter stays for anything else (unsupported).
3. `SEOProStack_Used_Css::plan()` recommends it where any source is active, with updated text; the setting description, the file headers, README.md, readme.txt, changelog.txt and the AGENTS.md rule ("Do not widen it…") updated to the new scope.

## How to check

1. `scripts/lint.sh php`, `phpcs`, `phpstan`.
2. Re-run the pilot comparison on both pilot sites (and a Fluent Forms page): no differences in `blocked` shots other than lazy images; the single site's hero slider has no bullet.
3. View source of a page: the end comment `SEO Pro Stack Used CSS: N stylesheets` counts Tutor, Syndication Links, Readabler, IndieWeb and Webmention stylesheets where they load.
4. PageSpeed mobile on the pilot sites: render-blocking requests drop to none (or third-party only).
