title: Speed: load AI Engine's site-wide chatbot on first use, not in every page's head
body:
## What

New Speed feature, on by default: **Load AI Engine's chatbot on first use**. Where AI Engine (or AI Engine Pro) shows a site-wide chatbot, its script, React and its theme stylesheet load when the visitor first interacts with the page (pointer, touch, key or scroll), instead of in the page's head.

## Why (evidence)

PageSpeed Insights mobile, 5 November 2026, two Kadence sites with AI Engine Pro 3.9.0's site-wide chatbot: mobile scores 60 and 69, LCP 7.2 s and 7.5 s; Lighthouse's render-blocking audit puts AI Engine's files first, with an estimated 3 to 5 s saving. One of them is the only site of the 15 measured whose Chrome UX Report field data is "slow".

AI Engine Pro 3.9.0 (`classes/modules/chatbot.php`, `register_scripts()`): with a site-wide chatbot (`botId` option), `wp_enqueue_scripts` enqueues `mwai_chatbot` (`app/chatbot.js`, 349 KB, registered with `in_footer` false and the `wp-element` dependency) and `mwai_chatbot_theme_<id>` (`themes/<id>.css`) on every page, so React, ReactDOM and the chatbot script are synchronous scripts in the head. `inject_chat()` prints the chatbot's container in the footer. The script mounts every `.mwai-chatbot-container` on `DOMContentLoaded` and exposes `window.mwaiInitialize` for later mounting.

## How

Modelled on **Load Fluent Forms' Turnstile when a form comes near** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-fluentforms-turnstile.php`, #1210).

- New `includes/features/class-seoprostack-ai-engine-later.php` (`SEOProStack_Ai_Engine_Later`, key `ai_engine_later`, Speed tab, default on), registered in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES`; in `SEOProStack_Speed_Plan::items()` while AI Engine is active.
- On the front end, at `wp_print_scripts`/`wp_print_styles` in the head: take `mwai_chatbot`, `mwai_highlight` and the `mwai_chatbot_theme_*` styles out of the queue, and with them the dependencies no other queued script needs (React, ReactDOM, `wp-element` and their own).

- Does nothing without AI Engine, in the admin, in the block editor, or for AMP, feeds and REST requests.
- README.md (Features, a section), readme.txt, changelog.txt.

## How to check

1. `scripts/lint.sh php`, `phpcs`, `phpstan`.
2. `scripts/test-site.sh` with AI Engine and a site-wide chatbot: logged out, the home page's HTML has no `app/chatbot.js`, React or theme stylesheet in the head; after a click or scroll the launcher appears and a message can be sent (REST nonce works); the browser console has no errors.
3. On one of the two sites above, after release: PageSpeed mobile shows no AI Engine file in render-blocking requests, and the chatbot opens and answers.

title: Load plugins only where needed: try skipping Tutor LMS on pages without Tutor content
body:
## Problem

**Load plugins only where needed** never tries skipping Tutor LMS (and Tutor LMS Pro) on pages without Tutor content, such as Kadence home pages, so every uncached view of those pages loads and runs them.

Read-only check on a live Kadence site (Tutor LMS and Tutor LMS Pro 4.2.0): the learned map (`seoprostack_plugin_front`) notes `tutor/tutor.php` as `always, content, pages, login, bar` and `tutor-pro/tutor-pro.php` as `content, pages, login`. `front_propose()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`) leaves out every plugin noted `always` or `login`, so neither is ever checked per address. The callbacks behind those notes:

| Hook (kind) | Callback |
|---|---|
| `determine_current_user` (always) | `TUTOR\RestAuth::api_auth` |
| `wp_login` (login) | `TUTOR\User::update_user_last_login`, `TUTOR\User::set_timezone` |
| `login_form` (login) | `TUTOR\User::add_timezone_input`, `TutorPro\Auth\SpamProtection::extend_login_form` |
| `authenticate` (login) | `TutorPro\Auth\SpamProtection::auth_check` |
| `wp_authenticate_user` (login) | `TUTOR_PRO\EmailVerification::check_status`, `TutorPro\Auth\_2FA::check_login` |
| `registration_errors` (login) | `TutorPro\Auth\SpamProtection::handle_registration_spam_protection` |

None of them acts on the requests a checked address skips plugins on (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::front_request()`: GET or HEAD of `index.php`, not the REST API, only harmless query arguments; and for checked addresses also no cookies and no Authorization header):

- `api_auth()` returns the user unchanged unless `RestAuth::is_tutor_api_request()` sees a Tutor REST route in the path, which `front_request()` already refuses.
- `authenticate`, `wp_authenticate_user`, `wp_login` and `registration_errors` run only when someone logs in or registers (a POST to `wp-login.php`, Tutor's own forms or AJAX), which loads every plugin.
- `login_form` adds fields to a login form: an address whose form shows them renders differently without Tutor, so its check keeps Tutor.

## Change

In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`, a list of known callbacks that do nothing on those requests (Tutor LMS and Tutor LMS Pro 4.2.0, by hook, as `woo_can_skip()` lists WooCommerce's), which `front_notes()` does not note. Any other callback on those hooks keeps today's behaviour. Then the per-address checks (`SEOProStack_Front_Verify`) try Tutor like other plugins that add to pages, and an address skips it only if it renders the same without it.

## Verify

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Test site with Kadence and Tutor LMS: after learning, `seoprostack_plugin_front` notes for `tutor/tutor.php` no longer include `always` or `login`; the home page kind proposes Tutor; after a check, the home page skips Tutor (X-SEO Pro Stack loader header or the plugin count), while a course page, the courses archive and the dashboard keep it.
- README.md (Load plugins only where needed), changelog.txt.

title: Media storage: a picture kept after one retryable removal failure stays kept until --retry-failed, holding import drains
body:
## What happens

A picture whose removal check fails once with a retryable service error is marked `kept:<signature>` in `_seoprostack_storage_local` (`local_result()`, "One attachment must not hold up the whole library"). Nothing clears that mark except `wp seoprostack media-storage upload --retry-failed` (or switching "Remove local copies after upload" off and on), which drops every kept mark on the site. Until a person runs it, the picture keeps all its local files.

SEO Pro Directory's import drain waits for each picture's local files to go, in order, so one kept picture holds its part in `draining` until the job's one-hour no-progress stop, and resuming only restarts the hour. `remove_local_now()` / `remove_local_many()` answer `storage_kept` for it, so callers that ask SEO Pro Stack to remove it cannot either.

Observed on 6 November 2026 (SEO Pro Stack 1.3.160, SEO Pro Directory 0.4.118): the last part of a 27-part regional import stood 41 minutes on one attachment, the only kept picture on that site. It was `uploaded`, and every one of its 11 local files (JPEG sizes plus WebP/AVIF copies) was in its `_seoprostack_storage` record. The site's last storage error at the time was "The kept original is in use by another request. Try again shortly." Dropping that one picture's kept mark let the next removal pass take it; the part drained and the job ended within 4 minutes. Another importing site had one kept picture as well.

## Expected

A kept mark from a retryable failure is revisited on its own after a while, as the comment beside it intends ("retry-failed or a changed connection can revisit the mark"). An import should not need a person to notice it.

## Suggested fix

In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-media-storage.php`:

1. When `local_result()` marks a picture kept after a retryable failure, record when (for example `kept:<signature>:<time>`, or a separate meta key) instead of a permanent mark.
2. In the removal pass and in `remove_local_now()` / `remove_local_many()`, treat a retryable kept mark older than a short interval (for example 10 minutes) as not kept: check the picture again, keeping the existing mismatch/change handling in `removal_stopped()` permanent.
3. Leave the marks `restore_attachment()` and `removal_stopped()` set (mismatch or change) as they are: those need a person or a new upload.

Pattern to follow: the `LOCAL_WAIT` pause after a busy original, which already expires on its own.

## Verification

- Make one picture's removal fail once with a retryable error (or set its mark by hand with an old time), with "Remove local copies after upload" on: within the interval plus one batch its local files are removed and its mark becomes the signature, with no `--retry-failed`.
- A mismatch (`removal_stopped()`) still keeps its files.
- `wp seoprostack media-storage status` shows no kept pictures after a full import; an import whose pictures all upload runs to the end with no one-hour drain stop.

Related: #1256 (a removed picture whose later WebP/AVIF copies stay on disk also holds a drain).
